Any other refusal by the library (a ValueError, including an option combination the library rejects, such as --solver sparse with a method that has no sparse path, or a malformed triple line) writes run.json with "status": "failed", prints foambryo infer: error: failed: <message> (...) and exits 4. On a cropped mesh the library accepts undetermined tensions and reports the cut cells' pressures as nan (with a warning): that run is "complete".

docs.title: 4b. foambryo infer-over-seeds
docs.text:
foambryo infer-over-seeds MASK -o OUTDIR [--spacing DZ DY DX] [--spacing-unit UNIT] [--min-distance N]
                                         [--seeds N] [--combine tensions|angles] [--angle-reading READING]
                                         [--tension-method METHOD] [--max-workers K] [--overwrite]

What it does. Reconstructs the mask at the dither seeds 0..N−1, each as foambryo mesh would (delaunay-watershed-3d's default reconstruction, resampled to cubic voxels when one axis is longer), infers the tensions of each mesh, and combines them per interface, exactly as foambryo.infer_tensions_over_seeds(mask, seeds=range(N), spacing=..., ...) does. It writes tensions.csv, tensions_per_seed.csv and run.json; no pressures, because no single mesh carries them. The spread over seeds is reported as a lower bound on the error, not an error bar. N is fixed in advance: seeds are never chosen by their result.

Option Default (the library's) Library argument MASK required read as in § 3.1 -o, --output OUTDIR required created if missing --spacing DZ DY DX, --spacing-unit UNIT as for mesh (§ 3.2): no default spacing spacing --min-distance 3 min_distance (cubic voxels) --seeds N 8 (the library's seed list, 0..7) seeds=range(N) --combine tensions combine: tensions averages the seeds' tensions; angles (experimental, young-dupre only) averages their contact angles and infers once, and warns SeedEnsembleExperimentalWarning --angle-reading chord angle_reading; one of chord, quadric, oriented_chord, oriented_quadric --tension-method young-dupre mode --max-workers K 1 max_workers: K seeds at once, in separate processes, each holding one reconstruction; the result does not depend on it --overwrite off deletes tensions.csv, tensions_per_seed.csv and run.json (only those) before the run

tensions.csv: one row per interface found by at least one seed, sorted by label_1 then label_2, with the columns

label_1,label_2,tension,tension_seed_sd,n_seeds_found,found_by_fewer_than_half_the_seeds
0,1,0.8731...,0.0412...,8,false
  • tension: the ensemble tension (the mean over the seeds that found the interface, or with angles the one solve on the averaged angles); tension_seed_sd: the standard deviation of the seeds' own tensions (nan with fewer than two); both in the exact float format of § 4.2.
  • n_seeds_found: how many seeds found the interface with a finite tension.
  • found_by_fewer_than_half_the_seeds: true or false. On synthetic tissues with known geometry most such interfaces do not exist in the true tissue; they are kept, flagged, not removed.

tensions_per_seed.csv: every seed's own tensions, as infer_tensions gives them on that seed's mesh, one row per seed and interface, in the seeds' order and, within a seed, sorted by label_1 then label_2; same number format.

seed,label_1,label_2,tension
0,0,1,0.8692...
0,1,2,1.0511...
1,0,1,0.8774...

run.json, schema 1 (§ 5), with command = "foambryo infer-over-seeds" and these keys in place of the mesh-related ones: * input: path, sha256 and bytes of the mask file, its shape, the spacing used, its spacing_unit, and spacing_from ("command line" or the file's name); * options: seeds (N), combine, angle_reading, tension_method, min_distance, max_workers; * seeds: the seed list, [0, 1, …, N−1]; * reconstructions: one object per seed, with seed, points, triangles, crop_faces and seconds; * results: tensions, undetermined_tensions and found_by_fewer_than_half_the_seeds (counts); * units: tension (relative, each seed gauged to a mean of 1) and length (the spacing's unit).

library_call, status (complete or failed), error, warnings and outputs are as in § 5.

docs.title: 5. run.json, schema 1
docs.text:
A JSON object, UTF-8, indented. Non-finite numbers are written as the strings "nan", "inf", "-inf" (JSON has no such numbers). Keys may be added within schema 1; a reader must ignore keys it does not know. Removing or renaming a key, or changing a key's meaning, makes a new schema number and is announced in the CHANGELOG.

Key Type Content schema integer 1 command string "foambryo infer" arguments list of strings the arguments after foambryo, as given date string start of the run, ISO 8601 in UTC (2026-10-10T10:12:00+00:00) elapsed_seconds number wall time from reading the mesh to writing the last result versions object python, foambryo, delaunay-watershed-3d, numpy, scipy (installed distribution versions) input object path (as given), sha256 (of the file's bytes), bytes, metadata (the .rec appendix as delaunay-watershed-3d reads it, its version under appendix_version; null for a file with no appendix or not a .rec) options object tension_method, pressure_method, mean_tension, base_pressure, solver, diagnostics: every option, in the command's spelling, defaults included. With --no-pressures, also no_pressures: true, and pressure_method and base_pressure are null (not used); without it there is no no_pressures key library_call string the equivalent Python call, e.g. infer_forces(mesh, mean_tension=1.0, base_pressure=0.0, mode_tension=TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre, mode_pressure=PressureComputationMethod.Variational, solver='auto', diagnostics=False); with --no-pressures, infer_tensions(mesh, mean_tension=1.0, mode=TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre, solver='auto', diagnostics=False) mesh object points, triangles, materials (medium included), crop_faces (count), cut_cells (list of labels) results object tensions, undetermined_tensions, pressures, undetermined_pressures (counts; the pressure counts are null when no pressure was computed, with --no-pressures among other cases) units object tension (relative, gauged to a mean tension of <T>), pressure (tension per <unit>, the unit being the appendix's spacing_unit for physical coordinates, voxel for voxel coordinates, else mesh length unit (not recorded in the mesh file)) status string "complete", "pressures refused" or "failed" error string or null the library's message when status is not "complete" warnings list one object per distinct warning: category (the class name), message, count solves list or null with --diagnostics basic or spectrum: one object per linear solve, in the order they ran (the scalars of the library's SolveRecord: system, solver, n_rows, n_unknowns, rank, residual_norm, condition_number, condition_number_source, seconds, …; the same values as solves.csv); null with none outputs list of strings the files written in OUTDIR, run.json included

docs.title: 6. foambryo view
docs.text:
foambryo view MESH [--results OUTDIR] [--colour-bars FILE] [--figure FILE] [--no-show]
                   [--scale-bar LENGTH | --no-scale-bar] [--scattered [COEFF]]
                   [--tension-method METHOD] [--pressure-method METHOD | --no-pressures] [--mean-tension T]
                   [--base-pressure P] [--solver auto|dense|sparse]
foambryo view MASK [--spacing DZ DY DX] [--spacing-unit UNIT] [--min-distance N] [--scattered [COEFF]]
                   [--scale-bar LENGTH | --no-scale-bar] [the inference options above]
Option Default Meaning MESH required read with dcel_mesh_from_file --results OUTDIR none read what foambryo infer or foambryo infer-over-seeds wrote in OUTDIR (§ 6.2). Without --results, the tensions then the pressures are inferred exactly as foambryo infer does with the same options (the inference options below); if the library refuses the pressures, the tensions alone are shown, with a warning; if it refuses the tensions, exit 4 --colour-bars FILE none write the colour bars of what the viewer shows (§ 6.1) to FILE; the format follows the suffix (.png, .pdf, .svg, …). Needs matplotlib. Written before any window opens --figure FILE none write the window's first view with its colour bars and its scale bar (§ 6.4) to FILE (.png, .pdf, .svg, …). Needs Polyscope and a display. Prints wrote FILE --no-show off do not keep a viewer window open. With --colour-bars alone it runs without a display and without Polyscope installed; with --figure, Polyscope renders the view once and the window closes. Without either, refused (exit 2) --scale-bar LENGTH a round length the length scale bar's length, in the mesh's unit (§ 6.3) --no-scale-bar off draw no length scale bar --scattered [COEFF] off; COEFF 0.2, the viewer functions' scatter_coeff open the window exploded: each cell moved by COEFF × (its centroid − the tissue's centroid) (DcelData.compute_scattered_arrays); the panel changes it --no-pressures off the tensions only (infer_tensions), as foambryo infer --no-pressures; refused with --pressure-method, --base-pressure or --results MASK, --spacing, --spacing-unit, --min-distance as for mesh (§ 3.2) a mask (.npy, .npz, .tif, .tiff) is opened in the window to be reconstructed there (§ 6.5); the three options are refused with a mesh --tension-method, --pressure-method, --mean-tension, --base-pressure, --solver infer's (§ 4.1): the library's the options of foambryo infer, passed to the same library calls, when the viewer infers. Refused with --results (exit 2): the values are then read, not inferred. --diagnostics is not an option of view: the window's Export has its own diagnostics choice (§ 6)

The window is foambryo.viewing.plot_force_inference(mesh, tensions, pressures, ...), or plot_tension_inference(mesh, tensions, ...) when there are no pressures (an ensemble, --no-pressures, or pressures the library refused). It needs Polyscope and a display (foambryo[viewing]). Its panel, foambryo, shows:

  • which values the colours show: the library call that produced them (inferred by 'foambryo view': infer_forces(mesh, …)), or read from NAME (foambryo infer: <run.json's library_call>), NAME the results folder's own name, never the path to it;
  • the colour bars of § 6.1, drawn in the window with the library's colours over the library's ranges; an outlined green swatch, undetermined (nan), when a value is nan (or an interface has no tension), and a glass swatch, crop face, when the mesh has crop faces;
  • with tensions and pressures, colour the surface by tensions (the default) or pressures. In the tension view an undetermined tension's interface is not filled and its triangles' edges are drawn in the undetermined green (undetermined tensions' outlines, a check box); crop faces are never filled with a value's colour and are drawn as glass, with their edges (crop faces, a check box hides them);
  • the background (a choice): white (Polyscope's), light grey 0.70, dark grey 0.20, black (BACKGROUND_COLOURS, the napari plugin's choices too) or a custom colour; on a dark background the scale bar, the frame, their labels and the graph view's black nodes are drawn light (the mirror of their grey), on a light one dark; a background set in Polyscope's own menu is followed too. Polyscope tone-maps its background (exposure 1.1, gamma 2.2: 0.20 was shown 0.50): the window gives it (c ** 2.2) / 1.1, which it shows as c;
  • the x, y, z frame (a check box): three segments along the mesh's columns (z, y, x), from just outside the drawn box's lowest corner (moved out by 10 % of its largest side), of the scale bar's round length, labelled z, y, x at their tips and with their length at the corner, in the window and in saved figures;
  • flat colours: draws the surface unlit, so that its colours are exactly the bars' (by default the surface is shaded, as any 3-D view);
  • the scale bar's check box (§ 6.3);
  • Save figure and Save colour bars, each with a file name (default foambryo_figure.png, foambryo_colour_bars.png, in the working directory): PNG, PDF or SVG by the suffix. The window never overwrites a file: an existing name gets _2, _3, …; the panel says which file it wrote;
  • Explode: a check box and a coefficient (0 to 1), the scattered view, followed live (each view is prepared on a background thread, the window keeps turning and draws the last one asked for); Cut: a scene slice plane normal to z, y or x (the mesh's axes 0, 1, 2), at a position in the mesh's unit along the drawn box, keeping the lower or the higher side (Polyscope keeps the side the plane's normal points to: measured in a real window, 2.6.1);
  • a choice of tension method, pressure method or pressures unticked (the tensions only), and solver, and Recompute: the library is called again with them (and the same mean tension and base pressure), and the colours and bars follow; then the foambryo infer MESH -o results … line that writes the same numbers. Not for an ensemble. A diagnostics choice (none, basic, spectrum) keeps the solve records for Export;
  • Export, to a folder (default foambryo_export): foambryo infer's files for the values shown, written by the command's writers, tensions.csv, pressures.csv (when inferred), solves.csv and spectra.npz (with diagnostics), run.json (the command's record, its input the mesh file), and colour_bars.png as --colour-bars writes it; a mesh reconstructed in the window adds its mesh.rec. When the folder holds any of these files, the panel lists them and asks Cancel or Replace; another file is never touched. Values given to the window (--results) are exported with a run.json that says so (values_given_to_the_window). Not for an ensemble (foambryo infer-over-seeds writes its files).

The coloured surface draws the back of a triangle like its front: the triangles' winding follows the label order, so the outside of a tissue faces away from Polyscope's camera, and Polyscope's default shading of back faces drew every colour about 15 % darker than its bar.

docs.title: 6.1 Colour bars
docs.text:
foambryo.viewing.save_colour_bars(mesh, dict_tensions, dict_pressures, path, alpha=0.05) writes one image with one bar per quantity. The bars use the same computation as the viewer's surface colours, through one shared function:

  • Surface tension: colour map coolwarm (blue for low, light grey for the mean, red for high), over a range centred on the mean of the finite tensions of the map (one value per interface; the mean is mean_tension, 1 by default, for every method that meets its gauge exactly) and symmetric around it, its half-width the farther of the alpha and 1 − alpha quantiles from the mean (tension_colour_range). Tensions beyond either end are drawn with the end's colour (the viewer clips them). The bar's middle tick is the mean. (Until 0.7.0: jet between the two quantiles.)
  • Pressure: colour map magma reversed (light for low, dark for high) and trimmed to its 10–90 % range (PRESSURE_COLOUR_MAP_RANGE: a fraction x is drawn magma(0.1 + 0.8 x), so no pressure is black or near-white and none vanishes on a black or a white background; until 0.7.0 the whole map), from 0 to the 1 − alpha quantile of the finite pressures over the mesh's triangles, each triangle carrying the pressure of the higher-labelled of its two materials (this is how the viewer's surface colours them). Negative pressures are drawn with the colour of 0. This is the viewer's only pressure scale: the surface, the graph view's cell nodes and the bar take it from one function, so a pressure has the same colour in all three. (Until this revision the graph view took its own quantile over cells: 5.383 against the surface's 5.472 on benchmark case 000.)
  • A swatch labelled "undetermined" when any value is nan: green (UNDETERMINED_COLOR, #1b9e77), outside both maps; a viewer that can draws an undetermined interface as its green outline, without fill, and fills it green otherwise. A "crop face" swatch when the mesh has crop faces: see-through glass with its edges drawn (CROP_FACE_COLOR, CROP_FACE_OPACITY, CROP_FACE_EDGE_COLOR); crop faces carry no value.
  • Each bar's two ends are labelled with their values. The function returns them, so they can be checked against the viewer's own range (the viewer prints it as "Extremas …").
  • matplotlib only (its non-interactive canvas): no window, no display, no Polyscope.
  • foambryo view prints wrote FILE: tension <low> to <high>, pressure 0 to <high> (6 significant digits; the pressure part only when there are pressures). No finite tension: exit 4, no colour bar: no tension is finite: there is no colour scale to draw.

In the window the same bars are drawn by the panel (ImGui rectangles, flat colours, no interpolation): the colours are those save_colour_bars samples, over the ranges colour_bar_ranges returns. Polyscope draws the surface from the colours, not from the values: its own colour maps would draw nan in their top colour. The graph view (cell nodes, and edges between them) is coloured over the same two ranges. The scattered view (plot_force_inference(..., scattered=True)) colours pressures over its own triangles (each cell's triangles carry that cell's pressure), and its pressure bar says so. Save colour bars in the panel writes save_colour_bars' image whenever the window's bars are its bars (not scattered, not an ensemble), and the panel's own bars otherwise.

docs.title: 6.2 Results of infer and of infer-over-seeds
docs.text:
• infer's results: OUTDIR/tensions.csv and, if present, OUTDIR/pressures.csv. If OUTDIR/run.json exists, its input.sha256 must equal MESH's: results computed from another mesh are refused (exit 3).
  • infer-over-seeds' results, recognised by the columns of tensions.csv (§ 4b): the ensemble tensions are drawn on MESH's interfaces, matched by label pair (MESH is one reconstruction of the same mask, for example foambryo mesh's). Their run.json names the mask, not a mesh, so the mesh cannot be checked against it: a warning says how many of the ensemble's interfaces are not on MESH (not drawn) and how many of MESH's are not in the ensemble (drawn undetermined), and no interface in common is refused (exit 3). The colour scale and --colour-bars are taken over the interfaces drawn. The window adds the seeds' spread, tension_seed_sd, as a second surface quantity with its own bar (jet, clipped at the 5 % and 95 % quantiles), and draws the interfaces flagged found_by_fewer_than_half_the_seeds over the surface, as a magenta wireframe (their triangles' edges, so that their own colour stays visible). No pressure is shown: no single mesh carries an ensemble's pressures.

docs.title: 6.3 The length scale bar
docs.text: When MESH is a .rec file whose appendix records physical coordinates and their unit (coordinate_frame = physical, spacing_unit; foambryo mesh writes both), the window draws a segment in the scene, under the tissue (along the first coordinate axis, 8 % of the tissue's largest side below it), of length 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten, the longest at most a quarter of the tissue's largest side (or --scale-bar LENGTH). Its length is written beside it in the window and in saved figures (20 µm; the unit um is written µm). It is exact in 3-D and foreshortened on screen like any length in a perspective view. A mesh without a recorded unit has no scale bar, unless --scale-bar is given: it is then labelled in voxel for a mesh in voxel coordinates, else in mesh units.

docs.title: 6.4 Figures
docs.text: A figure is Polyscope's own rendering of the view, without the user interface (screenshot_to_buffer), and under it, drawn by matplotlib: the colour bars of § 6.1, the swatches of what has no value, and a caption, Values: …, the panel's first line (it names the results folder, never its path). The scale bar's length is written under the segment, where Polyscope's camera projects its ends (in the lower left corner when an end is off the view). --figure writes the first view, framed on MESH (Polyscope's home view); Save figure writes the current one. From Python: plot_force_inference(mesh, ..., save_figure=PATH, show=False).

docs.title: 6.5 From a mask
docs.text:
foambryo view MASK --spacing DZ DY DX reads the mask and its spacing exactly as foambryo mesh does (the same checks, messages and exit codes; the mask report is printed), then opens the window on the mask: its cell voxels as points at index × spacing, one colour per label, the medium left out (strided above three million points). Polyscope's volume grids cannot leave a value out, so the medium would hide the tissue: the points are what lets the cells be seen, and the cut slices them. The panel then offers, top to bottom once there are values:

  • Values (as in § 6, without Recompute);
  • Mask and reconstruction: show the mask, min distance, the estimate (time and memory, foambryo.reconstruction_cost: a fit to measured reconstructions, with its in-sample band, the one the napari plugin gives), Reconstruct and Cancel. The reconstruction is foambryo.io.reconstruct_mask (foambryo mesh's call) in a child process: the window keeps drawing (no frame over 1 s on benchmark case 000), shows the elapsed time, and Cancel stops the process and keeps nothing. The mesh is then drawn half transparent over the mask;
  • Inference: one mesh (infer_tensions_then_pressures on the reconstruction, foambryo infer's call) or seed ensemble (infer_tensions_over_seeds on the mask, foambryo infer-over-seeds' call, with the number of seeds, workers and combination; its progress seed by seed), the tension method, the pressure method or pressures unticked, the solver, the diagnostics (one mesh); Infer and Cancel, also in a child process; and the command lines that give the same numbers (foambryo mesh … then foambryo infer …, or foambryo infer-over-seeds …). Once values are drawn the mask is hidden (its points would speckle the surface); its check box shows it again.

With a mask, --results, --figure, --colour-bars and --no-show are refused (exit 2): they need a mesh; foambryo mesh writes it without a window. The values are drawn once prepared in the background: the mask and the reconstruction stay on screen until then.

From Python, foambryo.viewing.view_mask(mask, spacing, *, spacing_unit="um", min_distance=None, mean_tension, base_pressure, mode_tension, mode_pressure, solver, pressures=True, scattered=False, scatter_coeff=0.2, scale_bar=True, mask_name="mask.npz") opens the same window (every default the library's; min_distance=None is delaunay-watershed-3d's); a mask or spacing the command refuses raises ValueError.

docs.title: 7. Messages and exit codes
docs.text:
• Errors go to standard error as one line, foambryo <sub-command>: error: <message>, followed by the exit code below. No Python traceback, except for an unexpected error (code 1).
  • Warnings (the library's, and the command's own) go to standard error as foambryo <sub-command>: warning: <Category>: <message>, once per distinct warning, with (<n> times) appended when it was raised more than once. infer also records them in run.json.
  • Results (the lines naming each file written) go to standard output.
Code Meaning Examples 0 success 1 unexpected error: a defect, reported with its traceback 2 the command line is invalid or incomplete unknown option; a value out of range; a mask that records no spacing, without --spacing; an output suffix other than .rec; --no-show without --colour-bars or --figure; an inference option of view with --results 3 a file cannot be used as asked an input that does not exist; a file that cannot be read or does not hold what is expected (not 3-D integer labels, no mask array, no label1 / label2); results from another mesh; an output that exists without --overwrite; an optional package that is not installed 4 the reconstruction or the inference refused this input the library raised its documented refusal (§ 4.4); what was computed before the refusal is written

The messages the acceptance tests pin:

foambryo mesh: error: no such file: 'missing.npy'
foambryo infer: error: no such file: 'missing.rec'
foambryo mesh: error: mask.npy records no voxel spacing: give it with --spacing DZ DY DX (for example --spacing 1 1 1 to keep voxel units)

docs.title: 8. What equals what (the acceptance tests)
docs.text:
1. infer: tensions.csv and pressures.csv, read back as 64-bit floats, are bitwise equal to infer_forces(dcel_mesh_from_file(MESH), …) with the same options, for every tension method, every pressure method, and non-default --mean-tension / --base-pressure / --solver / --diagnostics.
  2. mesh: the arrays of MESH.rec (points, triangles, labels, crop-face mask) have the same SHA-256 as construct_mesh_in_physical_units's, in the same crop-face row order, and the file is byte for byte that reconstruction's own export; with and without a cell reaching the image box; with cubic voxels of 1 and of 0.5 and with a z step twice the pixel size. With cubic voxels, the points are also those of the plain reconstruction times the spacing. A spacing with two different short axes is refused (exit 2, or 3 from an .npz); above k = 3 both warnings are printed.
  3. run.json: every key of § 5 is present with its type. solves.csv reads back equal to the same run's solves, field by field, floats bitwise. 3b. infer --no-pressures: tensions.csv is bitwise infer_tensions (and infer_forces' tensions) with the same options; no pressures.csv; a pressure option given with it is refused.
  4. Exit codes and messages: a missing mask, a missing mesh, a mask without spacing.
  5. Colour bars: the ends of each bar equal the range the viewer prints for the same input; the image is written with no display and with Polyscope absent.
  6. No defaults of the command differ from the library's (a test reads the library's signatures).
  7. infer-over-seeds: every column of tensions.csv, and every row of tensions_per_seed.csv, read back, equals infer_tensions_over_seeds' result for the same mask, seeds, spacing and options, bitwise for the floats, with cubic voxels, with a z step twice the pixel size, and with --combine angles --angle-reading quadric; run.json lists the seeds; a refused combination writes run.json only and exits 4.

Synthetic masks and benchmark meshes only.

docs.title: 9. Possible extensions
docs.text:
None of these is in schema 1; each would be a change to this specification. Requests and comments are welcome on the issue tracker.

  • Formats. Masks are read from .npy, .npz and .tif, meshes from .rec; mesh could also write .vtk.
  • TIFF metadata. mesh does not read the spacing from a TIFF (ImageJ spacing and the resolution tags), because these tags are often missing or wrong and a wrong spacing is silent; it could, for software whose tags are reliable.
  • Exit codes. Codes 2, 3 and 4 tell batch runs why a command stopped; a simpler "0 or not 0" would also do.
  • Anisotropic voxels. The mask is resampled to cubic voxels before meshing (§ 3), with a warning whenever the voxels are not cubic and a second one above k = 3, where the accuracy was not measured. The first warning could become optional for batch runs.
  • Options not in schema 1. Each is a library option already: --angle-reading for infer (infer-over-seeds has it), --sparse-threshold N, a way to declare physical image faces (a coverslip), the wedge-refusal policies, and a table of tensions per junction-graph component.
  • A record for mesh. mesh could also write a JSON record (versions, options, the mask's SHA-256); today the provenance chain starts at the mesh file (its SHA-256 in run.json).
  • Preprocessing. A foambryo preprocess sub-command could expose delaunay-watershed-3d's mask-preprocessing functions.
  • Seed ensembles (§ 4b). infer-over-seeds starts from the mask and writes no pressures. Its per-seed table, tensions_per_seed.csv, is a long table; one column per seed is the alternative. The default N = 8 costs eight reconstructions, each with its memory.

docs.title: 10. Every message, verbatim
docs.text:

Code Sub-command Message 2 all argparse's usage line, then <option>: <reason> (must be a finite number, not '…', must be greater than 0, not '…', must be an integer of at least 1, not '…', must be one ASCII word (letters, digits, _ . - / ^), not '…', invalid choice: …) 2 mesh <name> records no voxel spacing: give it with --spacing DZ DY DX (for example --spacing 1 1 1 to keep voxel units) 2 mesh the mesh is written as .rec: -o must end in .rec, not '<name>' 2 mesh --spacing: spacing (<dz>, <dy>, <dx>) has two different fine axes; On success each sub-command prints, on standard output, one wrote <path>… line per file written.

docs.title: 11. Changes since the first version
docs.text:
• 14 Oct 2026: the text agrees with the command (§ 2, § 4.1, § 4b, § 6, § 7, § 10): solves.csv in the pipeline, the order of the tension methods, the four values of --angle-reading, --spacing optional for an .npz that records it in view MASK, the window's diagnostics choice, --no-pressures in the choice of window. The warning for interfaces missing from an ensemble now says they are drawn undetermined (it said grey; they are drawn as undetermined values are, since the green outlines).

  • 12 Oct 2026: foambryo view MASK, --scattered, --no-pressures (§ 6, § 6.5): the window starts from a mask, reconstructs and infers it in child processes; the panel has explode, cut, the solver and pressures.

  • 12 Oct 2026: foambryo infer --no-pressures and solves.csv (§ 4). The tensions only, and the solve diagnostics as a table beside run.json; the mask report of foambryo mesh is worded as information (§ 3.4).

  • 11 Oct 2026: foambryo mesh resamples anisotropic masks to cubic voxels (§ 3), and the viewer has one pressure scale (§ 6.1).

  • 11 Oct 2026: a fourth sub-command, foambryo infer-over-seeds (§ 4b). Several reconstructions of one mask at fixed dither seeds, with the tensions combined over them, and the three new tensions.csv columns tension_seed_sd, n_seeds_found and found_by_fewer_than_half_the_seeds, and a second table, tensions_per_seed.csv, with every seed's own tensions. run.json gains seeds and reconstructions. Its acceptance test is § 8, item 7, its messages are in § 10, and its possible extensions are in § 9, Seed ensembles.
  • 12 Oct 2026: the viewer's window (§ 6): the colour bars drawn in the window, the coloured surface's back faces drawn like its front faces, a length scale bar (§ 6.3), --figure (§ 6.4) and Save figure / Save colour bars in the window, infer's inference options for view (refused with --results), the results of infer-over-seeds (§ 6.2), and a choice of methods with Recompute in the window. A refused tension inference in view now exits 4 with failed: … (it raised a traceback, exit 1).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
foambryo needs Python 3.11 or later. Install it from PyPI, in a virtual environment:

pip install foambryo                 # the library (delaunay-watershed-3d comes with it)
pip install "foambryo[viewing]"      # and the Polyscope viewer (Polyscope, matplotlib)
pip install "foambryo[cli]"          # and TIFF masks for the foambryo command (tifffile)

The napari plugin: pip install "napari[all]" napari-foambryo (its version 0.1.0 is released with foambryo 0.7.0).

docs.title: The input: a segmentation mask
docs.text: A 3-D array of non-negative integer labels: one label per cell, 0 for the medium around the tissue. Axis 0 is z, axes 1 and 2 are y and x. Its voxel size is (dz, dy, dx), in any one unit; one axis (the z step) may be longer than the other two, which must be equal. foambryo never guesses it: give it, or work in voxel units.

docs.title: In Python
docs.text:
import tifffile
from foambryo import dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask, infer_forces
from foambryo.viewing import plot_force_inference, save_colour_bars

mask = tifffile.imread("segmentation.tif")
mesh = dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask, spacing=(1.0, 0.5, 0.5))  # (dz, dy, dx) in um; mesh in um
tensions, pressures = infer_forces(mesh)       # {(label_1, label_2): tension}, {label: pressure}
save_colour_bars(mesh, tensions, pressures, "colour_bars.png")   # no window needed
plot_force_inference(mesh, tensions, pressures, length_unit="um")  # needs a display

The tensions are normalised to a mean of 1 (mean_tension), the pressures are relative to the medium's (0, base_pressure), in tension per um here. Undetermined values are nan. See the methods.

docs.title: On the command line
docs.text:
foambryo mesh segmentation.tif --spacing 1.0 0.5 0.5 -o tissue.rec   # the mesh, in um
foambryo infer tissue.rec -o results                                 # tensions.csv, pressures.csv, run.json
foambryo view tissue.rec --results results                           # the Polyscope window

foambryo infer gives exactly the numbers of infer_forces(dcel_mesh_from_file("tissue.rec")). See the command-line specification and the example.

docs.title: In napari
docs.text: With the napari-foambryo plugin: File › Open Sample › foambryo › Benchmark case 000; Plugins › foambryo › Reconstruct (the layer and its voxel size are chosen; click Reconstruct); Infer; Results; Export. The plugin's numbers are those of the library, bit for bit. See Viewers.

docs.title: Methods note: what foambryo computes
docs.text: This note says what foambryo infers from a multimaterial mesh and how, so that its results can be read correctly. It describes what is implemented, not how well each method performs: for measured accuracy see BENCHMARKS.md and the methods guide; for every argument, the API reference. The method itself is published in Ichbiah et al., Nature Methods (2023), cited at the end.

docs.title: Unknowns and conventions
docs.text:
The mesh is a set of triangles, each separating two regions: cells, labelled by positive integers, and the medium, label 0. The triangles between regions \(i\) and \(j\) form the interface \((i, j)\), written with \(i < j\); the edges where three regions meet form the triple lines (junction lines).

foambryo infers

  • one surface tension \(\gamma_{ij}\) per interface (an energy per unit area), and
  • one pressure \(p_i\) per cell; the medium's pressure is base_pressure (0 by default).

It assumes the mesh is at mechanical equilibrium for the capillary energy

\[ E = \sum_{i<j} \gamma_{ij} A_{ij} \;-\; \sum_{i \ge 1} p_i V_i , \]

with \(A_{ij}\) the area of interface \((i, j)\) and \(V_i\) the volume of cell \(i\). Line tensions are not inferred: every triple line contributes no energy of its own.

A shape fixes only the ratios of the tensions, not their scale, and only the differences of pressures, not their level. So the tensions are normalised: their mean is mean_tension (1 by default), and the pressures are relative to the medium's. With the default normalisation the tensions are dimensionless (in units of the mean tension) and the pressures are in units of tension per length unit of the mesh: per voxel for a mesh in voxel coordinates, per micrometre for a mesh in micrometres. The normalisation holds in each connected piece of the junction graph separately; tensions in different pieces cannot be compared (a JunctionGraphGaugeWarning says when there are several). An interface that touches no triple line (a closed surface) has no measurable tension and is reported as nan.

docs.title: Angle-based tension methods
docs.text:
Young–Dupré at a triple line. Where regions \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) meet, the three tensions pull along their interfaces, perpendicular to the line, and balance: \(\gamma_{ab}\,\mathbf t_{ab} + \gamma_{bc}\,\mathbf t_{bc} + \gamma_{ac}\,\mathbf t_{ac} = 0\), with \(\mathbf t\) the unit vector in each interface, normal to the line and pointing away from it. Let \(\theta_f\) be the contact angle of region \(f\): the angle between the two interfaces that bound \(f\), measured inside \(f\), so that \(\theta_a + \theta_b + \theta_c = 2\pi\). Projecting the balance on each of the three directions gives three equations,

\[ \gamma_{ab} + \gamma_{bc}\cos\theta_b + \gamma_{ac}\cos\theta_a = 0, \quad \gamma_{ab}\cos\theta_b + \gamma_{bc} + \gamma_{ac}\cos\theta_c = 0, \quad \gamma_{ab}\cos\theta_a + \gamma_{bc}\cos\theta_c + \gamma_{ac} = 0 . \]

YoungDupre, the default. On the mesh, each edge of a triple line carries three wedges, one per region. Each contact angle is averaged over the edges of its line (an arithmetic mean), the three equations of each line are weighted by the line's share of the total junction length, and all lines are solved together by least squares, with the mean tension imposed exactly.

How an angle is read. By default (angle_reading="chord") the wedge angle on an edge is the angle between the two flat triangles that share it. Because a triangle is flat, on a curved interface this is the angle of the chord to the triangle's far vertex, not of the tangent at the line. angle_reading="quadric" (opt-in) fits a quadric surface to the interface's own vertices in a small window around the edge and reads that surface's tangent instead; where the window holds too few vertices, the edge keeps the chord reading, and a report (or an AngleReadingCoverageWarning) says how many. Either way, no vertex moves.

YoungDupreLocal imposes the same three equations once per mesh edge instead of once per line, so least squares does the averaging along the line; the row weights keep each line's total weight equal to YoungDupre's.

Other members write the same balance differently: with sines as well as cosines (ProjectionYoungDupre), through Lami's theorem (Lami, InvLami, LogLami), or through the cotangent formula of Yamamoto et al. (2026) (Cotan, InvCotan); Equilibrium imposes the vector balance itself, component by component, at every junction edge. The methods guide lists them, with their limits.

docs.title: Force-balance tension methods
docs.text:
The virtual-work balance. At equilibrium, moving any one mesh vertex \(\mathbf x_v\) does no work:

\[ \frac{\partial E}{\partial \mathbf x_v} = \sum_{i<j} \gamma_{ij}\,\frac{\partial A_{ij}}{\partial \mathbf x_v} - \sum_{i \ge 1} p_i\,\frac{\partial V_i}{\partial \mathbf x_v} = 0 \qquad \text{for every vertex } v . \]

The derivatives are exact for the triangulated surface: a triangle's area gradient at one corner is \(\tfrac12\,\mathbf n \times \mathbf e\), with \(\mathbf n\) its unit normal and \(\mathbf e\) the opposite edge, and a cell's volume gradient at one corner is \(\tfrac16\,\mathbf x_b \times \mathbf x_c\) from the two other corners, each summed over the triangles that contain the vertex. Stacking three rows per vertex gives a linear system \(M\beta = 0\) in the unknowns \(\beta = (\gamma, p)\), with one column per interface and one per cell (the medium has no column: its pressure is the reference). A reconstructed mesh is never exactly at equilibrium, so foambryo minimises \(\lVert M\beta \rVert^2\), and since \(\beta = 0\) would minimise it, it fixes the scale with the mean tension. The three members differ only in how:

  • ForceBalance: $\overline{\gamma} = $ mean_tension exactly, as a constraint (a Lagrange multiplier: a KKT system).
  • ForceBalanceSoftRow: the same condition as one more least-squares row, so the mean is met only approximately.
  • ForceBalanceMAP: a Gaussian prior on the tensions (mean mean_tension, standard deviation 0.3 × mean_tension) and a broad one on the pressures; the result is the posterior's maximum, with its covariance. The prior anchors the scale softly, so the mean tension is not exactly mean_tension; the relative tensions do not depend on the mesh's length unit.

foambryo.force_balance_inference.infer_force_balance returns the tensions and the pressures of the same solve.

Variational minimises the same quantity, \(\lVert M\beta\rVert^2\) with the mean tension met exactly, by a different factorisation (the normalisation is eliminated by substitution and the reduced problem solved by QR), and agrees with ForceBalance to rounding. foambryo's original route, which divides each normal equation by its row sum, weights the equations differently; it is kept inside the library so that published numbers can be reproduced.

docs.title: Pressures
docs.text:
Given the tensions, infer_pressures computes the pressures with one of three methods:

  • Variational (the default): the pressures that best balance every vertex at those tensions, the least-squares solution of \(\sum_i p_i\,\partial V_i/\partial\mathbf x_v = \sum_{i<j}\gamma_{ij}\, \partial A_{ij}/\partial\mathbf x_v\). It reads no curvature, and it is the only method that handles cropped tissues.
  • Laplace: Laplace's law on each interface, \(p_a - p_b = 2\gamma_{ab}H_{ab}\), with \(H_{ab}\) the interface's mean curvature, positive when its centre of curvature lies on \(a\)'s side, averaged over the interface's vertices off the triple lines; all interfaces are solved together by least squares.
  • WeightedLaplace: the same, with the curvature averaged with area weights.

Every pressure is relative to the medium, whose pressure is base_pressure: a non-zero base_pressure shifts all pressures by that amount and changes no difference. An interface whose vertices all lie on triple lines has no curvature, and a cell that no remaining Laplace equation connects to the medium gets nan, with an UndeterminedPressureWarning.

docs.title: Diagnostics, error bars and seed spread
docs.text:
compute_inference_diagnostics describes how well the mesh determines the force-balance solution:

  • \(\rho\), at given tensions, is the fraction of the surface-tension force left unbalanced once the best pressures are fitted, \(\lVert M\beta\rVert / \lVert M_\gamma\gamma \rVert\) (\(M_\gamma\): the tension columns of \(M\));
  • \(\rho_\text{free}\) is the same ratio with the tensions free (at the ForceBalance solution): how far the mesh is from an equilibrium of any tensions; above 0.2, no tensions balance the mesh and the force-balance methods should not be trusted on it;
  • \(\sigma_\text{soft}\) is the smallest singular value of \(M\) (columns scaled to unit norm) after the one that belongs to the overall scale: the least well determined combination of unknowns; and \(\operatorname{cond}(M)\) is the condition number of \(M\).

infer_tensions_with_uncertainty adds an interval to each tension. For YoungDupre it propagates the measured spread of each contact angle along its line through the solve, to first order: this is a lower bound on the error, not a calibrated error bar, because most of a reconstruction's error is a bias that no scatter measures. For the force-balance family the interval is scaled by the force residual. Neither function handles crop faces, and both stop at about 1 300 cells: they need the dense operator \(M\) and its singular value decomposition.

infer_tensions_over_seeds reconstructs the same mask at a fixed list of seeds of the point placement and averages the tensions; their standard deviation over the seeds measures only the part of the error that changes with the seed, so it too is a lower bound.

docs.title: Cropped tissues
docs.text: Where a cell reaches the image box, the mesh closes it with crop faces: triangles on the box, which are not contact with the medium. Every tension method leaves them, and every junction edge and vertex that touches them, out of its equations; an interface made only of crop faces has no tension. The pressures of the cells the crop cuts are nan, with a CutCellPressureWarning, because part of their surface and volume was not observed. The Laplace methods and the uncertainty functions refuse a cropped mesh. A tissue that really ends on an image face (a coverslip) is declared with physical_image_faces. See cropped tissues.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Ichbiah S., Delbary F., McDougall A., Dumollard R., Turlier H. Embryo mechanics cartography: inference of 3D force atlases from fluorescence microscopy. Nature Methods 20(12), 1989–1999 (2023), doi:10.1038/s41592-023-02084-7.
  • Yamamoto et al. (2026), for the cotangent formula, doi:10.1016/j.devcel.2026.04.013.
  • foambryo's API reference: tension inference, force-balance inference, pressure inference, uncertainty, crop faces, validation.

docs.title: Release notes — 0.7.0, 17 October 2026
docs.text: foambryo and delaunay-watershed-3d ship together as 0.7.0, the first release on PyPI since 0.5.1. 0.6.0 was prepared but not published; its changes are part of 0.7.0 and are included below. This is what changes for you and what can mislead you; CHANGELOG.md has the full list, and dw3d's RELEASE_NOTES.md covers reconstruction. Install both with pip install --upgrade foambryo delaunay-watershed-3d.

docs.title: What changes for you: results that differ from 0.5.1
docs.text:
1. Meshes of cells that touch the image border change, and so do the tensions and pressures inferred from them. The border triangles were wound the wrong way (in delaunay-watershed-3d), and a cell closed by the image border read too small a volume, often a negative one. On ten benchmark masks cut through their middle, the inferred tensions changed by up to 199 %, and every cell pressure by 37–139 %. Reconstruct and infer again any tissue cropped through its cells.
  2. Cropped tissues: crop faces are kept out of the equations, and cut cells get nan pressures. Where a cell reaches the image box, the mesh's crop faces used to be read as contact with the medium. On 433 plane crops of the benchmark tissues, the tensions of the interfaces next to the crop had 13–40 % error that way, and 9–12 % now; the cut cells' pressures, reported before, had 15–46 % error and are now nan with a CutCellPressureWarning. The Laplace pressure methods, infer_tensions_with_uncertainty and compute_inference_diagnostics refuse a cropped mesh. On a mesh without crop faces nothing changes.
  3. The normalisation is exact, so the scale of the tensions changes. The returned tensions now have exactly the mean mean_tension (per connected piece of the junction graph). Tension ratios are unchanged; the overall scale changes by one factor per mesh: for YoungDupre by 3e-6 typically and up to 1.4 %, for YoungDupreLocal up to 12 %, for InvCotan up to 8 %, for Equilibrium by 10 % typically. Pressures computed from those tensions scale by the same factor.
  4. ForceBalanceMAP gives different tensions at a mesh's own scale. It no longer depends on the mesh's length unit nor on mean_tension (rescaling a mesh used to move its relative tensions by up to 43 %). On 45 reconstructions with a simulation truth, the median of the per-case median relative tension error fell from 0.177 to 0.120 (better on 35, worse on 10).
  5. A cell that no Laplace equation determines gets a nan pressure, with an UndeterminedPressureWarning, instead of silently the medium's pressure. The variational method (the default) is not affected.
  6. Cotan, InvCotan, Lami and LogLami leave out flat junction lines (wedges of exactly 0 or 180 degrees), with a DegenerateWedgeWarning, instead of solving a system with infinite coefficients. On every mesh without such a line, every number is unchanged.
  7. The first-order error bars of YoungDupre are larger: they include a term they missed (a median 3 % larger on reconstructions of the benchmark tissues, 3.9–4.7 % on the same tissues voxelised at real cell size, and 21–23 % on simulated tissues of 90 and 165 cells at real cell size), and they are documented as a lower bound (see below).
  8. The viewers' colours changed. Tensions are drawn with coolwarm, light grey at the mean tension, blue below, red above; pressures with magma trimmed to its 10–90 % range; undetermined values in green. Figures made with 0.5 are not comparable colour for colour.
  9. dw3d's set_pixel_size scaled the wrong axes when the xy and z sizes differ: re-run any analysis that used it (dw3d's notes).
  10. With Laplace or WeightedLaplace and a non-zero base_pressure, every cell's pressure is now base_pressure lower: it used to be added twice. Nothing changes at the default base_pressure = 0 or with the variational method.
  11. Higher minimum versions, the oldest with which the test suite passes (on Python 3.11): delaunay-watershed-3d 0.7.0, numpy 2.0.0, scipy 1.13.0, networkx 3.2, trimesh 4.0.0; for the extras polyscope 2.6.1, matplotlib 3.8.4, tifffile 2023.1.23 and torch 2.3.0. The old floors (numpy 1.21.6, scipy 1.4.1, …) were never tested, and their releases have no wheels for Python 3.11. foambryo 0.7.0 needs delaunay-watershed-3d 0.7.0: the command's mesh and infer-over-seeds call its new physical-units reconstruction.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• Masks with anisotropic voxels: dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask, spacing=(dz, dy, dx)) resamples the mask to cubic voxels first and returns the mesh in the unit of the spacing.
  • Large tissues: sparse solves from 2 000 unknowns, solver="auto" | "dense" | "sparse", diagnostics=True, and an estimate of the reconstruction's time and memory (foambryo.reconstruction_cost). Below 2 000 unknowns every result is bitwise what it was. On a 1 866-cell tissue meshed on its native grid, from mask to tensions, 0.7.0 took 9.5 min and 30.9 GiB of peak memory where 0.5.1 took 47.5 min and 54.7 GiB (one machine, nothing else running; the tension solve itself 0.4 s instead of 226 s). Resampled to cubic voxels first, the same tissue's reconstruction takes about 13.5 min and 38 GiB.
  • Seed ensembles: infer_tensions_over_seeds.
  • The foambryo command: mesh, infer, infer-over-seeds, view.
  • The viewer: colour bars, length scale bar, explode and cut, backgrounds, saved figures, export, a window that starts from a mask, seed-ensemble results.
  • Public helpers for other front ends: foambryo.results, foambryo.colour_scales, foambryo.segmentation_masks, reconstruct_mask, infer_tensions_then_pressures.
  • Documentation: a user guide and examples in docs/, and a documentation website built from them.

docs.title: What can mislead you
docs.text:
1. A seed ensemble's spread is a lower bound on the error, not an error bar. A single seed's ±1 SD interval held the true tension for about half of the interfaces on synthetic tissues. Fix the seed list in advance.
  2. No error bar is calibrated on a reconstructed mesh. One reconstruction's first-order ± std held the true tension for 26–54 % of interfaces (nominal 68 %), ± 2 std for 48–79 % (nominal 95 %).
  3. combine="angles" is experimental. On synthetic masks degraded by a smooth random warp of about one voxel, it lost its advantage over the default on tissues of 90 and 165 cells while keeping it on small aggregates.
  4. Anisotropy above 3 was not measured; delaunay-watershed-3d warns and builds the mesh anyway. Keep the default angle reading on such meshes: the quadric reading made every route worse at real cell size.
  5. Error bars stop at about 1 300 cells. infer_tensions_with_uncertainty and compute_inference_diagnostics decompose a dense operator that scipy cannot take past 2**31 - 1 entries; on a larger mesh they refuse at once. Use infer_tensions_over_seeds for a seed spread (a lower bound on the error).
  6. The reconstruction estimate is a fit, on one machine, to medians over the benchmark tissues (2 to 10 cells) and to single tissues of 90 to 1 866 cells; its band is the largest in-sample ratio, not a guarantee.
  7. The limitations listed for 0.5.0 below still hold, except 7, fixed in 0.7.0 (item 4 above), and the end of 8: the faster neighbour search planned for 0.5.1 is in 0.7.0, and on a 1 866-cell tissue the relocation guard takes 45 s instead of 6.6 min, with the same meshes (dw3d's CHANGELOG.md).

docs.title: Release notes — 0.5.1
docs.text: 0.5.1 is the final 0.5.0 (as on GitHub's main since 27 September), published again. The 0.5.0 wheel and source archive on PyPI were built from an earlier snapshot of the release: their licence metadata says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 instead of GPL-3.0-or-later, and the force viewer is the version before its fixes (it crashes with numpy 2). GitHub's v0.5.0 tag points at that earlier snapshot too. Install 0.5.1 (pip install --upgrade foambryo delaunay-watershed-3d); 0.5.0 is withdrawn from PyPI (yanked). Inference is unchanged: every tension and pressure 0.5.1 infers is the one the final 0.5.0 infers. The 0.5.0 notes below apply to 0.5.1 as they are.

docs.text:
foambryo and delaunay-watershed-3d ship together as 0.5.0; this foambryo requires delaunay-watershed-3d>=0.5.0. This is what changes for you and what can mislead you; CHANGELOG.md has the full list, and dw3d's RELEASE_NOTES.md covers reconstruction.

0.5.0 is the first release on PyPI since 0.3.5; CHANGELOG.md also lists the changes of 0.4.0–0.4.2, which were never published there.

docs.title: What changes for you
docs.text:
• Meshes reconstructed with dw3d 0.5.0 differ from 0.4 meshes: junction relocation is on by default there, so angles and tensions inferred from a freshly reconstructed mesh move. Reconstruct with relocate_junctions=False to reproduce a 0.4 mesh.
  • dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask now defaults to min_distance=3 (was 5), dw3d's own default: a denser mesh, slower to build. Pass min_distance=5 for the 0.4 spacing.
  • The pressure and force functions now raise instead of returning a non-finite field. infer_pressures, infer_pressures_and_residuals and infer_forces raise UndeterminedTensionError (a ValueError) naming every interface whose tension is not finite; on the real embryo series this happens on 5 of 154 timepoints, all outside the segmentation-quality window, where 0.4 returned 54–71 non-finite pressures out of 55–72 without a warning. Tensions are unchanged, and pressures from finite tensions are bitwise unchanged.
  • The second-order reading (angle_reading="quadric") is now independent of the mesh's units, which moves previously published second-order numbers by up to 0.14°.
  • AngleReadingCoverageWarning now carries its numbers: the measured coverage fraction and how many trijunction lines were not fully corrected.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
Every item is measured; each is one sentence and its number.

  1. The benchmark under-rewards tangent-based improvements. Its ground-truth meshes are facet-equilibrated (Surface Evolver), so an improvement in the surface-tangent description of a contact angle is scored against a facet-based truth and can read as no change.
  2. The second-order angle reader has its own floor, and it cannot resolve junction relocation's effect. On a perfectly smooth analytic surface it reads contact angles with a floor of 0.245°, and at every point spacing measured (0 of 32 spacing-by-variant cells) its check could not resolve the effect of junction relocation on tangent-based angles, in either direction.
  3. On real embryos, do not use second-order line means at sub-degree scale. The second-order reader covers a median 0.804 of incident trijunction faces on real embryo meshes (minimum 0.454), and its line means move by 1.75° [1.41, 2.17] when uncovered faces are excluded instead of filled by the chord reading.
  4. Real embryo cells are small in voxels, so every benchmark statement is about one spacing step optimistic for them. Their equivalent radius at trijunctions is a median 17.6 voxels against 38.2 in the benchmark, so real data at min_distance 3 sits where the benchmark sits at min_distance 4; for cells this small, consider a smaller min_distance.
  5. Folded trijunctions on real meshes are mostly real geometry. Real embryo meshes carry 3.2× the benchmark's fraction of reflex (folded) trijunctional edges, and more than half of them sit where the segmentation mask's own wedge already exceeds 180°.
  6. The force-balance residual rho_free alarms on every reconstructed mesh. Its median is 0.578 on reconstructed meshes against 0.0118 on the reference meshes, so a high value on your mesh is expected and is not by itself a sign of a bad segmentation.
  7. ForceBalanceMAP is not scale-invariant, contrary to its docstring: rescaling a mesh moves its relative tensions by up to 43 %; plain ForceBalance is exact under rescaling.
  8. Junction relocation, now on by default, has a cost that grows faster than linearly with mesh size. It adds about +0.75 s to a ~5 s benchmark reconstruction (+15 %) and 0.1–1.5 s per timepoint to a ~0.6 s real-embryo reconstruction (median 0.34 s and 0.48 s on two developmental time series, about 65 s per 154-timepoint series); within one real series it grows with triangle count with a fitted exponent of 2.68 over a 2.2-fold range of mesh sizes, which is not a tissue-scale law. A faster neighbour search is planned for 0.5.1, and will leave every relocated mesh bit-for-bit unchanged.

docs.title: Colour scales
docs.text:
The colour scales of the force viewer, for every front end that colours tensions and pressures.

The Polyscope viewer (foambryo.viewing), foambryo view --colour-bars and the napari plugin colour with these functions, so one value has one colour in all of them, and a colour bar spans exactly the range the colours were clipped to:

  • tensions: coolwarm (TENSION_COLOUR_MAP: blue for low, light grey for the mean, red for high), over a range centred on the mean of the finite tensions and symmetric around it, reaching the farther of the alpha and 1 - alpha quantiles (tension_colour_range, tension_colour_fractions, tension_colours);
  • pressures: magma reversed and trimmed to its 10-90 % range (PRESSURE_COLOUR_MAP, PRESSURE_COLOUR_MAP_RANGE: no pressure is black or near-white, so none vanishes on a black or a white background), from 0 to the 1 - alpha quantile of the finite pressures over the surface's triangles (surface_pressure_colour_upper, pressure_colour_fractions, pressure_colours);
  • other per-interface quantities (a seed spread, a residual): jet between the alpha and 1 - alpha quantiles (quantile_colour_range, clipped_colour_fractions, quantity_colours);
  • undetermined values (nan): UNDETERMINED_COLOR, green, outside every map; a viewer that can draw outlines draws an undetermined interface as its outline in this green, without fill;
  • crop faces: see-through glass, CROP_FACE_COLOR at CROP_FACE_OPACITY with edges in CROP_FACE_EDGE_COLOR;
  • the backgrounds a viewer offers, by name (BACKGROUND_COLOURS: black, dark grey, light grey, white).

alpha is DEFAULT_CLIP_QUANTILE (0.05) unless given. save_colour_bars writes the bars to an image file and returns the values at their ends (ColourBarRanges). This module needs matplotlib (installed by foambryo[viewing]), but neither Polyscope nor a display. The functions are implemented in foambryo._colour_scales; this module is their public interface.

save_colour_bars(mesh: DcelData, dict_tensions: dict[tuple[int, int], float], dict_pressures: dict[int, float] | None, path: str | PathLike[str], alpha: float = DEFAULT_CLIP_QUANTILE, *, tension_label: str = 'Surface tension', pressure_label: str = 'Pressure') -> ColourBarRanges

Write the colour bars of the force viewer's surface colours to an image file.

One horizontal bar per quantity, each spanning exactly the range the viewer colours over (colour_bar_ranges), drawn with the viewer's own colour function, with its two end values written under it:

  • surface tension: coolwarm, centred on the mean of the finite tensions (one per interface; light grey), symmetric, its half-width the farther of the alpha and 1 - alpha quantiles from the mean (tension_colour_range); the viewer draws tensions beyond either end in the end's colour; the bar's middle tick is the mean;
  • pressure: magma reversed (light for low) and trimmed to its 10-90 % range, so that neither end is black or near-white, from 0 to the 1 - alpha quantile of the finite pressures over the mesh's triangles, each carrying the pressure of the higher-labelled of its two materials, as on the viewer's surface; negative pressures are drawn as 0.

A green swatch, "undetermined", is added when any value is nan, and a glass swatch, "crop face", when the mesh has crop faces. The viewer's graph view (cell nodes) colours pressures on this same scale (surface_pressure_colour_upper).

Headless: matplotlib's non-interactive canvas, no window, no Polyscope.

docs.title: Cropped tissues
docs.text: Cropped tissues: what a crop face is, and what inference does with it.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
A tissue imaged in part, or cropped from a larger image, has cells that the image boundary cuts. The mesh closes them with triangles lying on the boundary: crop faces, labelled (0, c) like contact with the medium, although nothing beyond them was observed. Read as medium contact, they make three kinds of error:

  • a tension unknown for an interface that does not exist (the crop), and a fake junction line (0, a, b) wherever the crop meets a cell-cell interface (a, b), with angles set by the crop plane rather than by the tissue;
  • force balances written at vertices on the crop, where the tissue that was cut away pulled;
  • a pressure for every cut cell, from a volume that is partly the crop.

Measured on 433 plane crops of the 47 benchmark tissues (YoungDupre, median over the 42 equilibrium cases of the relative error of the gauge-matched tensions of the interfaces that touch the crop): 13 %, 33 % and 40 % error with 10 %, 25 % and 40 % of the tissue cropped away when crop faces are read as medium contact, against 10 %, 9 % and 12 % when they are kept out; every one of the 13 tension methods improves at 25 % and 40 %, and LogLami stops failing on 25 of the crops. The interfaces away from the crop are affected too: at 40 % their error was 17 points above the uncropped tissue's, and 2 points above it with the crop kept out.

docs.title: What inference does with a crop face
docs.text:
A mesh carries its crop as a mask of faces (DcelData(..., crop_faces=...)), never as a reserved label. Then, in every tension method:

  • a crop face carries no tension unknown and enters no equation; an interface made only of crop faces (DcelData.crop_interfaces) is absent from the tension map, never a number;
  • a junction edge with a vertex on a crop face gives no equation; the rest of a junction line that ends on the crop still does (the angle-reading methods exclude such edges from the line mean, as foambryo.wedge_refusal.WedgeRefusalPolicy.ExcludeEdgeFromLineMean does for a folded edge, and both reasons combine);
  • a vertex on a crop face gives no force balance (the Variational and ForceBalance* methods drop its three rows; Equilibrium drops the edges that touch it);
  • an interface left with no equation is nan, as an interface with no junction line already is.

And in the pressure methods, a cut cell (DcelData.cut_cells: a cell with a crop face or a vertex on one) keeps its pressure as an unknown, so that its force is not pushed into anyone else's, but the pressure is not reported: it comes back nan, with a CutCellPressureWarning naming the cells. On the benchmark crops the cut cells' pressures read as measurements had 15 % to 46 % error; withholding them leaves the other cells' pressures as accurate as without the crop.

What has no formulation for crop faces yet refuses a cropped mesh with a ValueError, rather than read the crop as medium: the two Laplace pressure methods (PressureComputationMethod.Laplace and WeightedLaplace; PressureComputationMethod.has_crop_face_formulation says which methods accept a cropped mesh), foambryo.compute_inference_diagnostics and foambryo.infer_tensions_with_uncertainty. infer_force_balance follows the rules above.

On a mesh without crop faces none of this runs.

docs.title: Where crop faces come from
docs.text: delaunay-watershed-3d (dw3d) marks them during the reconstruction: the triangles a cell has on a face of the image box that the cell reaches in the mask, unless that face is declared physical (a coverslip); a mask none of whose cells reaches the image box has none. They reach foambryo through dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask, or through a .rec file whose metadata appendix records crop_faces = <first row> <count> (dw3d writes them as the last rows), or a .vtk file with a crop_face cell array. A file written before crop faces were recorded carries no such record; when its mesh has faces that look like a crop, dcel_mesh_from_file warns (UnrecordedCropFacesWarning) instead of silently reading them as medium contact.

docs.title: CutCellPressureWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Emitted when a pressure inference withholds the pressures of cut cells, reported as nan.

A cut cell has a crop face, or a vertex on one: part of its surface and volume lie outside the imaged volume. Its pressure is solved for, so that its force does not end up in the other cells' pressures, but it is not a measurement and is reported as nan. The other cells' pressures are unaffected.

docs.title: UnrecordedCropFacesWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Emitted when a mesh read from a file looks cropped but the file records no crop faces.

Such a mesh has triangles (0, c) lying flat on a face of its own bounding box, like the faces a reconstruction places where the image boundary cuts a cell. Without a record of which they are, they are read as contact with the medium, which puts large errors on the tensions near them and on the pressures of the cells they close. Re-export the mesh with a current delaunay-watershed-3d, or pass the crop faces explicitly (DcelData(..., crop_faces=...)).

docs.text:
border_like_faces(points: NDArray[floating], triangles: NDArray[integer], labels: NDArray[integer]) -> NDArray[np.bool_]

Triangles that look like crop faces although nothing says they are.

A crop face, as a reconstruction writes it, is a triangle between the medium and a cell lying flat on a face of the volume, so on a face of the mesh's own bounding box. A triangle counts here when its labels are (0, c) in either order and its three vertices have exactly the bounding box's minimum or maximum coordinate on one axis; and a bounding-box face counts only when such triangles span at least BORDER_LIKE_MIN_SPAN of its extent on both of its other axes and the largest patch of them connected through shared edges covers at least BORDER_LIKE_MIN_PATCH_AREA of the face, so that the few scattered flat triangles an uncropped tissue has at its extremes do not count.

A heuristic, used only to decide whether to warn: it misses the few crop-face vertices a junction relocation moved off the plane, and it cannot tell a crop from a large flat contact that coincides with the bounding box.

docs.text:
Mean curvature of a mesh's interfaces, from the cotangent Laplacian, as the Laplace pressure methods read it.

Curvatures are in inverse mesh length units. An interface all of whose vertices lie on junction lines has no curvature (nan); see foambryo.pressure_inference.UndeterminedPressureWarning.

Sacha Ichbiah, 2021. Matthieu Perez, 2024.

docs.title: compute_laplacian_cotan
docs.text:
compute_laplacian_cotan(points: NDArray[float64], triangles: NDArray[int64]) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.float64]]

Laplacian computation.

Consider a mesh M = (V, F), with verts of shape Nx3 and faces of shape Mx3. The Laplacian matrix L is a NxN matrix such that LV gives a matrix of vectors: LV[i] gives the normal scaled by the discrete mean curvature. For vertex i, assume S[i] is the set of neighboring vertices to i, a_ij and b_ij are the "outside" angles in the two triangles connecting vertex v_i and its neighboring vertex v_j for j in S[i], as seen in the diagram below. .. code-block:: python a_ij /\ / \ / \ / \ v_i /________\ v_j \ / \ / \ / \ / \/ b_ij The definition of the Laplacian is LV[i] = sum_j w_ij (v_j - v_i) For the uniform variant, w_ij = 1 / |S[i]| For the cotangent variant, w_ij = (cot a_ij + cot b_ij) / (sum_k cot a_ik + cot b_ik) For the cotangent curvature, w_ij = (cot a_ij + cot b_ij) / (4 A[i]) where A[i] is the sum of the areas of all triangles containing vertex v_i. There is a nice trigonometry identity to compute cotangents. Consider a triangle with side lengths A, B, C and angles a, b, c. .. code-block:: python c /|\ / | \ / | \ B / H| \ A / | \ / | \ /a_____|_____b\ C Then cot a = (B^2 + C^2 - A^2) / 4 * area We know that area = CH/2, and by the law of cosines we have A^2 = B^2 + C^2 - 2BC cos a => B^2 + C^2 - A^2 = 2BC cos a Putting these together, we get: B^2 + C^2 - A^2 2BC cos a _______________ = _________ = (B/H) cos a = cos a / sin a = cot a 4 * area 2CH [1] Desbrun et al, "Implicit fairing of irregular meshes using diffusion and curvature flow", SIGGRAPH 1999. [2] Nealan et al, "Laplacian Mesh Optimization", Graphite 2006.

docs.title: The force-balance family
docs.text:
Tensions and pressures in one solve, from the unified discrete force-balance operator.

infer_force_balance is the entry point; the ForceBalance* members of foambryo.TensionComputationMethod call it through infer_tensions. Where the eight classical methods in foambryo.tension_inference each impose a local balance written in measured angles (Young-Dupre, Lami, cotangent) or in per-interface area gradients (Variational), this module inverts the global discrete equilibrium condition directly:

E(v) = sum_interfaces gamma_m A_m(v) - sum_cells p_c V_c(v),
equilibrium  <=>  grad_v E = 0  <=>  M beta = 0,     beta = (gamma, p),

with M = [M_gamma | M_p] assembled by foambryo.validation.force_balance.force_balance_operator: row block i is the gradient of E with respect to vertex i, built from the discrete area and volume gradients of its triangles (the documentation's methods note describes it). By the package author's design choice the line-tension block M_t is not used: beta = (gamma, p).

Sign convention. The operator's pressure columns are +dV_c/dv, so the energy above puts pressure in with a minus and the solved pressure-block entries are -p. This module negates them, so ForceBalanceResult.pressures are physical pressures on foambryo's usual convention (exterior medium at 0, higher pressure inside a convex cell). The exterior label is not a column at all — mesh_io.cell_labels drops it — which is what fixes the additive pressure gauge; without that the constant-pressure shift would be an exact null direction of M_p and every solve below would be singular.

The normalisation (the gauge), and the three variants. M beta = 0 is homogeneous: beta = 0 minimises it and only tension ratios are physical, so one scale convention has to be added: the tensions are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension. This module offers three ways of imposing it, ForceBalanceNormalisation:

  • Kkt — mean(gamma) = mean_tension as a hard constraint: minimise ||M beta||^2 subject to a^T beta = mean_tension (a = 1/ni on the surface-tension entries, 0 on the pressures) by solving the KKT system [[2 M^T M, a], [a^T, 0]] @ (beta, lambda) = (0, mean_tension). Exact by construction, and the constraint cannot compete with the physics rows.
  • SoftRow — one extra least-squares row sum(gamma) = ni * mean_tension, the convention the angle-reading, cotangent and Equilibrium methods used until 0.6.0 (since 0.7.0 they meet the normalisation exactly, see foambryo.junction_graph). The normalisation then competes with the physics rows, so the returned mean is only approximately mean_tension.
  • BayesianMap — Gaussian prior on beta, MAP estimate and posterior covariance (map_estimate). The prior anchors the scale softly and shrinks the tensions toward the prior mean, so this variant's gauge is deliberately not exact; report it gauge-matched (the rule every accuracy comparison in this package follows).

All three produce a per-interface standard deviation. For Kkt it is the constrained-GLS covariance with sigma_f estimated from the fit's own residual, so it carries no free hyperparameter and is exactly zero along the fixed gauge direction; see foambryo.validation.force_balance.constrained_covariance for the model and for the caveat that i.i.d. force noise understates the true (spatially correlated) uncertainty.

Reliability on reconstructed meshes -- read every number from this module with this. The operator is inverted on the mesh it is given, and a dw3d-reconstructed mesh is not a force balance for any tension assignment: its rho_free (foambryo.uncertainty) is about fifty times the reference meshes' own value, on every case and independent of which sampler produced it. Measured on the 40 equilibrium cases of the benchmark cohort against their own reference meshes (shipped default reconstruction: dithered point placement, seed 42, min_distance = 3): rho_free median 0.578, range 0.479-0.718, against the references' 0.0118, range 0.00066-0.036 -- a ratio of medians of 49, a median per-case ratio of 50, per-case ratios from 17 to 850 -- and every one of the 40 above the 0.2 alarm threshold; the deterministic variant reads 0.623. The five non-equilibrium cases' references already sit at 0.26 and their reconstructions at 0.59. rho at the Kkt solution equals rho_free by construction, so the solve cannot lower it. Every ForceBalance* tension and pressure inferred on a reconstruction, and every comparison of one reconstruction against another through this family, stands on that floor until the reconstruction itself moves it; the angle-reading family (YoungDupre and relatives) never inverts M and is not bounded this way. Whether the family is repairable on reconstructed meshes is an open scientific question, not addressed here.

docs.title: ForceBalanceNormalisation
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

How the overall tension scale (the normalisation, or gauge) is fixed when inverting M beta = 0.

  • Kkt: mean(gamma) = mean_tension, exactly, through a KKT system. The default, and the one TensionComputationMethod.ForceBalance uses.
  • SoftRow: the same condition as one more least-squares row, met only approximately (TensionComputationMethod.ForceBalanceSoftRow).
  • BayesianMap: a Gaussian prior centred on mean_tension, so the mean is deliberately not exactly mean_tension (TensionComputationMethod.ForceBalanceMAP).

See the module docstring.

Per-interface standard deviation, shape (ni,), from the variant's own model (for Kkt, i.i.d. force noise, which understates the uncertainty; see foambryo.uncertainty for measured error bars).

normalisation ForceBalanceNormalisation

Which gauge treatment produced this.

mean_tension_deviation float

|mean(tensions) / mean_tension - 1|. Exactly the quantity the three variants are compared on; ~1e-16 for Kkt by construction.

residual_norm float

||M beta||.

rho float

||M beta|| / ||M_gamma gamma|| at the inferred tensions — the fraction of the surface-tension force this mesh leaves unbalanced under them. For Kkt it is rho_free: the ratio at the minimiser of ||M beta|| under the gauge, which is close to, but not strictly, the lowest ratio any tensions reach (see foambryo.validation.force_balance.effective_surface_tensions).

condition_number float

Condition number of the linear system actually solved (the KKT matrix, the augmented operator, or the posterior precision).

sigma_f float

Force-residual noise scale used for the error bars.

docs.text:
infer_force_balance(mesh: DcelData, mean_tension: float = 1, normalisation: ForceBalanceNormalisation = ForceBalanceNormalisation.Kkt) -> ForceBalanceResult

Infer tensions and pressures by inverting the discrete force-balance operator.

One solve produces both blocks of beta = (gamma, p), so unlike the classical path (tensions from angles, then pressures from a second variational solve) the two are consistent by construction.

Warning -- reconstructed meshes. On dw3d output the returned rho is about fifty times what the same operator reads on the simulator's reference meshes (median 0.578 against 0.0118 on the 40-case equilibrium cohort, all 40 above the 0.2 alarm threshold of InferenceDiagnostics.identifiability_report); no tension assignment balances such a mesh, so the tensions and pressures returned are the least-bad fit to a geometry that is not an equilibrium. Read rho before reading the tensions. See the module docstring.

Cropped meshes (foambryo.crop_faces): the force balances of the vertices on crop faces are left out; the crop interfaces are absent from interfaces; an interface or cell left without an equation is nan; and the pressures of the cut cells are solved for and reported as nan, with a CutCellPressureWarning naming them.

docs.title: Tensions and pressures together
docs.text:
Tensions and pressures in one call: infer_forces, and infer_tensions_then_pressures for front ends.

infer_forces runs infer_tensions then infer_pressures and raises when either refuses; infer_tensions_then_pressures makes the same two calls, keeps the tensions when the pressure solve refuses them, and returns the refusal as an InferenceOutcome instead of raising it.

Sacha Ichbiah 2021 Matthieu Perez 2024

infer_forces(mesh: DcelData, mean_tension: float = 1, base_pressure: float = 0, mode_tension: TensionComputationMethod = TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre, mode_pressure: PressureComputationMethod = PressureComputationMethod.Variational, *, solver: str = 'auto', sparse_threshold: int | None = None, diagnostics: bool | str = False) -> tuple

Infer the relative tensions, then the pressures, of a 3D mesh.

infer_tensions(mesh, mean_tension, mode_tension, ...) then infer_pressures(mesh, tensions, mode_pressure, base_pressure, ...), with the same solver options; see those two functions for every convention, warning and failure.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

Mesh to analyze, in any length unit.

required mean_tension float

The normalisation: the tensions are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension, exactly, in each connected piece of the junction graph (see foambryo.infer_tensions). Defaults to 1.

1 base_pressure float

Pressure of the exterior medium (label 0). Defaults to 0.

0 mode_tension TensionComputationMethod

Method for tension computation. Defaults to TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre.

YoungDupre mode_pressure PressureComputationMethod

Method for pressure computation. Defaults to PressureComputationMethod.Variational.

Variational solver str

"auto" (the default), "dense" or "sparse", passed to both the tension and the pressure solves (foambryo.linear_solves). "auto" is dense below sparse_threshold unknowns and sparse at or above, and bitwise the dense result below it. "sparse" raises ValueError for a tension method with no sparse path (Equilibrium, Variational, ForceBalance*). Keyword-only.

'auto' sparse_threshold int | None

unknowns at which "auto" goes sparse; None (the default) is foambryo.junction_graph.SPARSE_SOLVE_MIN_UNKNOWNS (2 000). Keyword-only.

None diagnostics bool | str

False (the default), True or "spectrum": also return a foambryo.linear_solves.SolveDiagnostics holding the records of the tension solves then of the pressure solve. Keyword-only.

False

Returns:

Type Description tuple

tuple[dict[tuple[int, int], float], dict[int, float]]: - map of interface (label_1, label_2), label_1 < label_2 -> relative tension on this interface. An undetermined interface (for example one with no triple line at all) is float("nan"); a triple-junction graph in several pieces gives tensions normalised separately in each piece, which are not on the same scale (see foambryo.tension_inference.infer_tensions's return value, and foambryo.tension_inference.infer_tensions_by_junction_component for the per-piece alternative). - map of cell label (0 = exterior, at base_pressure) -> pressure, in the unit of the tensions divided by the mesh's length unit; nan for a cell whose pressure is undetermined or that the crop cuts. - with diagnostics on, a third value: the SolveDiagnostics.

The pressure solve couples every cell to every tension, so such a tension would make nearly every pressure non-finite; pressures are refused instead. Call infer_tensions for the tensions alone (or infer_tensions_then_pressures, which keeps them), and infer_tensions_by_junction_component to see which interfaces are undetermined.
