as infer_tensions.

as infer_pressures.

infer_tensions_then_pressures(mesh: DcelData, mean_tension: float = 1, base_pressure: float = 0, mode_tension: TensionComputationMethod = TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre, mode_pressure: PressureComputationMethod = PressureComputationMethod.Variational, *, solver: str = 'auto', diagnostics: bool | str = False, with_pressures: bool = True) -> InferenceOutcome

The tensions then the pressures, by the two calls infer_forces makes, keeping what succeeds.

infer_forces runs infer_tensions then infer_pressures with these arguments and raises when either is refused. This function makes the same two calls itself, so that the tensions survive a pressure solve that refuses them (UndeterminedTensionError), and returns the refusal instead of raising it: what the foambryo infer command and the napari plugin need to report a partial result. The numbers are bitwise those of infer_forces with the same arguments. Every default is infer_forces's.

With with_pressures=False only the first call is made (infer_tensions with the same arguments, so the tensions are bitwise those of infer_forces), base_pressure and mode_pressure are not used, the outcome's pressures is None with the status "complete", and library_call is that infer_tensions call.

sparse_threshold is not an argument: the default threshold (2 000 unknowns) always applies.

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

the mesh, in any length unit.

required mean_tension float

the normalisation: the tensions are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension, exactly, in each connected piece of the junction graph. Defaults to 1.

1 base_pressure float

the pressure of the exterior medium, label 0. Defaults to 0.

0 mode_tension TensionComputationMethod

the tension method. Defaults to YoungDupre.

YoungDupre mode_pressure PressureComputationMethod

the pressure method. Defaults to Variational.

Variational solver str

"auto" (the default), "dense" or "sparse", as for infer_forces. Keyword-only.

'auto' diagnostics bool | str

False (the default), True or "spectrum", as for infer_forces; the solve records are returned in InferenceOutcome.records. Keyword-only.

False with_pressures bool

False infers the tensions only (no pressure solve). Defaults to True. Keyword-only.

True

Name Type Description InferenceOutcome InferenceOutcome

the tensions and pressures computed, the solve records, the status and the library call. A ValueError or MalformedTripleLineError from either call is returned as the status "failed" with its message (the tensions kept when they were computed), an UndeterminedTensionError from the pressure call as "pressures refused"; nothing of these is raised.

if the variational pressure system is singular (not caught).

docs.text:
Geometry on a DCEL mesh: trijunction angles and lengths, areas, volumes, and their derivatives.

Computation of trijunction mean angles (in radians, under any of the angle readings of foambryo.second_order_angle_reading) and lengths, interface and region areas, region volumes, and their derivatives with respect to the vertex positions. Every quantity is in the mesh's own length unit; interfaces are keyed (label_1, label_2), label_1 < label_2, label 0 the exterior medium.

Sacha Ichbiah, Sept 2021. Matthieu Perez, 2024.

Sparse area-gradient operator D (n_interfaces x 3*n_points), one row per interface.

Row i is the flattened gradient of interface keys[i]'s total area with respect to every vertex coordinate; vertex v's three components sit at columns 3v, 3v+1, 3v+2. The per-vertex contributions are identical to :func:compute_area_derivative_dict, but the operator is assembled by a single vectorised COO scatter-add over the triangle list (O(n_triangles) non-zeros, mean support ~6 % of points per interface) — no Python loop over interfaces or vertices, and never a dense (n_interfaces, n_points, 3) array. docs.title: compute_angles_tri
docs.text:
compute_angles_tri(mesh: DcelData, unique: bool = True, *, reading: str = CHORD_READING) -> tuple[dict[tuple[int, int, int], float], dict[tuple[int, int, int], float], dict[tuple[int, int, int], float]]

Compute three maps trijunction (id reg 1, id reg 2, id reg 3) to mean angle, mean angle (deg), length.

The keys are wedge keys: (min(e, g), f, max(e, g)) is the angle of the wedge inside region f at the triple line where regions e, f and g meet, so one triple line contributes three keys whose angles sum to 360 degrees.

That sum holds exactly only under an oriented reading. Under "chord" and "quadric" the angle is arccos of a dot product, whose range is [0, 180] degrees, so a wedge wider than a straight angle comes back as 360 - theta and its edge's three angles sum to 360 - 2 (theta - 180). "oriented_chord" and "oriented_quadric" return the wedge in [0, 360) and restore the identity; they are bitwise identical to their unoriented counterparts on every wedge that is not reflex.

unique. In earlier versions the parameter had no effect except to double every accumulator uniformly, which changes neither the mean angle nor the length ratio that every builder actually uses. It now means what its name says:

  • unique=True (the declared default) counts each geometric trijunctional edge exactly once per wedge key. dict_length[key] is then the true arclength of that triple line, and sum(dict_length.values()) / 3 — the total_length_mesh every builder computes — is then the true total junction length of the mesh, which it was not before.
  • unique=False reproduces the historical accumulation bit for bit: each geometric edge is visited once per incident half-edge (3) and each visit appends twice, so dict_length[key] = 6 * length and sum(...) / 3 = 6 * L_total. Every call site inside foambryo.tension_inference passes unique=False, so no inferred number moves.

The mean angles are identical either way — the over-count was, and remains, uniform on the benchmarking dataset (BENCHMARKS.md). That uniformity was verified rather than assumed: on all 47 of its meshes every trijunctional geometric edge has exactly 3 incident half-edges, and the three visits return bit-identical angles. The one construction where that edge accounting is not uniform — a triple line running off an open mesh boundary, where an edge that has lost one of its three films is dropped and the line's length weight is under-stated in proportion — is pinned in tests/test_per_edge_young_dupre.py.

reading. "chord" (the default) is the convention described above; adding the selector changed none of its numbers. "oriented_chord" is the same reading with the wedge angle reported in [0, 360) degrees instead of [0, 180], so a wedge wider than a straight angle is no longer reported as its reflection and the three wedge keys of a line really do sum to 360 degrees; it is bitwise identical to "chord" wherever no wedge is reflex. "quadric" replaces each triangle's chord by the tangent of a generic quadric fitted to that interface's own mesh vertices around the junction — see foambryo.second_order_angle_reading. It is not available on every face of every mesh: where the fit is inadmissible the chord is kept, so a "quadric" result can mix the two conventions. This function reports that mixing as an AngleReadingCoverageWarning; use :func:compute_angles_tri_with_report to receive the coverage numbers instead.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

Mesh to analyze.

required unique bool

Count each geometric edge once (True) or reproduce the historical 6x over-count (False). Defaults to True.

True reading str

"chord", "quadric", "oriented_chord" or "oriented_quadric". Keyword-only. Defaults to "chord", which is bit-identical to the historical behaviour.

CHORD_READING

Returns:

Type Description tuple[dict[tuple[int, int, int], float], dict[tuple[int, int, int], float], dict[tuple[int, int, int], float]]

tuple[dict, dict, dict]: mean angle (rad), mean angle (deg) and accumulated length, all keyed by wedge key.

The reporting entry point. Use it whenever a result will be published, compared or benchmarked: it is the only way to know which trijunction lines a "quadric" reading could not cover and therefore read as chords.

Uses the same convention helper as :func:compute_angles_tri (:func:_wedges_at_half_edge), so averaging this function's angles over the edges of a triple line reproduces compute_angles_tri's mean for that line to machine precision — pinned by tests/test_per_edge_young_dupre.py.

De-duplication is by the geometric edge's (min, max) vertex-key pair, keeping the lowest-keyed incident half-edge; the choice does not matter numerically (the three visits of every trijunctional edge in the 47 meshes of the benchmarking dataset were measured to be bit-identical) but it makes the output deterministic. Quadrijunctional edges are skipped, exactly as compute_angles_tri skips them.

reading selects the angle convention exactly as :func:compute_angles_tri does, and it is the route by which TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupreLocal reaches the second-order reading. The edge set, the lengths and the de-duplication do not depend on it — only the angles do.

docs.title: Reading meshes and masks
docs.text:
The meshes every inference reads: a DcelData from a segmentation mask, raw mesh arrays or a mesh file.

Inputs can be: - a segmentation mask (3D uint array) ; - a multimaterial mesh: points, triangles, labels ; - a file (.rec, or opened by meshio) containing a multimaterial mesh.

Output is always a DcelData mesh. Conventions: label 0 is the exterior medium; a mask's axes are (z, y, x) and the mesh's coordinates follow them, column 0 along axis 0; the mesh is in voxel units unless a spacing gives a physical one, and the inferred pressures are in the tension unit divided by that length unit.

Matthieu Perez 2024.

docs.title: MaskReconstruction dataclass
docs.text:
MaskReconstruction(points: NDArray[float64], triangles: NDArray[int64], labels: NDArray[int64], crop_faces: NDArray[bool_] | None, spacing: tuple[float, float, float], spacing_unit: str, min_distance: int, rec_bytes: bytes, n_cells: int, n_cut_cells: int)

A mask's mesh as foambryo mesh reconstructs it, held as plain arrays and the bytes of its .rec file.

Returned by reconstruct_mask. It holds no reconstruction algorithm, so it pickles to the size of the mesh (a front end can reconstruct in a child process and send it back), and it writes the .rec file foambryo mesh writes, byte for byte, because it holds the bytes delaunay-watershed-3d's own export wrote.

Attributes:

Name Type Description points NDArray[float64]

the mesh's points, in the unit of spacing, axis order (z, y, x).

triangles NDArray[int64]

the triangles, as the reconstruction returned them.

labels NDArray[int64]

the two materials of each triangle.

crop_faces NDArray[bool_] | None

True on the crop faces, aligned with triangles, or None when the reconstruction records none.

spacing tuple[float, float, float]

the voxel size the mask was reconstructed with, (dz, dy, dx).

spacing_unit str

its unit.

min_distance int

the reconstruction's min_distance, in cubic voxels of the shortest spacing.

rec_bytes bytes

the .rec file (crop faces as its last triangle rows, metadata appendix included).

n_cells int

the labels other than the medium that the mesh holds.

n_cut_cells int

the cells the image boundary cuts.

docs.title: reconstruct_mask
docs.text:
reconstruct_mask(segmentation_mask: NDArray[uint], spacing: tuple[float, float, float], *, spacing_unit: str = 'um', min_distance: int = 3) -> MaskReconstruction

Reconstruct a mask's mesh in physical units, exactly as foambryo mesh does.

The call is delaunay-watershed-3d's entry point for masks with a voxel size, get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm(min_distance, False).construct_mesh_in_physical_units(mask, spacing, spacing_unit=spacing_unit, axis_order="zyx"): a mask whose voxels are longer along one axis is resampled to cubic voxels of the shortest spacing, meshed, and the mesh is scaled to the unit of spacing; cubic voxels are meshed as they are. Every face of the image box is a crop. The mesh's numbers are those of dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask, min_distance, spacing=spacing); only the unit recorded in the .rec file depends on spacing_unit.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default segmentation_mask NDArray[uint]

3-D labels, axis 0 = z (see foambryo.segmentation_masks.check_segmentation_mask).

required spacing tuple[float, float, float]

(dz, dy, dx), the voxel size along axes 0, 1, 2; one axis may be longer than the other two, which must be equal.

required spacing_unit str

the unit of spacing, recorded in the .rec file. Keyword-only. Defaults to "um", the command's.

'um' min_distance int

minimum distance between the reconstruction's points, in cubic voxels of the shortest spacing. Keyword-only. Defaults to 3, delaunay-watershed-3d's.

3

Returns:

Name Type Description MaskReconstruction MaskReconstruction

the mesh's arrays, its .rec bytes and its counts.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

on a spacing the resampling cannot handle, or a mask the reconstruction refuses; or if the installed delaunay-watershed-3d has no construct_mesh_in_physical_units.

docs.title: dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask
docs.text:
dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(segmentation_mask: NDArray[uint], min_distance: int = 3, print_info: bool = False, *, physical_image_faces: Iterable[str] = (), spacing: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None) -> DcelData

Obtain a DcelData mesh from a segmentation mask using Delaunay-Watershed 3D.

The default mesh reconstruction algorithm is used (its dither seed is 42; see foambryo.infer_tensions_over_seeds for other seeds), with its junction relocation (on by default since dw3d 0.5.0). The mesh carries the reconstruction's crop faces: the triangles a cell has on a face of the image box that the cell reaches in the mask, where the image cut the tissue (see foambryo.crop_faces). Every inference method keeps them out of its equations and reports the pressures of the cells they cut as nan.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default segmentation_mask NDArray[uint]

Instance segmentation image: 3-D integer labels, axes (z, y, x), label 0 the medium, one label per cell. The mesh's coordinates follow the mask's axes, column 0 along axis 0.

required min_distance int

minimum distance between points of the output mesh, in voxels. Defaults to 3, dw3d's own default (it was 5 up to foambryo 0.4.2). Pass 5 to reproduce the 0.4 spacing; at 5 or more dw3d emits CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning once per reconstruction.

3 print_info bool

print mesh construction details. Defaults to False.

False physical_image_faces Iterable[str]

faces of the image box where the tissue really ends, for example on a coverslip: "axis0_low" (index 0 along the mask's first axis), "axis0_high", ... "axis2_high". Cell surfaces on them are contact with the medium. Keyword-only. Defaults to none: every image face is a crop.

() spacing tuple[float, float, float] | None

the voxel size along the mask's axes 0, 1, 2, in any one unit; one axis (a z step) may be longer than the other two, which must be equal. Keyword-only. Defaults to None: the mesh is reconstructed on the voxel grid and returned in voxel units. Given, the call is delaunay-watershed-3d's construct_mesh_in_physical_units: the mask is resampled to cubic voxels of the shortest spacing (shape-based interpolation), meshed with the same settings (min_distance then counts cubic voxels), and the mesh is returned in the unit of spacing, with DcelData.source_spacing set. Measured on 12 simulated tissues of 90 and 165 cells at a real cell size, down-sampled along z, against the same tissues meshed at full resolution: resampling first costs +0.83, +0.71 and +1.17 degrees of contact-angle error at an anisotropy of 5/3, 2 and 3, against +1.38, +1.97 and +4.10 for meshing the native grid and scaling the mesh. Above 3 nothing was measured at that cell size, and delaunay-watershed-3d warns (UnmeasuredAnisotropyWarning); the mesh is built anyway. The cost is that of a mask acquired at the short spacing: the anisotropy times the voxels.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description DcelData DcelData

The mesh reconstructed from the segmentation and ready for force inference, in voxel units without spacing and in the spacing's unit with it.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

if physical_image_faces names an unknown face, or is given to a dw3d that does not record crop faces; if spacing is not three positive finite numbers with at most one longer axis, or is given to a dw3d without construct_mesh_in_physical_units.

Warns:

Type Description UserWarning

the reconstruction's own warnings, from delaunay-watershed-3d (for example CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning at min_distance 5 or more, or UnmeasuredAnisotropyWarning above an anisotropy of 3).

dcel_mesh_from_multimaterial_mesh(points: NDArray[float64], triangles: NDArray[int64], labels: NDArray[int64], *, crop_faces: NDArray[bool_] | NDArray[integer] | None = None, source_spacing: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None) -> DcelData

which triangles are crop faces, as a boolean mask or row indices (see DcelData). Keyword-only. Defaults to None, no crop face.

None source_spacing tuple | None

None

Name Type Description DcelData DcelData

The mesh ready for force inference.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

as DcelData: a triangle with the same material on both sides, an invalid crop_faces or source_spacing.

docs.title: dcel_mesh_from_file
docs.text:
dcel_mesh_from_file(filename: str | Path) -> DcelData

Obtain a DcelData mesh for force inference from a multimaterial mesh file.

It can be either a .rec (or .arec) file created from Delaunay-Watershed 3D, or a mesh that can be opened by meshio and contains a "label1" and "label2" data. The .vtk meshes saved by Delaunay-Watershed 3D are an example of such meshes. The mesh is read in the length unit of the file.

Crop faces are read from the file when it records them: in a .rec file, the metadata appendix's crop_faces = <first row> <count> (the last block of triangle rows); in a file meshio opens, a crop_face cell array. A file that records neither is read without crop faces; if its mesh has triangles that look like crop faces (between the medium and a cell, lying flat on a face of the mesh's bounding box over a large patch), an UnrecordedCropFacesWarning says so, because they are then read as contact with the medium.

The source voxel size is read from a .rec file whose appendix says the mesh is in physical units (coordinate_frame = physical, spacing = ...), as DcelData.source_spacing; it changes no number. Any other file gives None.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default filename str | Path

Path to the file on disk.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description DcelData DcelData

The mesh ready for force inference.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

if the file's crop record is inconsistent with its triangles, or as DcelData (a triangle with the same material on both sides).

Warns:

Type Description UnrecordedCropFacesWarning

when the file records no crop faces but its mesh has triangles that look like them.

docs.title: The junction graph and the normalisation
docs.text:
The junction graph of a mesh, and the tension solves normalised in each of its connected pieces.

The normalisation (the "gauge"). A mesh determines tension ratios only, so every tension solve adds one condition that fixes the overall scale: the tensions are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension, exactly, in each connected piece of the junction graph. This module calls that condition the gauge, and a connected piece of the graph a component.

Why per piece. A Young-Dupre-family solver couples two interfaces only when they share a triple line. Build the graph with interfaces as nodes and an edge wherever two interfaces meet at a triple line (foambryo.validation.mesh_io.list_junctions). If that graph has k connected components, the tension system decomposes into k blocks each determined only up to its own scale, while mean(gamma) = mean_tension supplies a single global constraint. Ordinary least squares then returns the minimum-norm solution, which drives the k - 1 unpinned blocks towards zero -- giving a gauge-matched relative error of exactly 1.0, silently. This was found on 12 of the 72 ground-truth simulator meshes of 91-166 cells described in BENCHMARKS.md.

A degenerate sub-case. An interface that is a fully closed surface (an engulfed cell, a sealed lumen) has no triple line at all, so it is an isolated node in no junction-graph edge and no equation in any builder's physics rows. Its tension is not merely unpinned in scale -- it is wholly undetermined, and this module reports it as such (float("nan")), never as a number, never silently folded into a component.

The design. Infer per component, normalised per component: each block's tensions are internally consistent and comparable only within the block. That is surfaced in the output, not buried in a docstring -- ComponentTensionSolution carries, for every interface, which component it belongs to and which normalisation was applied to that component; isolated/closed interfaces are reported as undetermined, never as a component with a normalisation and never as a number; and any code that would aggregate tensions across components must refuse rather than silently blend two incompatible scales (require_single_component_solution below).

The normalisation is exact (since 0.7.0). The builders still append a row of ones, sum(gamma) = n * f(mean_tension); solve_gauged_least_squares reads its value and replaces the row by solve_with_exact_gauge: a gauge row weighted to the physics rows' median norm (the best-conditioned weight), then an exact rescale (homogeneous rows) or shift (difference rows), so that each component's tensions meet their gauge exactly. Until 0.6.0 the row of ones was a soft least-squares row of weight 1. Because the physics rows are homogeneous, its weight changed only the overall scale of the solution, never a tension ratio, but it missed the requested mean (by ~1e-6 for YoungDupre, up to 80 % for Equilibrium) and raised the condition number by up to three orders of magnitude (2.8e7 against 311 on a 1 866-cell tissue's YoungDupre system), which is what limited the iterative solve's accuracy to ~1e-6 of the tension scale.

Scope: which methods. This module decomposes any solver whose assembled system is [physics rows; one trailing global gauge rowsum(gamma) = n * f(mean_tension)], which is every method in foambryo.tension_inference and foambryo.per_edge_tension_inference except:

  • TensionComputationMethod.Equilibrium, whose physics rows are keyed by geometric mesh edges (len(edge.twin) != 1), which include quadrijunction edges that mesh_io.list_junctions does not enumerate (it only finds edges bordering exactly three regions) -- so this module's triple-line-only graph would not necessarily match Equilibrium's actual row coupling. A known limitation: Equilibrium is normalised over the whole mesh at once, never decomposed;
  • the ForceBalance* and Variational family, whose operator additionally carries area and volume gradients tied to shared cells and is column-coupled through the pressure block rather than through the triple-junction graph alone -- measured not to fragment the same way, so these are normalised over the whole mesh at once and never decomposed here.

lsqr did not converge on a large linear system.

docs.title: MalformedTripleLineError
docs.text:
MalformedTripleLineError(edge: tuple[int, int] | None, triple: tuple[int, int, int] | None, missing_interface: Interface)

Bases: RuntimeError

A triple-line edge names an interface pair absent from the mesh's own interface list.

Structurally, this should not be reachable after mesh_io.list_junctions's stricter admission rule: a genuine triple line's three sub-interfaces are, by construction, its three incident triangles' own region pairs (see that function's docstring). This is a named, catchable safety net standing in for what used to be a bare KeyError naming an internal union-find dict key -- for any future change to list_junctions's guarantee, or any caller that builds junctions/edge_to_triple some other way.

Attributes:

Name Type Description edge

The mesh edge (u, v), u < v, that synthesized triple -- None if no edge in edge_to_triple could be matched to it.

triple

The region-triple (a, b, c) the edge synthesized.

missing_interface

The interface pair from triple that has no key in the union-find parent map, i.e. does not occur as any triangle's actual region pair.

Build the error from the offending edge, its synthesized triple, and the missing interface.

docs.title: JunctionGraphPartition dataclass
docs.text:
JunctionGraphPartition(interfaces: tuple[Interface, ...], components: tuple[tuple[Interface, ...], ...], component_of: dict[Interface, int], isolated: tuple[Interface, ...])

Connected-component partition of a mesh's interfaces by its triple-junction graph.

Attributes:

Name Type Description interfaces tuple[Interface, ...]

Every interface present on the mesh (mesh_io.list_interfaces).

components tuple[tuple[Interface, ...], ...]

One tuple of interface keys per connected component, ordered largest first (ties broken by the component's smallest key); a mesh with a fully connected junction graph has exactly one component containing every touched interface.

component_of dict[Interface, int]

Map interface -> component index, for every interface except the isolated ones (which are never assigned a component -- see isolated).

isolated tuple[Interface, ...]

Interfaces touching no triple line at all (closed surfaces). Disjoint from every entry of components.

docs.title: n_components property
docs.text:
n_components: int

Number of proper (gaugeable) components -- excludes isolated interfaces.

docs.title: fragmented property
docs.text:
fragmented: bool

True iff a single global mean(gamma) = mean_tension normalisation no longer pins one scale.

This is the case whenever there is more than one component, or at least one isolated interface -- an isolated interface is already a failure of the single-gauge assumption even if the rest of the mesh's junction graph is fully connected.

docs.title: JunctionGraphGaugeWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Emitted when a mesh's triple-junction graph is in several pieces or has an undetermined interface.

Fires whenever JunctionGraphPartition.fragmented is true: more than one component (a connected piece of the junction graph, normalised on its own), at least one undetermined interface (no surviving triple line, e.g. a fully closed surface), or both. Tensions in different components sit on different, arbitrary relative scales -- comparing or averaging them directly is meaningless -- and an undetermined interface is reported as nan, never a number. Emitted by infer_tensions, infer_tensions_and_residuals, infer_forces and infer_tensions_over_seeds, whose flat maps hold the tensions of every component side by side; use foambryo.tension_inference.infer_tensions_by_junction_component to get each interface's component explicitly instead of blending them.

docs.title: ComponentTensionSolution dataclass
docs.text:
ComponentTensionSolution(tensions: NDArray[float64], dict_tensions: dict[Interface, float], component_of: dict[Interface, int | None], gauge_notes: dict[int, str], undetermined: tuple[Interface, ...], lstsq_residuals: NDArray[float64], fragmented: bool, n_components: int, solver_notes: dict[int, dict[str, object]] = dict())

One inference's tensions, decomposed by the junction graph.

When fragmented is False this is the solve of the whole mesh with one normalisation, mean(gamma) = mean_tension met exactly. When fragmented is True, each connected component of the interfaces' triple-junction graph was solved with its own mean(gamma) = mean_tension normalisation, met exactly; a component's tensions are therefore comparable only to each other, never across components, and gauge_notes says so per component. Isolated interfaces (no triple line at all) are undetermined: dict_tensions maps them to float("nan"), and component_of maps them to None.

Attributes:

Name Type Description tensions NDArray[float64]

(n_interfaces,), aligned with the keys the caller passed in; float("nan") at every undetermined interface.

dict_tensions dict[Interface, float]

The same, keyed by interface. float("nan") for undetermined interfaces -- never a number.

component_of dict[Interface, int | None]

Interface -> component index, or None for an undetermined interface.

gauge_notes dict[int, str]

Component index -> a one-line description of the gauge applied to it.

undetermined tuple[Interface, ...]

Interfaces with no triple line at all (closed surfaces).

lstsq_residuals NDArray[float64]

Concatenation of each component's squared physics residual (a length-1 array per component; the normalisation, met exactly, adds none). When fragmented is False, the single whole-mesh solve's.

fragmented bool

Whether the junction graph required per-component gauging.

n_components int

Number of gauged components (1 when not fragmented).

solver_notes dict[int, dict[str, object]]

Component index -> which least-squares solver ran on it and, for the sparse solver, its stop code, iteration count, residual norm and condition estimate (_solve_least_squares). Component 0 is the whole mesh when not fragmented. Empty for solutions not built by solve_gauged_least_squares, and for LogLami, which rebuilds its solution from the one this function returned.

docs.title: GaugeNotExactWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

A gauge could not be made exact: the solution is the well-scaled soft row's.

Raised only for a system whose physics rows are neither homogeneous (zero right-hand side) nor differences (each row sums to zero): no method of this package builds one.

docs.title: warn_on_junction_graph_fragmentation
docs.text:
warn_on_junction_graph_fragmentation(fragmented: bool, n_components: int, isolated: tuple[Interface, ...], stacklevel: int = 3) -> None

Emit JunctionGraphGaugeWarning when a mesh's junction-graph gauging was fragmented.

Called only from the entry points that drop the underlying gauge structure on the floor -- mirrors second_order_angle_reading.warn_on_partial_coverage's precedent: the report/solution-returning entry point (infer_tensions_by_junction_component) hands the caller the ComponentTensionSolution this warning would have described, and stays silent; infer_tensions_and_residuals (and, through it, infer_tensions) does not, so it calls this instead.

Takes the three scalars directly, rather than a JunctionGraphPartition, so a caller that already solved the system (and therefore already has a ComponentTensionSolution or YoungDupreLocalResult carrying these same three fields) does not need to recompute partition_from_mesh a second time just to decide whether to warn.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fragmented bool

Whether the junction graph required per-component gauging.

required n_components int

Number of gauged components (1 when not fragmented).

required isolated tuple[Interface, ...]

Interfaces with no triple line at all.

required stacklevel int

passed through to warnings.warn, so the warning points at the caller's own line rather than at this module. Defaults to 3.

3

docs.title: partition_by_junction_graph
docs.text:
partition_by_junction_graph(f: NDArray[int64], regions: NDArray[int64]) -> JunctionGraphPartition

Connected components of the triple-junction graph, from raw mesh arrays.

One node per interface (mesh_io.list_interfaces); an edge between two interfaces whenever they co-occur in a triple line (mesh_io.list_junctions gives each triple line's three constituent interfaces, all C(3,2) = 3 pairs among them become edges).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default f NDArray[int64]

Mesh triangles (vertex indices), shape (nf, 3).

required regions NDArray[int64]

Per-triangle region pair, shape (nf, 2).

required

Returns:

Name Type Description JunctionGraphPartition JunctionGraphPartition

The partition. A "healthy" mesh (every interface reachable from every other through some chain of shared triple lines, no closed interface) returns exactly one component holding every interface and an empty isolated.

Raises:

Type Description MalformedTripleLineError

If a triple line names an interface pair that is not present in mesh_io.list_interfaces(regions). mesh_io.list_junctions's admission rule (three interfaces on exactly three incident triangles) should make this unreachable in practice; this is the defensive, named replacement for what used to be a bare KeyError.

docs.title: partition_over_surviving_junctions
docs.text:
partition_over_surviving_junctions(f: NDArray[int64], regions: NDArray[int64], surviving: Collection[tuple[int, int, int]]) -> JunctionGraphPartition

:func:partition_by_junction_graph, restricted to the triple lines still carrying a row.

An estimator that declines some of its observations no longer couples the interfaces those observations coupled, so the gauge structure has to be read off the surviving junction lines rather than off the mesh. An interface left touching no surviving line is then isolated — exactly what this module already reports as float("nan") for a fully closed surface — and a survivor graph that falls into several pieces is gauged per component by :func:solve_gauged_least_squares, as a fragmented mesh already is.

surviving only ever removes lines: a triple that this mesh's own mesh_io.list_junctions does not admit as a genuine triple line is absent from the graph here exactly as it is absent from :func:partition_by_junction_graph's, so an estimator whose rows outrun that admission rule is treated identically with and without refusal.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default f NDArray[int64]

Mesh triangles (vertex indices), shape (nf, 3).

required regions NDArray[int64]

Per-triangle region pair, shape (nf, 2).

required surviving Collection[tuple[int, int, int]]

sorted region-triples whose row survived.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description JunctionGraphPartition JunctionGraphPartition

the partition of the same interfaces by the surviving lines alone. Passing every triple the mesh has reproduces :func:partition_by_junction_graph exactly.

docs.title: gauge_row_weight
docs.text:
gauge_row_weight(physics: NDArray[float64] | csr_matrix, n_unknowns: int) -> float

Weight of the gauge row: its norm is the median non-zero physics-row norm (to a power of two).

The row is weight * 1^T, norm weight * sqrt(n). Matching it to the physics rows' typical norm puts the system at the bottom of the condition number's V in the row weight (measured on a 1 866-cell tissue's Young-Dupre system: 311 against 2.8e7 for the unit row). 1.0 when no physics row has an entry.

docs.title: solve_with_exact_gauge
docs.text:
solve_with_exact_gauge(physics: NDArray[float64] | csr_matrix, physics_b: NDArray[float64], gauge_total: float, *, system: str = 'tension system', use_sparse: bool | None = None, scale_columns: bool = False) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.float64], dict[str, object]]

Least squares on physics @ x = physics_b with the gauge sum(x) = gauge_total met exactly.

The gauge row is appended with the weight gauge_row_weight (its norm equal to the median physics-row norm, where the system is best conditioned), the system is solved by _solve_least_squares (dense or sparse as the options say), and the gauge is then made exact without moving the solution off the physics rows' least-squares set:

  • homogeneous physics rows (physics_b == 0: every Young-Dupre-family, cotangent, Lami, per-edge and Equilibrium system): the solution of a soft gauge row of any weight is the exact-gauge solution times one factor (Sherman-Morrison; the two were measured to agree to 1e-13), so it is rescaled to sum(x) = gauge_total. Tension ratios are those of the exact constrained least-squares solution;
  • difference rows (each physics row sums to zero, e.g. LogLami in log space): adding a constant to every unknown leaves every physics residual unchanged, so the solution is shifted to meet the gauge;
  • otherwise (no builder of this package): the soft row's solution is returned with a GaugeNotExactWarning.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default physics NDArray[float64] | csr_matrix

(n_rows, n) physics rows, dense or CSR, without any gauge row.

required physics_b NDArray[float64]

(n_rows,) their right-hand side.

required gauge_total float

the value sum(x) must take (n * mean_tension for the tension methods).

required system str

label, for messages and diagnostics. Keyword-only.

'tension system' use_sparse bool | None

force a path, see _solve_least_squares. Keyword-only.

None scale_columns bool

see _solve_least_squares. Keyword-only.

False

Returns:

Name Type Description tuple NDArray[float64]

(x, residuals, record). residuals is the squared 2-norm of the physics rows'

NDArray[float64]

residual, physics @ x - physics_b, as a length-1 array: the gauge row is met exactly and

dict[str, object]

contributes nothing. record is _solve_least_squares's, plus gauge (how the gauge was

tuple[NDArray[float64], NDArray[float64], dict[str, object]]

made exact) and gauge_row_weight.

Nothing is raised beyond _solve_least_squares's exceptions; a zero-sum solution of homogeneous rows (no scale to rescale) is returned as solved, with a GaugeNotExactWarning.

docs.title: solve_gauged_least_squares
docs.text:
solve_gauged_least_squares(matrix_m: NDArray[float64] | csr_matrix, vector_b: NDArray[float64], keys: Sequence[Interface], mean_tension: float, partition: JunctionGraphPartition, *, system: str = 'tension system') -> ComponentTensionSolution

Solve matrix_m @ x = vector_b, gauging per junction-graph component if fragmented.

matrix_m must be exactly the shape every builder in foambryo.tension_inference produces: (n_rows, len(keys)), whose last row is the single global gauge sum(gamma) = vector_b[-1] (vector_b[-1] is len(keys) * mean_tension for every method except LogLami, which works in log-space -- this function reads vector_b[-1] directly rather than recomputing it, so it is agnostic to which convention the caller used). The row itself is not used: each component is solved by solve_with_exact_gauge, which meets its share of the gauge exactly (sum(gamma) over the component = vector_b[-1] * n_component / n, i.e. mean(gamma) = mean_tension). The residuals returned are the physics rows' (the gauge contributes none).

Each component's solve is dense or sparse as foambryo.linear_solves's options in force say (by default: dense below SPARSE_SOLVE_MIN_UNKNOWNS interfaces, lsqr at or above), see _solve_least_squares.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default matrix_m NDArray[float64] | csr_matrix

Assembled system, gauge row last. A sparse system is never densified as a whole: only the components that take the dense path are.

required vector_b NDArray[float64]

Right-hand side, gauge value last.

required keys Sequence[Interface]

Interface key per column of matrix_m, in order.

required mean_tension float

The gauge value the caller requested (only used for the human-readable gauge_notes; the actual constraint value is read from vector_b[-1]).

required partition JunctionGraphPartition

This mesh's junction-graph partition. Must cover exactly keys (checked).

required system str

what the system is, for messages and diagnostics. Keyword-only.

'tension system'

Returns:

Name Type Description ComponentTensionSolution ComponentTensionSolution

See its docstring.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If partition's interfaces do not exactly match keys, or (defensive, fragmented case only) if a physics row's nonzero columns span more than one component -- meaning the caller's row coupling does not match the triple-junction graph, and this decomposition must not be trusted for that builder.

docs.title: Linear solves and diagnostics
docs.text:
Solver choice and solve diagnostics for the inference's linear systems.

Every tension and pressure of this package is the solution of a linear least-squares system. Small systems are solved densely (scipy.linalg.lstsq), exactly; large ones sparsely (lsqr, or a sparse direct factorisation), because a dense system grows as the product of its dimensions in memory and as their cube in time: the Young-Dupre system of a 1 866-cell tissue is 49 984 x 11 746, 4.7 GB dense, and at 10 000 cells it would be some 120 GB.

This module holds what the public entry points (infer_tensions*, infer_pressures*, infer_forces) pass down to every solve:

  • solver: "auto" (the default) solves a system densely below sparse_threshold unknowns and sparsely at or above it; "dense" and "sparse" force one path whatever the size. Below the threshold, "auto" is bitwise the dense solve. Forcing "dense" on a system whose dense form would not fit in the memory available emits a DenseSolveMemoryWarning with the estimate, before anything is allocated. The tension methods Equilibrium, Variational and ForceBalance* have no sparse path: they are solved densely under "auto", and "sparse" raises ValueError for them. A sparse lsqr solve that does not converge falls back to the dense one with a SparseSolveFallbackWarning (or, when the dense one cannot fit in memory, returns lsqr's last iterate with that warning).
  • sparse_threshold: the number of unknowns at which "auto" switches (default foambryo.junction_graph.SPARSE_SOLVE_MIN_UNKNOWNS, 2 000). What counts as "unknowns" is the number of columns of the system the dense path would assemble: the interfaces of one junction-graph component for a tension solve, the materials for a Laplace pressure, the interfaces plus the cells for the variational pressure. One exception: the variational pressure of a cropped mesh is solved densely up to foambryo.pressure_inference.DENSE_CROP_PRESSURE_MAX_ENTRIES matrix entries under "auto", whatever sparse_threshold is.
  • diagnostics: False (the default: nothing is computed and each entry point returns its usual values), True (one SolveRecord per solve: solver, shape, rank, residual norm, condition number, time) or "spectrum" (also the extreme singular values of the large, sparse systems, by scipy.sparse.linalg.svds, at a measured extra cost). With diagnostics on, each entry point returns one more value, a SolveDiagnostics, last; save_solve_diagnostics writes it to a JSON file (the scalars) and an NPZ file (the singular values).

They are keyword-only on every entry point that takes them, and an invalid value raises ValueError (validate_solve_options). A lower-level function called directly (for example infer_tensions_young_dupre_local) uses the options in force, the defaults outside any entry point; solve_options puts others in force around such a call.

What the condition numbers are. On a dense least-squares solve, the 2-norm condition number s_max / s_min from the singular values scipy.linalg.lstsq computes anyway (free; inf when the smallest is zero). On an lsqr solve, lsqr's own running estimate of the Frobenius-norm condition number ||A||_F ||A^+||_F (free; an estimate, and an over-estimate of the 2-norm one by up to a factor n). On a sparse direct solve, the 1-norm condition number estimated from the factorisation (Hager-Higham, scipy.sparse.linalg.onenormest; cheap). The source is recorded beside every number: the three are not the same quantity.

How the options travel. A public entry point sets them in a context variable for the duration of its call, and the solve helpers read it, so the options reach every solve without threading an argument through each builder. The context is per thread and per asynchronous task (contextvars); outside any entry point the defaults apply.

extreme_singular_values(operator: spmatrix | sparray, *, symmetric_positive: bool = False) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64] | None, float, str | None]

The largest and smallest SPECTRUM_EXTREME_VALUES singular values of a sparse operator.

The largest by scipy.sparse.linalg.svds (ARPACK, which="LM"). The smallest first by svds with which="SM"; if ARPACK does not converge within SPECTRUM_MAX_ITERATIONS, by shift-invert at zero (eigsh(..., sigma=0), a sparse LU factorisation) of the operator itself when it is symmetric positive (symmetric_positive: its singular values are its eigenvalues) or of the normal matrix A^T A otherwise. The normal matrix squares the condition number, so those values are accurate only down to about 1e-8 of the largest; the note says which route gave them. Never raises on a failure: what is missing is said in the note.

docs.title: The mesh
docs.text:
The mesh every inference reads: DcelData, a multimaterial triangle mesh as a doubly connected edge list.

A DcelData holds the vertices, the triangles with the two materials each separates, and the half-edge structure the geometry (foambryo.geometry, foambryo.curvature) walks. Build one with foambryo.dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask, foambryo.dcel_mesh_from_file or foambryo.dcel_mesh_from_multimaterial_mesh.

Sacha Ichbiah, 2021. Matthieu Perez, 2024.

docs.text:
DcelData(points: NDArray[float64], triangles: NDArray[int64], labels: NDArray[int64], *, crop_faces: NDArray[bool_] | NDArray[integer] | None = None, source_spacing: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None)

A multimaterial triangle mesh as a doubly connected edge list (DCEL): faces, half-edges and vertices.

Conventions: label 0 is the exterior medium; every triangle's labels are stored as material_1 < material_2, its winding flipped to match (_normalize_label_order), so an interface is keyed (label_1, label_2) with label_1 < label_2; coordinates are in the mesh's own length unit (voxels, or the unit of the spacing the mesh was reconstructed with).

Attributes:

Name Type Description v NDArray[float64]

vertex positions, (nv, 3), unused vertices removed.

f NDArray[int64]

triangles and labels, (nf, 5) rows (v0, v1, v2, material_1, material_2), in the input's row order.

materials NDArray[int64]

the labels present, sorted (0 first when the medium is).

n_materials int

their number.

crop_faces NDArray[bool_]

(nf,), True on the crop faces (all False without).

source_spacing tuple[float, float, float] | None

the source mask's voxel size, if recorded.

vertices list[Vertex]

the DCEL's vertex records, aligned with v.

half_edges list[HalfEdge]

the DCEL's half-edge records.

faces list[Face]

the DCEL's face records, aligned with the rows of f.

Take a multimaterial mesh as input.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default points NDArray[float64]

Mesh vertex positions, shape (nv, 3).

required triangles NDArray[int64]

Triangles as vertex indices, shape (nf, 3).

required labels NDArray[int64]

The two materials each triangle separates, shape (nf, 2). A triangle's stored winding must put its right-hand-rule normal on the second label's side, i.e. point outward from the first — see _normalize_label_order for why, and for what goes wrong silently when a mesh from an outside source violates it.

required crop_faces NDArray | None

which triangles are crop faces: faces on the boundary of the imaged volume, where the tissue was cut by the crop rather than bounded by the medium. A boolean mask of shape (nf,) or the row indices of the crop faces, aligned with triangles. Keyword-only. Defaults to None, no crop face. A crop face keeps its labels (0, c); every inference method keeps it, and every junction edge and vertex that touches it, out of its equations, leaves the interfaces made only of crop faces out of its tension map, and reports the pressure of a cut cell as nan. See foambryo.crop_faces.

None source_spacing tuple[float, float, float] | None

the voxel size of the mask the mesh was made from, along the mask's axes 0, 1, 2, when the mesh records it: delaunay-watershed-3d's construct_mesh_in_physical_units writes it in the .rec file, dcel_mesh_from_file reads it, and dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask sets it when given a spacing. Keyword-only. Defaults to None, unknown. It changes nothing: the mesh is already in physical units, and no inference reads it. It is kept so that a mesh says which voxels it came from.

None

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If any triangle carries the same material on both sides, or if crop_faces is not a mask or a set of rows of triangles, or names a triangle that does not carry the medium label 0, or if source_spacing is not three positive finite numbers.

Move the graph to the mesh's scattered ("exploded") view, from its unexploded positions.

Each cell node, and the vertices of each interface with the medium, move by the displacement of their cell (mesh.clusters_displacements). Call it after mesh.compute_scattered_arrays(coeff). Every node then sits at its exploded cell's barycentre (up to rounding), and an interface with the medium moves with its cell; an interface between two cells does not move (its edge in the graph view is drawn between the two nodes).

The positions are computed from the graph's unexploded ones each time, into new arrays: they are recorded in graph.graph["unexploded_centroid"] and graph.graph["unexploded_verts"] at the first call, so that calling it again on the same graph (a new coefficient) does not add a second displacement, and the arrays the graph was built with (mesh.centroids itself for the nodes) are never modified.

docs.title: Per-edge Young-Dupré
docs.text:
Per-edge Young-Dupre tension inference: TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupreLocal.

TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre imposes the Young-Dupre balance once per triple line, on angles that have already been averaged along it (geometry.compute_angles_tri returns np.mean(...) per wedge key). Young-Dupre is a pointwise balance, so averaging first is valid only when the angle varies little along the line — and a review of the code during development measured per-line angle standard deviations of 0.7-14.1 degrees, so it does not. Averaging also destroys any route to per-edge residuals, robust weighting or uncertainty.

This module imposes the same balance once per geometric trijunctional edge:

.. math::

w_e \begin{pmatrix}
    1 & \cos\alpha^e_b & \cos\alpha^e_a \\
    \cos\alpha^e_b & 1 & \cos\alpha^e_c \\
    \cos\alpha^e_a & \cos\alpha^e_c & 1
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix} \gamma_{ab} \\ \gamma_{bc} \\ \gamma_{ac} \end{pmatrix} = 0

with a < b < c the three regions meeting on edge e, :math:\alpha^e_f the interior wedge angle in region f measured on that edge (see geometry._wedges_at_half_edge for this convention), and :math:w_e = \ell_e / L the edge's share of the mesh's total junction length. Summing the rows of one triple line reproduces the averaged builder's weight for that line exactly, so the two methods differ only in where the averaging happens: YoungDupre averages the angles and then takes the cosine; YoungDupreLocal takes the cosine per edge and lets least squares do the averaging. The difference is the Jensen gap of cos along the line, which is second order in the angle spread — so on a line whose angle is constant the two are identical, and they separate exactly where the angle varies along the line, i.e. where the mesh is noisy.

Row weighting is not a detail — it dominates the comparison, as measured. The naive choice :math:w_e = \ell_e / L (the literal per-edge formulation) does not keep a triple line's total influence fixed when its single row block is split into :math:n_e blocks: :math:n_e identical rows of weight :math:w are equivalent to one row of weight :math:w\sqrt{n_e}, so the naive choice silently reweights line k by :math:1/\sqrt{n_e} — it penalises well-resolved lines. On the benchmark's 42 equilibrium cases that reweighting alone costs two orders of magnitude, more than the per-edge idea itself is worth. Hence :class:PerEdgeWeighting:

  • LinePreserving (the default) sets :math:w_e = (\ell_k / L)\sqrt{\ell_e / \ell_k}, so :math:\sum_{e \in k} w_e^2 = (\ell_k / L)^2 — each line keeps exactly the total least-squares weight YoungDupre gives it, and the only remaining difference between the two methods is per-edge versus averaged angles. This is the variant that isolates the per-edge question; with the angles held fixed it reproduces YoungDupre to ~1e-14.
  • Edge sets :math:w_e = \ell_e / L, the literal per-edge formulation, kept so the measurement is reproducible.
  • Arclength sets :math:w_e = \sqrt{\ell_e / L}, which makes the objective a discretisation of :math:\int |r|^2\,\mathrm{d}\ell.

Read this outcome before using this. YoungDupreLocal was measured to be decisively worse than YoungDupre on the 42 equilibrium cases, for a reason that turns out to be structural: at a triple line in mechanical equilibrium the three wedge angles are fixed by the three (constant) tensions alone, so the true angle is constant along each line and every bit of measured along-line variation is error. Averaging the angles first is therefore a noise filter, while the pointwise form rectifies that noise into a systematic bias of order :math:\tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{Var}(\alpha) through the Jensen gap of cos. The method is kept — as an additional, non-default member — because its per-edge residual field is a genuinely more informative diagnostic than the per-junction one, and because a negative result that is reproducible is worth more than a deleted branch.

The normalisation is that of every junction-line method: the tensions are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension, exactly, in each connected piece of the junction graph (foambryo.junction_graph.solve_gauged_least_squares).

docs.title: PerEdgeWeighting
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

How each edge's row block is weighted. See the module docstring — this choice dominates.

  • LinePreserving: w_e = (l_k / L) * sqrt(l_e / l_k), so each triple line k keeps the total least-squares weight YoungDupre gives it. Default.
  • Edge: w_e = l_e / L, the literal per-edge formulation. Silently reweights line k by 1 / sqrt(n_e), i.e. penalises well-resolved lines.
  • Arclength: w_e = sqrt(l_e / L), making the objective a discretisation of the continuum integral |r|^2 dl.

The Young-Dupre residual of every trijunctional edge, as a renderable field.

The paper plots one residual per junction; this is one per edge, which is strictly more informative — it localises a bad junction to the part of the line that is bad. All arrays are aligned index-wise and ordered as geometry.compute_trijunction_edges.

Infer tensions with one Young-Dupre block per trijunctional edge.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

Mesh to analyze, in any length unit.

required mean_tension float

The normalisation: the tensions are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension, exactly, in each connected piece of the junction graph. Defaults to 1.

1.0 huber_delta float | None

Huber threshold, in units of the robust scale, for IRLS down-weighting of outlying edges. None (the default) disables robust weighting entirely, which is what TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupreLocal uses — the robust variant is an option, not the shipped behaviour. Pass DEFAULT_HUBER_DELTA for the classical 1.345.

None max_irls_iterations int

IRLS iteration cap. Defaults to 60 — convergence to irls_tolerance was measured at 45-50 iterations on the benchmark's meshes, and the answer at a 20-iteration cap already agrees with the converged one to ~1e-6.

60 weighting PerEdgeWeighting

row-weighting scheme. Defaults to LinePreserving, the only one that keeps each triple line's total influence equal to YoungDupre's — see the module docstring, this choice is worth two orders of magnitude.

LinePreserving irls_tolerance float

Stop IRLS when the max tension change falls below this. Defaults to 1e-10.

1e-10 angle_reading str

which trijunction angle convention to read, "chord" (the default, and bit-identical to the historical behaviour) or "oriented_chord". Keyword-only. See foambryo.second_order_angle_reading.

CHORD_READING refusal WedgeRefusal

which trijunctional edges this estimator declines to use, and how. Keyword-only; defaults to refusing nothing, which is bitwise the historical behaviour. This method's observation unit is a single edge, so ExcludeEdgeFromLineMean and DropLine are the same intervention here and agree exactly, while DownweightLine keeps the folded rows and scales their whole line. Refusing rows can leave an interface with no surviving line: it is then reported float("nan"), never a number. See foambryo.wedge_refusal.

NO_REFUSAL

The solve runs under the solver options in force (foambryo.linear_solves): called directly, dense below 2 000 interfaces per piece of the junction graph and lsqr at or above; foambryo.linear_solves.solve_options sets others around the call. On a cropped mesh every junction edge that touches a crop face is declined, whatever refusal is, and the crop interfaces are absent from the result.

Every interface is float("nan"), with an empty residual field, when the refusal leaves no row at all — an empty answer rather than an exception, so a caller can count how often a policy costs a whole mesh. docs.title: Pressures
docs.text:
Cell pressures inferred from a multimaterial mesh and its interface tensions.

The pressures are solved from the tensions (foambryo.tension_inference), by the variational method (the default) or by Laplace's law (PressureComputationMethod). They are in the unit of the tensions divided by the mesh's length unit: the tensions being relative (normalised to mean_tension), so are the pressures, which scale with the tensions. The exterior medium, label 0, has the pressure base_pressure; a cell whose pressure the mesh does not determine, or a cell the crop cuts, is nan, never a number.

Sacha Ichbiah 2021 Matthieu Perez 2024

docs.title: UndeterminedTensionError
docs.text:
UndeterminedTensionError(interfaces: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...])

Bases: ValueError

A pressure inference was handed an interface tension that is not a finite number.

Every pressure method solves for the cell pressures from the interface tensions, and the default variational method couples every cell to every tension, so a single non-finite tension makes nearly every inferred pressure non-finite: measured on five real embryo timepoints with one to four closed interfaces, all but one cell's pressure came back non-finite each time (54 of 55 cells up to 71 of 72). Such a field carries no usable value, so the pressure inference refuses it rather than returning it.

The usual cause is not a numerical failure. An interface with no triple line at all -- a closed surface, such as an engulfed cell or a sealed lumen, or a fragment that a segmentation left inside another cell -- has no angle from which its tension could be measured, and foambryo.infer_tensions reports it as float("nan") by design. The other tensions of such a mesh remain valid; use foambryo.infer_tensions_by_junction_component to see which interfaces are undetermined and which component each determined tension belongs to.

Subclasses ValueError, so code that already caught the generic error the least-squares solve raised on a non-finite input keeps working.

Attributes:

Name Type Description interfaces

the interfaces whose tension is not finite, sorted.

Build the error and its message from the offending interfaces.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default interfaces tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]

the interfaces whose tension is not finite.

required

docs.title: UndeterminedPressureWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Emitted when the Laplace pressure leaves cells undetermined; their pressure is nan.

Also emitted by the variational method on a cropped mesh, for a cell that the crop does not cut but whose every vertex lies on a crop face or on an interface without a tension.

The Laplace methods write one equation per interface, P_a - P_b = -2 H_ab T_ab, which needs the interface's mean curvature H_ab. The curvature is read at the vertices of the interface that are not on a junction line, so an interface all of whose vertices lie on junctions has no curvature (nan), and its equation is left out. When the equations that remain do not connect a cell to the exterior, through a chain of interfaces, nothing fixes that cell's pressure: it is reported as nan, never as a number. This is common on coarse meshes of small cells, where up to about a third of the interfaces can have no curvature and a few cells per hundred can be left undetermined.

The variational method (the default) does not use curvatures and is not affected.

docs.title: PressureComputationMethod
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

The pressure inference methods.

  • Variational (the default): the least-squares solution of the vertex force balance at the given tensions (see our article). It reads no curvature, gives a number for every cell of an uncropped mesh, and is the only method with a formulation for crop faces.
  • Laplace: Laplace's law, P_a - P_b = -2 H_ab T_ab, on each interface, with the interface's mean curvature H_ab averaged over its vertices off the junction lines.
  • WeightedLaplace: the same, with the curvature averaged with area weights.

The two Laplace methods need each interface's mean curvature. An interface with no measurable curvature contributes no equation, and a cell that the remaining equations do not connect to the exterior gets the pressure nan (see UndeterminedPressureWarning). They refuse a cropped mesh (ValueError); has_crop_face_formulation says which methods accept one.

docs.title: has_crop_face_formulation property
docs.text:
has_crop_face_formulation: bool

Whether the method infers pressures on a cropped mesh (one with crop faces, foambryo.crop_faces).

Only Variational does: the two Laplace methods read each interface's curvature, which on an interface the crop cuts is read partly on the crop, and infer_pressures refuses them on a cropped mesh. A front end can offer only the methods that have the formulation instead of failing after the tensions.

docs.title: infer_pressures
docs.text:
infer_pressures(mesh: DcelData, dict_tensions: dict[tuple[int, int], float], mode: PressureComputationMethod = PressureComputationMethod.Variational, base_pressure: float = 0, *, solver: str = 'auto', sparse_threshold: int | None = None, diagnostics: bool | str = False) -> dict[int, float] | tuple[dict[int, float], linear_solves.SolveDiagnostics]

Infer the pressure of every cell of a mesh from its interface tensions.

The pressures are in the unit of the tensions divided by the mesh's length unit, and scale with the tensions: tensions normalised to a mean of 1 give pressures relative to that scale.

Cropped meshes (foambryo.crop_faces, variational method only): the pressure of every cut cell is solved for and returned as nan, with a CutCellPressureWarning naming the cells; the force balances of the vertices on crop faces, and of the vertices of interfaces whose tension is nan, are left out, so nan tensions are accepted there; a cell those balances leave undetermined is nan too (UndeterminedPressureWarning). The crop interfaces need no entry in dict_tensions.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

Mesh to analyze, in any length unit.

required dict_tensions dict[tuple[int, int], float]

interface (label_1, label_2), label_1 < label_2, label 0 the exterior medium -> tension, one entry per interface of the mesh, as foambryo.infer_tensions returns it; all on one scale (tensions from separately normalised pieces of the junction graph are used as given). On an uncropped mesh every value must be finite; on a cropped mesh the crop interfaces may be absent and undetermined tensions nan.

required mode PressureComputationMethod

Computation method. Defaults to PressureComputationMethod.Variational.

Variational base_pressure float

Pressure of the exterior medium (label 0), returned as its pressure. Defaults to 0.

0 solver str

"auto" (the default), "dense" or "sparse": how the pressure system is solved (foambryo.linear_solves). "auto" is dense below sparse_threshold unknowns (materials for the Laplace methods, interfaces plus cells for the variational one) and sparse at or above, and bitwise the dense result below it. On a cropped mesh "auto" decides by DENSE_CROP_PRESSURE_MAX_ENTRIES instead. Keyword-only.

'auto' sparse_threshold int | None

unknowns at which "auto" goes sparse; None (the default) is foambryo.junction_graph.SPARSE_SOLVE_MIN_UNKNOWNS (2 000). Keyword-only.

None diagnostics bool | str

False (the default), True or "spectrum": also return a foambryo.linear_solves.SolveDiagnostics, last, with one record per solve. Keyword-only.

False

Returns:

Type Description dict[int, float] | tuple[dict[int, float], SolveDiagnostics]

dict[int, float]: map cell label (0 = exterior, at base_pressure) -> pressure. With a Laplace method, a cell whose pressure no equation fixes is nan (and UndeterminedPressureWarning is emitted); the variational method returns a number for every cell of an uncropped mesh. Raises:

Type Description UndeterminedTensionError

on an uncropped mesh, if any tension in dict_tensions is not a finite number -- for example the nan that infer_tensions reports for an interface with no triple line. if the variational system is singular.

docs.title: Reconstruction cost
docs.text:
The estimated wall time and peak memory of a reconstruction, before it runs.

A front end that reconstructs a mask (the napari plugin, foambryo view MASK) tells its user, before the run, how long it should take and how much memory it should need; on a large tissue it can be minutes and tens of GiB. This module is the one place the estimate is made, so every front end gives the same one.

The estimate is a power law of the voxels handed to delaunay-watershed-3d: the mask's voxels times the anisotropy, because an anisotropic mask is resampled to cubic voxels of its finest spacing before meshing (voxels_handed_to_dw3d). Its constants (RECONSTRUCTION_COST_FIT) were fitted by least squares in log-log to the median wall time and peak memory of delaunay-watershed-3d's default reconstruction (min_distance 3, junction relocation on) at seven anchors (RECONSTRUCTION_COST_ANCHORS): two medians over the benchmark's simulated tissues of 2 to 10 cells, and five reconstructions of single tissues of 90 to 1 866 cells, on one machine (Apple M3 Max, 16 cores, 128 GiB; timings mostly on a shared, loaded machine, so provisional; peak memory reliable).

Each estimate is a central value and a band: the band factor is the largest in-sample ratio between an anchor and the fit, not a validated prediction interval. Time and memory also depend on the number of cells and on the tissue's shape, which the estimate does not see.

docs.title: Result files
docs.text:
The result files of the foambryo command, for every front end that writes or reads them.

foambryo infer and foambryo infer-over-seeds write CSV tables and a JSON run record, run.json (schema 1); the napari plugin writes the same files. Both use this module, so a table written by either reads back as the library's 64-bit numbers, and a run record has the same keys:

  • the tables: write_tension_table / read_tension_table, write_pressure_table / read_pressure_table, the seed ensemble's write_ensemble_tension_table and write_per_seed_tension_table and their readers, the solve diagnostics' write_solve_table / read_solve_table (solves.csv, one row per linear solve) and write_spectra (spectra.npz), and format_float, the shortest decimal string that reads back as the same float. The file names are TENSION_TABLE, PRESSURE_TABLE, SOLVE_TABLE, SPECTRA, RUN_RECORD, ...; the readers and writers take a pathlib.Path;
  • the run record: infer_run_record and ensemble_run_record build it, write_run_record writes it, read_run_record reads it; RUN_RECORD_SCHEMA is its schema number;
  • what a run record names: the methods by their command-line spellings (option_name, TENSION_METHODS, PRESSURE_METHODS, DIAGNOSTICS), the versions (library_versions), and the warnings raised, each once with its count (WarningCollector).

The tables and the record's writers are implemented in foambryo._result_tables; this module is their public interface. Changing a column, or a run-record key's name or meaning, makes a new schema.

docs.title: WarningCollector
docs.text:
WarningCollector()

Catch the warnings raised inside a block, and count each distinct one.

Use it as a context manager (with WarningCollector() as collector: ...). DeprecationWarning, PendingDeprecationWarning, ImportWarning and ResourceWarning are ignored inside the block (neither shown nor counted); every other warning is caught, wherever it is raised, rather than once per code location, so a count is the number of times it was raised. Caught warnings are not shown. After the block, summary holds one entry per distinct warning (same category and message), {"category": ..., "message": ..., "count": ...} with the category's class name, in the order they were first raised: a run record's warnings.

Start with an empty summary.
