docs.title: Angle readings
docs.text:
The trijunction angle readings: the chord, the second-order (quadric) reading, and their oriented forms.

The angle_reading (or reading) selector of every angle-reading function takes one of ANGLE_READINGS: "chord" (the default), "quadric", "oriented_chord" and "oriented_quadric". Angles are in radians in every returned map.

docs.title: Why this module exists
docs.text:
foambryo.geometry._wedges_at_half_edge reads a trijunction wedge angle as arccos(n_i . n_j) between two incident triangles' face normals. Both normals are perpendicular to the shared junction edge, so both lie in the plane normal to it, and the angle between them equals the angle between the two triangles' in-plane traces — the straight lines from the junction out towards each incident triangle's apex. Production therefore reads a chord of each interface where the geometry has a tangent.

A flat P1 facet has no curvature to offer, so it cannot report a tangent; a circular arc's chord is rotated from its tangent by exactly kappa * L / 2, with L the in-plane distance from the junction-edge midpoint to the incident apex. This chord-for-tangent substitution was measured to account for 68.4 % of the length-weighted flattening slope of the reconstructed meshes.

This module supplies the second reading: fit a generic quadric height field to the interface's own mesh vertices in a 3-D window around each junction-edge midpoint, read that surface's normal-plane section curvature kappa analytically, and rotate the face normal about the junction edge by -kappa * L / 2. It is a local patch fit, keyed to foambryo's own trijunction identification.

docs.title: The oriented wedge reading
docs.text:
arccos returns [0, pi], so a wedge whose interior angle exceeds 180 degrees — a reflex wedge — is reported as 360 - theta. The three wedges of one junction edge then sum to 360 - 2 (theta - 180) instead of 360, and every average along the line inherits the deficit. This is not rare on a coarse reconstruction: measured on the benchmark meshes, 2 % to 25 % of trijunctional edges carry one, at a rate that differs by a factor of six between reconstruction strategies, so a comparison of two meshes through the unoriented reading compares two different amounts of clipping as if they were geometry.

ORIENTED_CHORD_READING and ORIENTED_QUADRIC_READING return the oriented wedge angle in [0, 360): the arc from film e|f to film f|g measured through region f. The magnitude is still arccos of the same dot product, evaluated by the same expression; the oriented sine dot(t, cross(n_first, n_second)) is used only to choose between theta and 360 - theta. So the oriented readings are bitwise identical to their unoriented counterparts on every wedge that is not reflex, and the three wedges of an edge sum to 360 degrees.

The axis t runs from the lower to the higher vertex key, as everywhere else in this module. Its sign is then resolved from the geometry, not asserted: three positive angles summing to 360 contain at most one greater than 180, so under the reversed axis the three oriented wedges sum to 720 rather than 360, and the reader takes whichever assignment sums to 360. A wedge whose oriented sine is exactly zero — an interior angle of exactly 0 or exactly 180 degrees — reads as non-reflex under either axis, which reproduces the unoriented reader there.

docs.title: Which inference methods this changes, and one that it breaks
docs.text:
MEASURED on the benchmark meshes. A method's exposure follows from the trigonometric function its rows use, because the reflection theta -> 360 - theta leaves cos unchanged and flips the sign of sin:

  • YoungDupreLocal builds every row from cos of a per-edge wedge, so it is exactly invariant -- its gauge-matched relative error moved by at most 1.6e-14 over 1035 reconstructed benchmark meshes. It could never see the defect and cannot benefit from it either; a reflex wedge and its reflection are the same row to it.
  • YoungDupre averages the wedge along the line and then takes cos of the mean, so the reflection does move it: up to 0.24 in absolute relative error, worse on 35 of the 46 reconstruction-variant cohorts measured and better on the rest.
  • ProjectionYoungDupre, Lami and InvLami use sin, which changes sign. Their error rises by 5-42 %. That is not a defect of the reading: three tensions whose wedge is reflex admit no planar equilibrium at all, and the negative sine is that fact surfacing where the unoriented reading manufactured a plausible positive number instead.
  • LogLami fails outright on a mesh with a reflex wedge: its rows take log(sin(theta)), which is nan for a negative sine, and the solve then raises. Measured on 115 of 360 benchmark meshes. Pair LogLami with an unoriented reading, or repair the reflex edges upstream.

The quadric window needs no reflex guard. It is defined per incident face, transverse to the junction along that face's own chord, and never refers to a wedge angle at all; a reflex wedge is a relation between two faces, so it cannot enter one face's window. What the quadric reading does do is rotate normals about the junction edge, which moves some wedges across 180 degrees in either direction, so its reflex count differs from the chord reading's on the same mesh. That is a property of the corrected geometry, not a defect of the window.

docs.title: The two junction-edge endpoints
docs.text:
The fit keeps a sample when it is inside the window and on the interface's own side of the junction, eta > 0. Two of the candidate samples are the junction edge's own two endpoints, and in exact arithmetic their eta is exactly zero — they sit on the eta = 0 axis of the frame by construction, being the two vertices whose midpoint is the frame's origin. A strict eta > 0.0 therefore resolves them on the sign of a rounding error, and the sign of a rounding error depends on the units the mesh is expressed in.

MEASURED, on the benchmark's reference meshes: rescaling one mesh by 117x — the ratio between the normalised frame those meshes are stored in and the voxel frame their reconstructions live in — changed the kept-sample count on 652 of 1 065 incident faces, changed the admission outcome on 19, and moved line-mean wedge angles by up to 0.14 degrees. The chord reading moves by 2.5e-13 degrees under the same rescaling. That is about eleven orders of magnitude of difference between two readings of one mesh, and it is why the same reference meshes have been published at 2.032 and at 2.046 degrees of contact-angle error under one name: the frame a mesh is in was part of that reading's construction and was never stated with it.

An angle between two surfaces cannot depend on the units the surfaces are measured in, so this is a correctness defect independently of any angle metric. JUNCTION_ENDPOINTS decides those two samples by vertex identity instead. They are included: they are exact, noise-free samples of the interface at the very point the frame is anchored, they constrain the along-edge coefficients that nothing else near eta = 0 constrains, and including them is a statement rather than an accident. "exclude" and the historical "rounding" remain reachable through quadric_angle_rotations so that the repair can be measured; neither is reachable through any reading selector or any inference entry point.

MEASURED after the repair, on the same reference mesh: rescaling by 10, 117 and 1000 moves the line-mean wedge angles by at most 2.3e-13 degrees, against the chord reading's own 2.5e-13. The two readings are now equally invariant, to rounding. On a smooth surface whose contact angles are a closed form the repair moves the reading itself by at most 0.016 degrees and by about 0.001 degrees at typical spacings — so it is a repair whose value is the invariance, not an accuracy gain, and saying so is part of the repair.

docs.title: The constant term, and the false reason it used to be omitted
docs.text:
The height field is fitted without a constant term. The reason recorded here used to be that "the junction-edge midpoint is the midpoint of two mesh vertices lying on this interface, so the interface passes through the origin by construction". That reason is false whenever the junction line is curved, which on any real mesh it is: the midpoint of two vertices lies on the junction edge's chord, and the line leaves that chord by about kappa_line * L^2 / 8, as does the interface bounded by it. The frame's origin is a point the surface does not contain.

The real reason, MEASURED rather than argued, on a smooth surface whose contact angles are a closed form and whose triangulation was varied over fourteen edge lengths spanning a factor of seventeen:

  • fitting the constant term makes the reading better at every fine triangulation — up to 43 % lower line-mean error at the finest, and better at ten of the fourteen edge lengths tried;
  • and worse at the four coarsest, by up to 7.4 degrees, because at those spacings the extra free parameter is estimated from a window holding barely twice as many samples as the fit has parameters, and the variance it adds exceeds the bias it removes;
  • the coarse spacings the software is actually run at may or may not be on the worsening side: that depends on how curved real interfaces are relative to their triangulation, which is not a number this project has measured.

So the term stays off — not because the surface passes through the origin, which it does not, but because switching it on is an improvement at fine triangulations bought with a degradation at coarse ones, and the operating point is not known well enough to take that trade. fit_constant_term=True turns it on for measurement. Turning it on also raises the minimum admissible sample count from 10 to 12, which lowers coverage on meshes whose windows are thinly populated. It does not change _section_curvature, because translating a plane curve does not change its curvature.

What would settle it: the same fourteen-rung measurement with the analytic films' curvature matched to real interfaces', or the equivalent measurement on reconstructions with a ground-truth angle. Either would say which side of the crossover the shipped spacings are on.

docs.title: Units and conventions
docs.text:
• Coordinates are in the mesh's own units: voxel indices on dw3d output reconstructed without a spacing, the spacing's unit with one. kappa is per mesh length unit and kappa * L / 2 is dimensionless (an angle in radians); the reading does not depend on the unit (see "The two junction-edge endpoints").
  • kappa is the signed in-plane curvature of the interface's normal-plane section at the junction, positive when the section turns counter-clockwise about the junction-edge direction (lower vertex key -> higher vertex key) as it leaves the junction.
  • The junction-edge axis runs from the lower to the higher vertex key. Using a half-edge's own direction instead would flip the sign of the correction on half the half-edges.

docs.title: Which correction form is applied, and which is not
docs.text: Only the closed form -kappa * L / 2 is applied. It was measured that the alternative — rotating the mesh's chord onto the fitted patch's own tangent — injects a zero-mean scatter of about 3.3 degrees at the median and 14.4 degrees at p90 on this patch fit, because a patch fit's absolute orientation carries the discrepancy between the fitted surface and the mesh's local orientation, which is not a chord-versus-tangent error and must not be rotated away. That form is not implemented here. The cost of the form that is implemented is that the circular-arc model becomes load-bearing: -kappa * L / 2 is exact for an arc and first-order in kappa * L otherwise.

docs.title: What enters the fit, exhaustively
docs.text:
The fit is generic: a quadric height field is the second-order Taylor statement about whatever surface is there, and injects only smoothness. No constant-mean-curvature constraint, no Laplace or Neumann relaxation, no tension, no pressure, no area, no volume, no ground-truth angle, no reference mesh, no .rec file, no segmentation mask. The complete list of inputs is:

  1. mesh.v, the mesh's vertex coordinates;
  2. mesh.f, its triangles and their two material labels;

and nothing else. quadric_angle_rotations takes a DcelData and, besides the window's measurement parameters, no other argument, so "no ground truth in the estimator" is structural here: there is no parameter through which a reference mesh, a ground-truth angle, a tension or a pressure could reach it.

docs.title: Identity at zero curvature
docs.text:
A fitted kappa of exactly 0.0 produces a rotation of exactly -0.0, and geometry._wedges_at_half_edge skips the Rodrigues call on a falsy angle, so the chord angle is returned bitwise. Pinned by tests/test_second_order_angle_reading.py, which also checks the stronger statement that an explicitly all-zero rotation map, and an empty one, are the identity to the bit.

The honest qualification, MEASURED rather than asserted: a geometrically flat interface does not fit to an exactly-zero c_ee, because the least-squares design matrix is not exactly rank-consistent in binary floating point. On a planar three-film phantom the residual rotation peaks at 4.1e-17 rad (2.3e-15 degrees) and moves a reported wedge angle by at most 2.8e-14 degrees — sixteen orders of magnitude below the ~5 degree per-line errors this reading exists to reduce, and below float64's own resolution at 120 degrees. So the bitwise statement is about kappa == 0, and the practical statement about a flat surface is "identity to 1e-14 degrees".

docs.title: Hyperparameters are fixed in production, and measurable outside it
docs.text:
QUADRIC_WINDOW_FACTOR = 4.0 and QUADRIC_AXIAL_FACTOR = 1.0 are fixed a priori (the axial one is the isotropic choice, which assumes least). Re-selecting them by held-out fit residual, with at least 85 % of incident faces covered, returns exactly these values, so they carry no selection freedom with respect to the metrics they are judged on.

They remain module constants, and no production path can change them: no reading selector, no inference entry point, no public convenience function and not rotations_for_reading takes a window. quadric_angle_rotations alone accepts them, keyword-only, defaulting to these constants, so that the cost of the window can be measured without a second implementation of the fit living outside this module — two implementations of one fit diverge, and this project has been bitten by that. Called at the defaults it is bitwise what it was before the parameters existed, which tests/test_second_order_angle_reading.py executes rather than asserts.

The prohibition that motivated keeping them constants is unchanged and is about selection, not about reachability: a window must never be chosen on the contact-angle flattening slope, the tension contrast or the per-line angle error of a mesh whose accuracy is being judged. A window may be chosen only on meshes that are not on trial — which is what makes measuring it admissible at all.

docs.title: Coverage, and why the fallback is reported rather than hidden
docs.text: The fit is not admissible everywhere: an incident face whose window holds fewer than two mesh vertices per fit parameter, or whose design matrix is rank-deficient, gets no rotation and falls back to the chord reading. Measured on dw3d's 47-case benchmark at min_distance = 3, coverage is 0.919 of incident faces; at min_distance = 4 it is 0.890. A result that mixes corrected and uncorrected angles without saying so would be unreadable as science, so quadric_angle_rotations returns an AngleReadingReport naming the coverage and every trijunction line that is not fully corrected, and the report-less convenience paths in foambryo.geometry and foambryo.tension_inference emit an AngleReadingCoverageWarning instead of staying silent.

docs.title: Measured behaviour
docs.text: The measured behaviour of the reading is in BENCHMARKS.md (foambryo repository).

docs.title: AngleReadingCoverageWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Emitted when a quadric reading corrects only part of a mesh's trijunction faces.

Applies to "quadric" and "oriented_quadric"; the chord readings always cover every face.

The uncorrected faces silently fall back to the chord reading, which mixes two angle conventions in one result. That is admissible — it is strictly better than dropping the lines — but it must never be invisible. Use the *_with_report entry points in foambryo.geometry and foambryo.tension_inference to receive the numbers instead of the warning.

docs.title: AngleReadingReport dataclass
docs.text:
AngleReadingReport(reading: str, n_incident_faces: int, n_corrected: int, n_no_samples: int, n_no_fit: int, coverage_fraction: float | None, uncorrected_lines: tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...], line_coverage: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, int]] = dict(), window_factor: float = QUADRIC_WINDOW_FACTOR, axial_factor: float = QUADRIC_AXIAL_FACTOR, junction_endpoints: str = JUNCTION_ENDPOINTS, fit_constant_term: bool = FIT_CONSTANT_TERM)

What a trijunction angle reading covered, and what it fell back on.

Attributes:

Name Type Description reading str

one of ANGLE_READINGS. Either chord reading always reports full coverage: it has no fit to fail, and it does not walk the junctions a second time, so its per-face counts are 0 and carry no information — only coverage_fraction, uncorrected_lines and is_complete are meaningful on a chord report.

n_incident_faces int

(trijunctional geometric edge, incident face) pairs visited. Three per trijunctional edge; quadrijunctional edges are skipped, exactly as foambryo.geometry.compute_angles_tri skips them.

n_corrected int

pairs that received a second-order correction.

n_no_samples int

pairs whose window held too few interface vertices to fit.

n_no_fit int

pairs whose design matrix was rank-deficient or whose curvature was not finite.

coverage_fraction float | None

n_corrected / n_incident_faces, or None on a mesh with no trijunctional edge at all.

uncorrected_lines tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]

every trijunction line — identified by its sorted material triple, the same three materials whose wedge keys compute_angles_tri returns — carrying at least one uncorrected face. Sorted.

line_coverage dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, int]]

material triple -> (corrected faces, total faces) for every trijunction line in the mesh.

window_factor float

the transverse window multiplier actually used.

axial_factor float

the axial window multiplier actually used.

junction_endpoints str

the policy actually used for the frame's own two junction-edge endpoints, one of JUNCTION_ENDPOINT_POLICIES.

fit_constant_term bool

whether the quadric height field actually fitted a constant term.

A trijunction line with partial coverage (some but not all of its faces corrected) is not, by itself, a known source of extra angle error: measured against the chord reading's own error on the same lines, the per-line displacement this correction makes does not trend with how much of the line was covered (a near-zero, statistically insignificant slope, most of what little apparent trend there is already present in the chord reading, which has no coverage concept at all). A low line_coverage_fraction is a coverage fact about the mesh, not a warning sign about the correction's accuracy.

docs.title: is_complete property
docs.text:
is_complete: bool

True when every trijunctional incident face was read with the selected reading.

docs.title: line_coverage_fraction property
docs.text:
line_coverage_fraction: float | None

Fraction of trijunction lines every one of whose faces was corrected.

The line analogue of coverage_fraction, which is per-face: a line with 2 of its 3 faces corrected counts as 0 here (it is in uncorrected_lines) but contributes 2/3 to coverage_fraction. None on a mesh with no trijunctional edge at all, mirroring coverage_fraction's own convention.

docs.title: describe
docs.text:
describe() -> str

A one-line human-readable summary, used as the coverage warning's message.

Leads with the two numbers a reader needs to judge the result: the measured face coverage fraction and how many trijunction lines were not fully corrected (out of how many), then lists those lines (at most _MAX_LINES_IN_WARNING of them).

docs.title: orthonormal_basis
docs.text:
orthonormal_basis(normal: NDArray[float64]) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.float64]]

A right-handed in-plane basis (e1, e2) with cross(e1, e2) = normal.

e1 is built from the world axis least aligned with normal, which is deterministic and never degenerate. Handedness matters: it fixes the sign of every curvature this module returns, and it is the reason rodrigues_about and the in-plane angles agree (cross(axis, e1) = e2 for this basis).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default normal NDArray[float64]

the plane's normal, any non-zero length.

required

Returns:

Type Description tuple[NDArray[float64], NDArray[float64]]

tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.float64]]: the unit vectors (e1, e2).

docs.title: rodrigues_about
docs.text:
rodrigues_about(axis: NDArray[float64], vector: NDArray[float64], angle: float) -> NDArray[np.float64]

Rotate vector about the unit axis by angle, counter-clockwise seen from +axis.

For a vector already perpendicular to the axis — which every face normal at a junction edge is — this reduces to v cos a + (axis x v) sin a, and it agrees with a counter-clockwise rotation in the (e1, e2) basis orthonormal_basis returns, because cross(axis, e1) = e2 for that right-handed basis.

The rotation is linear, so it acts identically on n and on -n: applying it before _wedges_at_half_edge's relabelling flip and applying it after are the same operation, and the sign the mesh happens to carry on a face normal does not enter.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default axis NDArray[float64]

unit rotation axis.

required vector NDArray[float64]

the vector to rotate.

required angle float

rotation angle in radians.

required

Returns:

Type Description NDArray[float64]

NDArray[np.float64]: the rotated vector.

docs.title: junction_frames
docs.text:
junction_frames(mesh: DcelData) -> list[dict]

One local frame per (trijunctional geometric edge, incident face), from the DCEL.

This walk is production's own trijunction identification, not a second one. A geometric edge is visited when at least one of its half-edges has more than one twin (the test compute_angles_tri and compute_trijunction_edges use), it is de-duplicated by its (min, max) vertex-key pair keeping the lowest incident half-edge, and its three incident faces are collected in exactly the order geometry._wedges_at_half_edge collects them — the half-edge's own face first, then its twins'. An edge with any number of incident faces other than three is a quadrijunction (or higher) and is skipped, exactly as production skips it. Keying the frames this way is what makes every corrected angle attributable to the same (trijunction, material) key the chord reading produces.

The frame at one edge:

  • axis runs from the lower to the higher vertex key, normalised;
  • midpoint is the edge midpoint, which is where production's chord is anchored;
  • (e1, e2) is orthonormal_basis(axis), whose handedness fixes every curvature sign;
  • chord is the in-plane unit vector from midpoint towards the incident face's apex — production's own reading direction — and lever is the in-plane distance to that apex.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

the mesh to walk.

required

Returns:

Type Description list[dict]

list[dict]: one entry per (edge, face) with keys edge, face, axis, midpoint, e1, e2, lever, chord, edge_length, pair (the face's sorted material pair) and materials (the edge's sorted material triple). Faces whose apex lies on the junction axis (lever == 0) are dropped: they have no chord to correct.

docs.title: quadric_angle_rotations
docs.text:
quadric_angle_rotations(mesh: DcelData, *, window_factor: float = QUADRIC_WINDOW_FACTOR, axial_factor: float = QUADRIC_AXIAL_FACTOR, junction_endpoints: str = JUNCTION_ENDPOINTS, fit_constant_term: bool = FIT_CONSTANT_TERM) -> tuple[dict[tuple[tuple[int, int], int], float], AngleReadingReport]

Per-(edge, face) normal rotations that turn the chord reading into the quadric one.

For each (trijunctional geometric edge, incident face) this fits a generic quadric height field to the incident interface's own mesh vertices inside an anisotropic window around the junction-edge midpoint, reads the normal-plane section's signed curvature kappa off the fitted surface, and returns the rotation -kappa * lever / 2 to apply to that face's normal about the junction-edge axis. That is the exact chord-to-tangent rotation for a circular arc of curvature kappa whose chord has in-plane length lever.

The window is window_factor * lever transversely and axial_factor times that along the junction edge. A sample is kept when |xi| <= axial window and hypot(eta, zeta) <= window, and then when eta > 0 — which keeps the fit on the side of the junction where the interface actually lies, since an interface is bounded by its junction line — except for the frame's own two junction-edge endpoints, whose membership junction_endpoints decides explicitly. See "The two junction-edge endpoints" in this module's docstring for why that exception is a correctness fix and not a tuning knob.

Failure modes, all of which fall back to the chord reading for that face and are counted in the returned report: fewer than _SAMPLES_PER_PARAMETER * 5 interface vertices in the window, a rank-deficient design matrix, or a non-finite curvature.

Determinism: the walk, the k-d trees and the least-squares solve are all deterministic functions of mesh.v, mesh.f and the four keyword arguments; there is no random seed anywhere in this module.

The two window factors are measurement affordances, not tuning knobs, and no production path can reach them. They default to the module constants, rotations_for_reading does not forward them, and no reading selector, inference entry point or public convenience function exposes them; a caller who wants a different window has to name this function and say so. They exist because measuring what the window costs otherwise requires re-implementing the fit outside this module, and two implementations of one fit diverge. Called at the defaults the function is bitwise what it was before the parameters existed — the same float in every entry of the same map — and tests/test_second_order_angle_reading.py executes that identity rather than asserting it. Choosing a window on any quantity an arm is judged by would be the tuning this module's own docstring prohibits; a window may be chosen only on meshes that are not being judged.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

the mesh to read, in any length unit. The only mesh-derived argument: see "What enters the fit" in the module docstring. No reference mesh, target angle, tension or pressure can reach this function.

required window_factor float

transverse window, as a multiple of the incident face's own in-plane lever. Keyword-only. Defaults to QUADRIC_WINDOW_FACTOR, and production never passes anything else.

QUADRIC_WINDOW_FACTOR axial_factor float

extent along the junction edge, as a multiple of the transverse window. Keyword-only. Defaults to QUADRIC_AXIAL_FACTOR.

QUADRIC_AXIAL_FACTOR junction_endpoints str

one of JUNCTION_ENDPOINT_POLICIES. Keyword-only. Defaults to JUNCTION_ENDPOINTS, which is "include". "rounding" reproduces the historical behaviour, in which these two samples' membership was decided by the sign of a rounding error; it exists so that the repair can be measured, not so that it can be chosen.

JUNCTION_ENDPOINTS fit_constant_term bool

fit the quadric's constant term. Keyword-only. Defaults to FIT_CONSTANT_TERM. False reproduces the historical five-parameter fit, including its lower minimum sample count, exactly.

docs.title: rotations_for_reading
docs.text:
rotations_for_reading(mesh: DcelData, reading: str) -> tuple[dict[tuple[tuple[int, int], int], float] | None, AngleReadingReport]

Dispatch on the reading selector, with a per-mesh cache for the quadric fit.

The quadric fit costs one k-d tree query and one 5-parameter least-squares solve per incident trijunction face — measured at roughly 0.5 s on a 47-case benchmark mesh, which is the same order as one inference. Every angle-reading tension method calls compute_angles_tri once, so a benchmark that runs eight methods over one mesh would pay for the fit eight times. The result is cached on the mesh instance under _angle_reading_rotations.

Cache validity. DcelData never mutates v or f after __init__, so the cache cannot go stale through any public method of this package. If you mutate those arrays yourself, del mesh._angle_reading_rotations first.

The cache is shared by "quadric" and "oriented_quadric": the rotations depend only on the mesh, and whether a wedge is then reported oriented is decided downstream, in foambryo.geometry. Only the returned report's reading label differs.

This function does not forward a window. It calls quadric_angle_rotations with no window arguments, so every reading reachable through a reading selector uses QUADRIC_WINDOW_FACTOR and QUADRIC_AXIAL_FACTOR. A measurement that wants another window calls quadric_angle_rotations itself; it may then seed this function's cache by assigning the pair to mesh._angle_reading_rotations, and the report it stores names the window it used, so a result read that way says so rather than looking like production's.

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

the mesh to read.

required reading str

one of ANGLE_READINGS.

required

Returns:

Type Description tuple[dict[tuple[tuple[int, int], int], float] | None, AngleReadingReport]

tuple[dict | None, AngleReadingReport]: the rotation map (None for either chord reading, which applies no rotation at all) and the coverage report.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

if reading is not one of ANGLE_READINGS.

docs.title: Seed ensembles
docs.text:
Tensions from several reconstructions of one mask: seed ensembles.

delaunay-watershed-3d places its tessellation points with a small random dither, fixed by a seed (42 by default). Two seeds give two slightly different meshes of the same mask, and the tensions inferred from them differ. How much depends on cell size: measured with the default reconstruction (min_distance 3, junction relocation on) and YoungDupre with the chord reading, a tension varies from seed to seed by

  • about 5 % (median coefficient of variation) on the 42 equilibrium cases of the benchmarking dataset, whose cells are about ten times larger in volume than real ones;
  • about 13-14 % on synthetic tissues voxelised at a real cell size (median cell 69 370 voxels, radius ~25) and on embryo frames;
  • about 21 % on a 110-cell and on a 1 866-cell tissue meshed on their native anisotropic grid.

Averaging the tensions of several seeds removes part of that variation. Against ground truth, an ensemble of 8 seeds lowers the median relative tension error (gauge-matched, median over interfaces, then over tissues) from 0.152 to 0.123 on 12 synthetic tissues at real cell size (-23 % per tissue, lower on all 12), and from 0.077 to 0.064 on the benchmark (-9 %, lower on 35 of 42 cases), where most of the error is bias rather than seed noise. The contact-angle error falls by about 2 degrees at real cell size.

What this module offers. :func:infer_tensions_over_seeds reconstructs a mask at a fixed list of seeds (0 to 7 by default), infers the tensions of each mesh, and combines them:

  • combine="tensions" (the default): the mean, per interface, of the seeds' tensions. Each seed's solve meets the normalisation (a mean tension of 1) exactly, so the means share one scale.
  • combine="angles" (experimental, YoungDupre only): the mean, per junction line, of the seeds' line-averaged contact angles and line weights, then one YoungDupre solve. With angle_reading="quadric" it was the most accurate ensemble measured on synthetic tissues with known tensions, voxelised at the cell size of real embryos (median tension error 45 % below the default ensemble's on 46 tissues), but its margin over averaging quadric-read tensions is small and inconsistent, and with the chord reading it is inconsistent on the larger tissues. On synthetic masks degraded by a smooth random warp of about one voxel, combine="angles" with the quadric reading lost its advantage over the default on larger tissues of 90 and 165 cells while keeping it on small aggregates. It is not the default; it warns with :class:SeedEnsembleExperimentalWarning. Use it as a comparison, not as a replacement.

The seed list is fixed by the caller and never chosen on a result. Choosing the seed that gives the "best-looking" tensions would tune on the quantity being measured. The default list is 0 to 7. Seed 42, the default of every single-seed function, is not in it, so an ensemble never silently includes the default mesh. seeds=[42] reproduces :func:foambryo.infer_tensions on :func:foambryo.dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask's mesh, bit for bit.

The seed spread is a lower bound on the error, not an error bar. tension_seed_sd is the standard deviation over the seeds. It sees the part of the error that changes with the seed, never the bias every seed shares. Against ground truth at real cell size, a single seed's ±1 SD interval contained the true tension for about half of the interfaces (nominal 68 %), and on the benchmark for about a third.

Interfaces found by only some seeds. A seed can create an interface that another seed does not (two cells that barely touch, or do not touch at all). At real cell size about a fifth of the interfaces are found by only some of 16 seeds. On synthetic tissues with known geometry, most of those found by fewer than half of the seeds do not exist in the true tissue. They are kept in the result with the flag found_by_fewer_than_half_the_seeds; read their tensions with that in mind.

Cost. One reconstruction per seed, so N times the single-seed cost. Measured per seed:

tissue time peak memory benchmark case ~3 s ~1.5 GiB 165-cell tissue at real cell size ~40-65 s ~8 GiB (up to 11) 1 866-cell tissue ~11 min ~30-35 GiB

max_workers runs seeds in parallel processes. Each holds one reconstruction in memory, so choose it from the memory, not only from the number of cores.

docs.title: infer_tensions_over_seeds
docs.text:
infer_tensions_over_seeds(mask: ndarray, seeds: Iterable[int] = DEFAULT_ENSEMBLE_SEEDS, *, min_distance: int = 3, mode: TensionComputationMethod = TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre, angle_reading: str = CHORD_READING, combine: str = COMBINE_TENSIONS, max_workers: int = 1, spacing: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None, progress: Callable[[int, int, int], None] | None = None, **reconstruction_options: object) -> SeedEnsembleResult

Reconstruct a mask at several dither seeds and combine the tensions inferred from each mesh.

See foambryo.seed_ensembles for what the seeds change, the measured gain, and why the seed spread is a lower bound on the error rather than an error bar: tension_seed_sd sees only the part of the error that changes with the seed, never the bias every seed shares.

Each seed's mesh is reconstructed as dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask reconstructs it, at that dither seed (crop faces included), and its tensions are infer_tensions(mesh, 1, mode, angle_reading=angle_reading): normalised to a mean of 1, chord-read unless angle_reading says otherwise, with the default solver options.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mask ndarray

instance segmentation image, as for foambryo.dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask: 3-D integer labels, axes (z, y, x), label 0 the medium.

required seeds Iterable[int]

the dither seeds, distinct; 0 to 7 by default. Fix the list in advance: never choose seeds by their result.

DEFAULT_ENSEMBLE_SEEDS min_distance int

minimum distance between tessellation points, in voxels. Defaults to 3, as dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask. Keyword-only.

3 mode TensionComputationMethod

the tension method, YoungDupre by default. Any method works with combine="tensions"; combine="angles" needs YoungDupre. Keyword-only.

YoungDupre angle_reading str

the angle reading of the angle-reading methods, "chord" by default. Keyword-only.

CHORD_READING combine str

"tensions" (the default): average the seeds' tensions. "angles" (experimental, YoungDupre only, emits SeedEnsembleExperimentalWarning): average the contact angles over the seeds, then infer once. With angle_reading="quadric" it was the most accurate option on synthetic tissues (median error -45 % against the default on 46 tissues), but its advantage over averaging quadric-read tensions is small and inconsistent, so it is not the default. On synthetic masks degraded by a smooth random warp of about one voxel, combine="angles" with the quadric reading lost its advantage over the default on larger tissues of 90 and 165 cells while keeping it on small aggregates. Keyword-only.

COMBINE_TENSIONS max_workers int

seeds reconstructed at once, in separate processes; 1 (the default) runs them one after another in this process. The result does not depend on it. Each worker holds one reconstruction: about 8 GiB for a 165-cell tissue at real cell size, about 30-35 GiB for a 1 866-cell tissue. Keyword-only.

1 spacing tuple[float, float, float] | None

the voxel size along the mask's axes 0, 1, 2, as for dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask: given, every seed's reconstruction resamples a mask with one longer axis to cubic voxels of the shortest spacing and returns the mesh in the spacing's unit (min_distance then counts cubic voxels). Defaults to None, the voxel grid. Keyword-only.

None progress Callable[[int, int, int], None] | None

called once per seed, as its tensions come back and in seed order, with (seeds done, seeds in all, that seed), for a front end's progress display; it changes no number. Defaults to None. Keyword-only.

None **reconstruction_options object

print_info and physical_image_faces, passed to the reconstruction as dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask passes them.

{}

the ensemble tensions, the seed spread (absolute and relative to the tension; a lower bound on the error, not an error bar), how many seeds found each interface, the flag for those found by fewer than half, and each seed's own tensions and reconstruction record. Every map is keyed by interface (label_1, label_2), label_1 < label_2, over the union of the seeds' interfaces.

docs.title: Segmentation masks
docs.text:
Segmentation masks as front ends receive them: read, checked, and described before a reconstruction.

A mask is a 3-D array of non-negative integer labels, 0 the medium, axis 0 = z, axis 1 = y, axis 2 = x. The foambryo command and the napari plugin read and check masks with these functions, so both accept and refuse the same arrays with the same messages:

  • read_segmentation_mask(path): a .npy, .npz (array mask, optionally spacing and spacing_unit) or .tif/.tiff file (needs tifffile, foambryo[cli]), checked;
  • check_segmentation_mask(mask): the checks alone, for an array already in memory;
  • segmentation_mask_report(mask): what a reconstruction will meet, counted and changed in nothing: the cells, the cells touching the image box (they will be cut cells), the cells in several pieces, the pieces of medium the tissue encloses, and the very small labels.

Labels need not be consecutive: a label is a name, and the mesh keeps it.

docs.title: Tensions
docs.text:
Surface tensions inferred from a multimaterial mesh, by any of the 13 methods of TensionComputationMethod.

The entry points are infer_tensions (a map interface -> tension), infer_tensions_and_residuals (the same, with the solve's residuals), infer_tensions_and_residuals_with_report (plus the angle reading's coverage, the entry point to use for anything published) and infer_tensions_by_junction_component (each interface's connected piece of the junction graph made explicit).

Conventions shared by every function here:

  • an interface is keyed (label_1, label_2) with label_1 < label_2; label 0 is the exterior medium;
  • tensions are relative: only their ratios are determined by the mesh. They are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension, exactly, in each connected piece of the junction graph (see TensionComputationMethod for the methods that normalise otherwise). Pressures computed from them (foambryo.pressure_inference) are in the same tension unit divided by the mesh's length unit;
  • an interface whose tension the mesh does not determine is float("nan"), never a number;
  • angles are read in radians.

Sacha Ichbiah 2021 Matthieu Perez 2024

docs.title: TensionComputationMethod
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

Describe the formula used to infer the tensions from contact angles at each junction.

It can be: - YoungDupre (Young-Dupré with cosines only), - YoungDupreLocal (the same balance imposed per trijunctional edge instead of once per triple line on angles averaged along it — see foambryo.per_edge_tension_inference), - ProjectionYoungDupre (Young-Dupré with cosines and sines), - Equilibrium, - Cotan (cotangent formula, see Yamamoto et al. 2026), - InvCotan (inverse of the cotangent formula), - Lami (Lami's theorem), - InvLami (inverse of the Lami's relation), - LogLami (logarithm of the Lami's relation), - Variational (variational formulation, see our article), - ForceBalance (the unified discrete force-balance operator with the mean-tension normalisation imposed exactly, through a KKT system), - ForceBalanceSoftRow (the same operator, with the normalisation as one more least-squares row, so its mean tension is only approximately mean_tension), - ForceBalanceMAP (the same operator, with a Gaussian prior; the normalisation is anchored only softly, so its mean tension is deliberately not exactly mean_tension; its relative tensions do not depend on the mesh's length unit or on the value of mean_tension, see foambryo.force_balance_inference._solve_bayesian_map).

The normalisation. Only tension ratios are determined by a mesh, so every method fixes the overall scale (the "gauge") by one more condition: the tensions are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension, exactly, in each connected piece of the junction graph. This holds exactly for every method but two: YoungDupre, YoungDupreLocal, ProjectionYoungDupre, Cotan, InvCotan, Lami and InvLami meet it in each piece of the junction graph (foambryo.junction_graph.solve_gauged_least_squares); LogLami meets it on the geometric mean; Equilibrium, Variational (both routes) and ForceBalance meet it over the whole mesh at once; ForceBalanceSoftRow (a least-squares row by definition) and ForceBalanceMAP (a prior) do not meet it exactly. On a cropped mesh the mean runs over the interfaces whose tension is determined. Until 0.6.0 the first group, Equilibrium and the Gram route of Variational imposed it as a least-squares row of ones too; that row changed only the overall scale of their tensions, never a ratio (see foambryo.junction_graph).

Cost on large tissues. Equilibrium, Variational and ForceBalance solve dense systems only: on a 1 866-cell tissue each took one to two hours with a peak of about 68 GiB, where YoungDupre, the default, takes seconds (see the user guide's page on large tissues).

The three ForceBalance* members are one estimator under three normalisations, not three physical models; they exist as separate members so that the comparison between the three is a regenerable benchmark row rather than a one-off table. See foambryo.force_balance_inference.

Which methods read angles and which invert an operator, and why the distinction now has measured consequences. YoungDupre, YoungDupreLocal, ProjectionYoungDupre, Lami, InvLami and LogLami are all built from measured contact angles at triple junctions — they read the mesh's local geometry pointwise and never assemble or invert a global operator. Cotan, InvCotan, Variational and the three ForceBalance* members instead assemble a discrete operator over the whole mesh (an area/volume-gradient system, or its force-balance generalisation) and solve or invert it. Equilibrium is a geometric-edge balance and does not cleanly fall in either family (see its own note in foambryo.validation.force_balance). This split matters because mesh-reconstruction quality affects the two families very differently: on dw3d-reconstructed meshes, the operator-inverting family's error tracks the mesh's distance from mechanical equilibrium (rho_free) far more strongly than the angle-reading family's does, so an operator- inverting method can be dramatically more or less accurate depending on which meshing pipeline produced its input, while an angle-reading method is comparatively insensitive to it. See dw3d's BENCHMARKS.md and this package's own BENCHMARKS.md for the numbers.

Degenerate junctions. Cotan, InvCotan, Lami and LogLami have coefficients that are infinite at a wedge of exactly 0 or 180 degrees (1/sin, cot(phi/2), log sin). Such wedges occur on short triple lines whose faces are exactly coplanar (mesh vertices on the voxel lattice). These four methods leave such a line's equations out, with a DegenerateWedgeWarning; an interface left without any equation is nan. The other methods' coefficients stay finite and bounded there, and they are unchanged. See DEGENERATE_WEDGE_TOLERANCE.

The operator-inverting family is unreliable on reconstructed meshes, measured. On the benchmark cohort's shipped-default reconstructions rho_free -- the distance of the mesh from any equilibrium of the force-balance operator -- has median 0.578 against the reference meshes' 0.0118 (a factor of about 50), and all 40 equilibrium cases exceed the 0.2 threshold at which foambryo.uncertainty reports that no surface tensions balance the mesh at all. Every ForceBalance* number obtained on a dw3d mesh, including every published comparison between reconstruction variants through this family, should be read with that floor in mind. See foambryo.force_balance_inference's module docstring.

docs.title: VariationalRoute
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

Which linear algebra TensionComputationMethod.Variational uses to reach its answer.

Both routes minimise the same discrete energy gradient; they differ in how, and the choice moves published numbers, which is why both are kept.

  • Gram (route P, the original): form the Gram normal equations M^T M, divide every row by its own row sum, Schur-eliminate the pressures, then least-squares with the mean-tension normalisation met exactly (foambryo.junction_graph.solve_with_exact_gauge; until 0.6.0 it was a least-squares row of ones). It has no formulation for crop faces.
  • Operator (route Q, the default): minimise ||M beta||^2 directly through M, with the normalisation eliminated by substitution. M^T M is never formed and there is no row normalisation.

TensionComputationMethod.Variational always takes the default route, VARIATIONAL_ROUTE_DEFAULT; Gram is reachable only through the internal _infer_tension_variational_yd(mesh, mean_tension, route=VariationalRoute.Gram).

The row normalisation is the substantive difference, and it has never been justified. Dividing normal-equation row i by sum_j (M^T M)_ij is not a symmetric preconditioner (it destroys the symmetry of the Gram matrix), it is not scale-invariant in any documented sense, and it has no derivation in the paper or its Supplementary Note. Measured on benchmarking-dataset: the divisors span a factor 57-140 within a single mesh and change sign, so it is a genuine, arbitrary reweighting of the physics rows — not a numerical nicety. That is why the two routes give different answers at all (~1.4e-4 per tension).

Operator is the default, chosen on measured evidence. See VARIATIONAL_ROUTE_DEFAULT and foambryo_benchmarks/run_variational_route.py. Gram stays reachable so every published number remains reproducible.

docs.title: DegenerateWedgeWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Triple lines with a wedge at 0 or 180 degrees were left out of a method whose coefficients are singular there.

Emitted by Cotan, InvCotan, Lami and LogLami, once per call, naming how many lines were left out and how many interfaces were left without any equation (reported as nan).

docs.title: infer_tensions
docs.text:
infer_tensions(mesh: DcelData, mean_tension: float = 1, mode: TensionComputationMethod = TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre, *, angle_reading: str = CHORD_READING, refusal: WedgeRefusal = NO_REFUSAL, solver: str = 'auto', sparse_threshold: int | None = None, diagnostics: bool | str = False) -> dict[tuple[int, int], float] | tuple[dict[tuple[int, int], float], SolveDiagnostics]

Infer the relative surface tension of every interface of a mesh, by the chosen method.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

Mesh to analyze, in any length unit (the tensions do not depend on it).

required mean_tension float

The normalisation: the tensions are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension, exactly, in each connected piece of the junction graph (for LogLami, their geometric mean; Equilibrium, Variational and ForceBalance normalise the whole mesh at once; ForceBalanceSoftRow meets it only approximately and ForceBalanceMAP deliberately not exactly; see TensionComputationMethod). Only tension ratios are measured, so this sets the unit of the tensions. Defaults to 1.

1 mode TensionComputationMethod

method to infer tensions. Defaults to TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre.

YoungDupre angle_reading str

which trijunction angle convention the angle-reading methods (ANGLE_READING_METHODS) consume, one of foambryo.second_order_angle_reading.ANGLE_READINGS: "chord" (the default, bit-identical to every published number), "quadric" (the second-order reading), "oriented_chord" or "oriented_quadric" (the same readings with reflex wedges reported above 180 degrees). Keyword-only. A quadric reading that could not cover every trijunction face falls back to the chord there and emits an AngleReadingCoverageWarning; use :func:infer_tensions_and_residuals_with_report to get the coverage numbers instead of the warning.

CHORD_READING refusal WedgeRefusal

which trijunction observations the angle-reading methods decline to use, and how -- see foambryo.wedge_refusal. Keyword-only; defaults to NO_REFUSAL (refusing nothing), which is bitwise the historical behaviour. A non-default policy on a method that reads no wedge angle raises rather than being ignored. Refusing rows can leave an interface, or a whole mesh, with no surviving junction line: those interfaces are reported float("nan"), never a number, and how often a policy does that is a number to report beside any accuracy it buys.

NO_REFUSAL solver str

"auto" (the default), "dense" or "sparse": how the linear systems are solved (foambryo.linear_solves). "auto" is dense below sparse_threshold unknowns and sparse at or above, and bitwise the dense result below it. "sparse" raises ValueError for a method with no sparse path (Equilibrium, Variational, ForceBalance*). Keyword-only.

'auto' sparse_threshold int | None

unknowns (interfaces) at which "auto" goes sparse; None (the default) is foambryo.junction_graph.SPARSE_SOLVE_MIN_UNKNOWNS (2 000). Keyword-only.

None diagnostics bool | str

False (the default), True or "spectrum": also return a foambryo.linear_solves.SolveDiagnostics, last, with one record per solve (solver, shape, rank, residual norm, condition number, time; "spectrum" adds the extreme singular values of the sparse solves). Keyword-only.

False

Returns:

Type Description dict[tuple[int, int], float] | tuple[dict[tuple[int, int], float], SolveDiagnostics]

dict[tuple[int, int], float]: map interface (label_1, label_2), label_1 < label_2, label 0 the exterior medium -> relative tension on this interface. An interface whose tension the mesh does not determine is float("nan"), never a number: one with no triple line at all (a fully closed surface -- an engulfed cell, a sealed lumen), one whose every line was refused or left out, or, for Cotan, InvCotan, Lami and LogLami, one left without any equation by a degenerate wedge (DegenerateWedgeWarning). On a cropped mesh the interfaces made only of crop faces (DcelData.crop_interfaces) are absent. If the mesh's triple-junction graph is in more than one disconnected piece, or has any undetermined interface, this flat map holds tensions normalised separately in each piece, which are not on the same scale (a JunctionGraphGaugeWarning is emitted in that case); use :func:infer_tensions_by_junction_component to get each interface's piece explicitly, and never average or compare tensions across pieces from this map. With diagnostics on, the tuple (map, SolveDiagnostics).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

on an invalid solver, sparse_threshold or diagnostics; on an unknown angle_reading; on a non-default angle_reading or refusal with a method outside ANGLE_READING_METHODS; on solver="sparse" with Equilibrium, Variational or a ForceBalance* member; with YoungDupreLocal, on a quadric reading or on a mesh with no trijunctional edge; with Cotan, InvCotan, Lami or LogLami, if the system still holds a non-finite coefficient after the degenerate lines are left out.

MalformedTripleLineError

if a triple line names an interface the mesh does not have (foambryo.junction_graph; not expected on a well-formed mesh).

Warns:

Type Description JunctionGraphGaugeWarning

when the junction graph is in several pieces or an interface is undetermined (the methods normalised per piece of the junction graph).

AngleReadingCoverageWarning

when a quadric reading fell back to the chord on part of the mesh.

DegenerateWedgeWarning

when Cotan, InvCotan, Lami or LogLami left out lines with a wedge at 0 or 180 degrees.

SparseSolveFallbackWarning

when lsqr did not converge on a large system (the dense solve runs instead, or lsqr's last iterate is returned if the dense one cannot fit in memory).

DenseSolveMemoryWarning

when solver="dense" is forced on a system too large for the memory available.

docs.title: infer_tensions_and_residuals
docs.text:
infer_tensions_and_residuals(mesh: DcelData, mean_tension: float = 1, mode: TensionComputationMethod = TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre, *, angle_reading: str = CHORD_READING, refusal: WedgeRefusal = NO_REFUSAL, solver: str = 'auto', sparse_threshold: int | None = None, diagnostics: bool | str = False) -> tuple

Infer the relative surface tensions by the chosen method, with the solve's residuals.

infer_tensions returns this function's second value. Every argument, warning and exception is infer_tensions's; this function is where its JunctionGraphGaugeWarning and AngleReadingCoverageWarning are emitted.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

Mesh to analyze, in any length unit.

required mean_tension float

The normalisation: the tensions are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension, exactly, in each connected piece of the junction graph (see :func:infer_tensions for the methods that normalise otherwise). Defaults to 1.

1 mode TensionComputationMethod

method to infer tensions. Defaults to TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre.

YoungDupre angle_reading str

one of foambryo.second_order_angle_reading.ANGLE_READINGS; "chord" is the default. Keyword-only. See :func:infer_tensions.

CHORD_READING refusal WedgeRefusal

which trijunction observations the angle-reading methods decline to use, and how -- see foambryo.wedge_refusal. Keyword-only; defaults to NO_REFUSAL (refusing nothing), which is bitwise the historical behaviour. See :func:infer_tensions.

NO_REFUSAL solver str

"auto" (the default), "dense" or "sparse", as for :func:infer_tensions. Keyword-only.

'auto' sparse_threshold int | None

unknowns at which "auto" goes sparse; None (the default) is foambryo.junction_graph.SPARSE_SOLVE_MIN_UNKNOWNS (2 000). Keyword-only.

None diagnostics bool | str

False (the default), True or "spectrum": also return a foambryo.linear_solves.SolveDiagnostics, last. Keyword-only.

False

Returns:

Type Description tuple

tuple[NDArray[np.float64], dict[tuple[int, int], float], NDArray[np.float64]]: - the relative tensions as an array, in the map's key order (sorted interfaces); - map interface (label_1, label_2) -> tension on this interface. See :func:infer_tensions's return value for the undetermined-interface (nan) and junction-graph (normalised per piece) caveats -- they apply here identically; - the squared norm of the residual of the solved equations, without the normalisation (which is met exactly and adds none): a length-1 array, one entry per connected piece of the junction graph when there are several, empty when no interface is determined; in log space for LogLami; - with diagnostics on, a fourth value: the SolveDiagnostics.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

as :func:infer_tensions.

MalformedTripleLineError

as :func:infer_tensions.

infer_tensions_and_residuals_with_report(mesh: DcelData, mean_tension: float = 1, mode: TensionComputationMethod = TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre, *, angle_reading: str = CHORD_READING, refusal: WedgeRefusal = NO_REFUSAL, solver: str = 'auto', sparse_threshold: int | None = None, diagnostics: bool | str = False) -> tuple

:func:infer_tensions_and_residuals, plus which trijunction faces the reading covered.

The reporting entry point, and the one to use for anything that will be published or benchmarked. It emits neither AngleReadingCoverageWarning nor JunctionGraphGaugeWarning: the caller holds the coverage report, and can read the junction graph's pieces with :func:infer_tensions_by_junction_component. Every other warning is :func:infer_tensions's.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

Mesh to analyze, in any length unit.

required mean_tension float

The normalisation: the tensions are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension, exactly, in each connected piece of the junction graph (see :func:infer_tensions for the methods that normalise otherwise). Defaults to 1.

1 mode TensionComputationMethod

method to infer tensions. Defaults to TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre.

YoungDupre angle_reading str

one of foambryo.second_order_angle_reading.ANGLE_READINGS; "chord" is the default. Keyword-only. See :func:infer_tensions.

CHORD_READING refusal WedgeRefusal

which trijunction observations the angle-reading methods decline to use, and how -- see foambryo.wedge_refusal. Keyword-only; defaults to NO_REFUSAL (refusing nothing), which is bitwise the historical behaviour. See :func:infer_tensions.

NO_REFUSAL solver str

"auto" (the default), "dense" or "sparse", as for :func:infer_tensions. Keyword-only.

'auto' sparse_threshold int | None

unknowns at which "auto" goes sparse; None (the default) is foambryo.junction_graph.SPARSE_SOLVE_MIN_UNKNOWNS (2 000). Keyword-only.

None diagnostics bool | str

False (the default), True or "spectrum": also return a foambryo.linear_solves.SolveDiagnostics, last. Keyword-only.

False

Returns:

Type Description tuple

tuple[NDArray[np.float64], dict[tuple[int, int], float], NDArray[np.float64], AngleReadingReport]: the three values :func:infer_tensions_and_residuals returns, plus the coverage report. For a method outside ANGLE_READING_METHODS, or for a chord reading, the report is the trivial complete-coverage one. With diagnostics on, a fifth value: the SolveDiagnostics.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

as :func:infer_tensions; in particular if angle_reading is not "chord" and mode does not read angles.

MalformedTripleLineError

as :func:infer_tensions.

docs.title: infer_tensions_by_junction_component
docs.text:
infer_tensions_by_junction_component(mesh: DcelData, mean_tension: float = 1, mode: TensionComputationMethod = TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre, *, refusal: WedgeRefusal = NO_REFUSAL, solver: str = 'auto', sparse_threshold: int | None = None, diagnostics: bool | str = False) -> ComponentTensionSolution | tuple[ComponentTensionSolution, SolveDiagnostics]

Infer tensions with each connected piece of the triple-junction graph made explicit.

Two interfaces are coupled only when they meet on a triple line. When the graph of these couplings falls into several pieces, each piece's tensions are determined only up to their own scale: this function normalises each piece separately (its mean tension is mean_tension, exactly) and says which interface belongs to which piece, rather than collapsing them into one map. See foambryo.junction_graph's module docstring for the mechanism.

Use this instead of infer_tensions/infer_tensions_and_residuals whenever a mesh might have a disconnected triple-junction graph (12 of the 72 simulator meshes of 91-166 cells in BENCHMARKS.md do) or a fully closed interface, and the caller needs to know which interfaces are (or are not) on a common scale before comparing or aggregating their tensions. It always reads the chord angles; it emits no JunctionGraphGaugeWarning, since the result carries what the warning would say.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

Mesh to analyze, in any length unit.

required mean_tension float

The normalisation, applied per piece: the tensions of each connected piece are normalised so that their mean is mean_tension, exactly (for LogLami, their geometric mean). Defaults to 1.

1 mode TensionComputationMethod

Which method to use: one of YoungDupre, YoungDupreLocal, ProjectionYoungDupre, Cotan, InvCotan, Lami, InvLami and LogLami. Defaults to YoungDupre.

YoungDupre refusal WedgeRefusal

which trijunction observations the estimator declines, and how (foambryo.wedge_refusal). Keyword-only; defaults to NO_REFUSAL (refusing nothing), which is bitwise the historical behaviour. This is the entry point to prefer under a refusal policy: refusing rows can itself split the junction graph, and this function hands the caller the resulting pieces and undetermined interfaces rather than blending them.

NO_REFUSAL solver str

"auto" (the default), "dense" or "sparse": how the linear systems are solved (foambryo.linear_solves). "auto" is dense below sparse_threshold unknowns and sparse at or above, and bitwise the dense result below it. Every method accepted here has a sparse path. Keyword-only.

'auto' sparse_threshold int | None

unknowns (interfaces of one piece) at which "auto" goes sparse; None (the default) is foambryo.junction_graph.SPARSE_SOLVE_MIN_UNKNOWNS (2 000). Keyword-only.

None diagnostics bool | str

False (the default), True or "spectrum": also return a foambryo.linear_solves.SolveDiagnostics, last, with one record per solve (solver, shape, rank, residual norm, condition number, time; "spectrum" adds the extreme singular values of the sparse solves). Keyword-only.

False

Returns:

Name Type Description ComponentTensionSolution ComponentTensionSolution | tuple[ComponentTensionSolution, SolveDiagnostics]

dict_tensions maps every interface (label_1, label_2), label_1 < label_2, to its relative tension, or float("nan") if it is undetermined (no surviving triple line); component_of maps every interface to its piece, or None if undetermined; gauge_notes states, per piece, the normalisation applied; solver_notes which solver ran on each piece. Tensions of different pieces are on different scales and must not be compared. On a cropped mesh the crop interfaces are absent. With diagnostics on, the tuple (solution, SolveDiagnostics).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If mode is Equilibrium, Variational or a ForceBalance* member -- these methods' coupling structure is not the triple-junction graph (see foambryo.junction_graph's "Scope: which methods"), so this decomposition does not apply to them; use infer_tensions(mesh, mean_tension, mode) instead. Also on an invalid solver option, and as :func:infer_tensions for the method itself.

MalformedTripleLineError

as :func:infer_tensions.

Warns:

Type Description DegenerateWedgeWarning

as :func:infer_tensions.

SparseSolveFallbackWarning

as :func:infer_tensions.

DenseSolveMemoryWarning

as :func:infer_tensions.

docs.title: Error bars and diagnostics
docs.text:
Error bars on inferred tensions, with their measured calibration, and identifiability diagnostics.

infer_tensions_with_uncertainty returns the tensions of infer_tensions (it never changes a point estimate) together with an interval and the diagnostics needed to decide whether to trust it; compute_inference_diagnostics returns the diagnostics alone. Neither has a formulation for crop faces yet: both raise ValueError on a cropped mesh.

Large tissues. Both compute the diagnostics from the dense force-balance operator, three rows per mesh vertex and one column per interface and per cell, and its singular value decomposition. Past DENSE_OPERATOR_ENTRY_LIMIT entries (2**31 - 1, the most scipy's LAPACK can index) that decomposition cannot run, so both raise ValueError at once, before building anything; a mesh of the default reconstruction reaches it at about 1 300 cells of real size. Below the limit the cost grows with the operator: on a generated 1 200-cell foam (0.8 of the limit) infer_tensions_with_uncertainty(mesh, 1, YoungDupre) took about 30 minutes and 46 GiB.

Read this before using an error bar from here. No interval of this module is a calibrated error bar on a reconstructed mesh. The first-order interval of the YoungDupre tensions (AnglePropagation) is a lower bound on the error: measured on 2 400 reconstructions with ground truth, one reconstruction's +- std contained the true tension for 26-54 % of interfaces (nominal 68 %), because the error is mostly the reconstruction's bias, which no propagated scatter measures. The calibration figures below are for the simulator's reference meshes.

The goal here is not "add error bars" — it is produce an interval whose error/std is O(1), or state plainly that we cannot. error/std (the ratio of the actual error against ground truth to the reported standard deviation, gauge-matched) is the calibration metric: 1 is calibrated, >>1 is optimistic (dangerous), <<1 is conservative (safe but uninformative). Measured over the 42 equilibrium cases of benchmarking-dataset (foambryo_benchmarks/run_uncertainty_calibration.py):

model estimator median error/std worst case verdict ProbeResidual force balance 0.233 0.93 O(1), and conservative on 42/42 CoherentResidual force balance 1.33 29.9 O(1) at the median, not uniformly EdgeBootstrap YoungDupreLocal 0.27 1.57 ~4x conservative (measured on all 47 cases) BayesianMap force balance 0.21 0.61 O(1) by choice of prior, not by measurement AnglePropagation YoungDupre 0.015 0.078 ~65x conservative here; too narrow on reconstructions ClusterRobust force balance 204 1.5e4 optimistic; not recommended ClusterBootstrap force balance 216 3e4 optimistic; not recommended IidGls force balance 246 5.4e3 optimistic; not recommended (the naive posterior) LineBootstrap YoungDupre 1.3e-05 — ~1e5 conservative, weight-confounded; diagnostic only

AnglePropagation's row is on the reference meshes, whose angles are nearly exact. On 2 400 reconstructions of five tissue populations with ground truth, one reconstruction's +- std contains the true tension for only 26-54 % of interfaces (nominal 68 %), +- 2 std for 48-79 % (nominal 95 %): it is not a calibrated interval there, and no single factor makes it one.

So that goal is met: ProbeResidual is an interval with error/std = O(1), and it errs on the safe side on every one of the 42 cases.

Why the naive posterior fails by 250x, and why the fix is one factor. The i.i.d. model says the per-component vertex force residual is N(0, sigma_f^2) with sigma_f estimated as ||M beta|| / sqrt(dof). On a 11 000-vertex mesh that is ~34 000 rows, so the estimator averages the noise down by sqrt(34 000) ~ 185 and claims to know each tension to ~1e-4. It does not: the residual was measured to be systematic — the meshes are the equilibrium of the generator's volume-constraint projection, not of M beta = 0 — so it does not average down at all. Measured, the implied n_eff (the number of independent observations the rows are actually worth, dof / (error/std)^2) has median 0.57 on the 42 and is below 1 on 29 of them: the ~33 000 rows are worth less than one independent observation.

CoherentResidual replaces the probabilistic assumption with a deterministic one, and it is the same linear algebra with sigma_f -> ||M beta||: treat the residual as one coherent perturbation of measured norm and unknown direction. The worst-case-direction first-order bound on the estimator is then

|d gamma_i| <= sigma * sqrt(Sigma_unit_ii),

with Sigma_unit the constrained-GLS shape matrix of foambryo.validation.force_balance.constrained_covariance at sigma_f = 1. That is the n_eff = 1 extreme, and it moves the median calibration from 246 to 1.33 — the whole 250x gap is that one sqrt(dof) factor, nothing else. But it is not uniform: 10 of the 42 cases still come out above 10, worst 29.9.

ProbeResidual closes that, and the mechanism is measured rather than guessed. The remaining failure is self-fitting: ||M beta_hat|| is the residual at the estimate, and beta_hat was chosen to minimise it. The residual at the truth is a median 5.4x and up to 87x larger, and that ratio is what predicts the failures (Spearman 0.80). Worse, the bound fails worst on the best meshes — a mesh close to M's equilibrium lets the fit drive ||M beta_hat|| to almost nothing while the true error stays put (Spearman against rho_free: -0.81). ProbeResidual therefore takes sigma from the residual at an independent tension estimate (PROBE_METHOD, YoungDupre, which never touches M). Measured: the probe residual reproduces the residual at the ground truth to 0.1 % on every case, so this is the oracle bound without an oracle — and probe error can only inflate sigma, so it fails safe. See _probe_residual_norm.

Why resampling does not rescue the i.i.d. model. ClusterRobust (a cluster-robust sandwich) and ClusterBootstrap (resampling whole cells) both model correlation; neither can model a bias. Measured, they move 246 to 204 and 216 — a factor 1.2, not 250. That is the honest reason to prefer the deterministic bound: the dominant term is not variance, so there is nothing for a resampling scheme to find.

Why ForceBalanceMAP's apparently-good 0.21 is not an answer. Its interval's width is set by MAP_PRIOR_TENSION_STD, a hyperparameter documented as "deliberately broad" and never derived. Sweeping it over 0.03-1.0 moves error/std over 2.93-0.061, a log-log slope of -1.03: the interval is the prior. Any calibration it shows was chosen. Both CoherentResidual and ProbeResidual have no such knob — their scale is a measured residual norm.

The negative control behaves differently, and that is a check on the mechanism. On the five non-equilibrium cases excluded from every accuracy claim, the residual is genuinely large and spread over interface interiors, so the implied n_eff is 370 rather than 0.57, IidGls improves to 9.0, and ProbeResidual/CoherentResidual become ~20x conservative. The models fail in the safe direction exactly where the mesh is bad — which is the behaviour one wants and not something that was fitted.

Why the angle family is conservative rather than optimistic. YoungDupre reads triple-line angles and never touches M. Propagating the measured along-line angle spread through the operator over-predicts its error by ~2 orders, because (as measured) the dataset's angle deviations from Neumann lie nearly orthogonal to the Young-Dupre operator's column space. So its interval is safe and nearly useless, and its point estimate (2.3e-05) is far better than any interval we can defend around it.

One caveat, and it is load-bearing. YoungDupre's accuracy is weighting-critical: a factor-~4 change in relative inter-line weights costs two orders of magnitude. LineBootstrap resamples whole triple lines, which is such a reweighting (n copies of a line of weight w act as one row of weight w sqrt(n)), so its width is dominated by weight perturbation rather than by angle noise. It is reported for that reason, not despite it. Nothing here changes the junction-length weighting of any shipped method — every point estimate returned by this module is bit-identical to the corresponding infer_tensions call.

docs.title: UncertaintyModel
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

How the interval around an inferred tension is produced.

See the module docstring for the measured error/std of each. ProbeResidual is the one recommended for reporting — O(1) and conservative on every one of the 42 equilibrium cases. The others are kept because a calibration claim that cannot be reproduced against its alternatives is not a calibration claim, and because two of them (IidGls, ClusterRobust) are the models a reader would otherwise reach for.

Attributes:

Name Type Description ProbeResidual

CoherentResidual, but scaled by the residual at an independent tension estimate instead of at the fitted one, which removes the self-fitting. Force-balance / Variational family. Default, and the only model measured to be conservative on every one of the 42 cases.

CoherentResidual

Deterministic worst-case-direction bound, sigma_f = ||M beta|| (n_eff = 1). Force-balance / Variational family. O(1) at the median but not uniformly — see the module docstring.

IidGls

the naive constrained-GLS posterior, sigma_f = ||M beta|| / sqrt(dof). Retained for comparison and not for reporting — ~250x optimistic.

ClusterRobust

Cluster-robust (sandwich) covariance, clusters = cells.

ClusterBootstrap

Nonparametric bootstrap resampling whole cells.

AnglePropagation

First-order propagation of the measured along-line angle spread through the Young-Dupre solve. Angle family (YoungDupre), and its default. Not a calibrated interval on reconstructions: a lower bound on the error (one reconstruction's +- std held the true tension for 26-54 % of interfaces, nominal 68 %).

LineBootstrap

Nonparametric bootstrap resampling whole triple lines. Angle family; weight-confounded, see the module docstring.

docs.title: InferenceDiagnostics dataclass
docs.text:
InferenceDiagnostics(n_interfaces: int, n_cells: int, n_rows: int, rho: float | None, rho_free: float, sigma_gauge: float, sigma_soft: float, soft_mode_fractions: tuple[float, float, float], condition_number: float)

Per-mesh diagnostics saying whether any tension inference on it can be trusted.

These are properties of the mesh and the operator, not of a method, which is what makes them usable on dw3d output where no ground truth exists. rho_free is the one to read first: it was measured that the force-balance / Variational family's error is limited by it (median rho_free 0.012 against a median error 0.021 on the 42), while YoungDupre's is not.

Attributes:

Name Type Description n_interfaces int

Number of interfaces (tension unknowns).

n_cells int

Number of cells (pressure unknowns; the exterior is the gauge).

n_rows int

Rows of M = 3 * n_vertices.

rho float | None

||P_perp M_gamma gamma|| / ||M_gamma gamma|| at the tensions passed in, pressures marginalised — the fraction of the surface-tension force this mesh leaves unbalanced at those tensions. None if no tensions were given. Gauge-invariant.

rho_free float

The same quantity with the tensions themselves free — the distance of this mesh from any equilibrium of M. It is the ratio at the minimiser of ||M beta|| under the mean-tension gauge, so rho at given tensions can fall slightly below it, but not by more than the gap between that minimiser and the minimum of the ratio. Gauge-invariant. ~1e-10 for a mesh that minimises M; 0.0007-0.036 on the 42 simulation meshes; 0.26-0.28 on the five non-equilibrium cases excluded from every accuracy claim. On dw3d-reconstructed meshes of the same cases it is about 50x the reference value: median 0.578 (range 0.48-0.72) on the 40-case equilibrium cohort, every case above the 0.2 alarm below, so the force-balance family's numbers on reconstructions stand on a floor no gauge choice can lower.

sigma_gauge float

Smallest singular value of the column-normalised M — the overall-scale gauge direction. Should be near zero; if it is not, the operator has no scale gauge and something is wrong.

sigma_soft float

Second-smallest singular value: the worst-determined physical direction. 1 / sigma_soft is the noise amplification (1.2-5.5 on the 42).

soft_mode_fractions tuple[float, float, float]

How much of that soft direction sits in the (surface tension, line tension, pressure) blocks. The line entry is always 0 here — the harness operator carries no line-tension block, by the package author's design choice.

condition_number float

cond(M), the operator actually inverted.
