docs.title: infer_tensions_with_uncertainty
docs.text:
infer_tensions_with_uncertainty(mesh: DcelData, mean_tension: float = 1, method: TensionComputationMethod = TensionComputationMethod.ForceBalance, model: UncertaintyModel | None = None, n_resamples: int = DEFAULT_N_RESAMPLES, seed: int = 0) -> TensionUncertaintyResult

Infer tensions and an interval whose calibration has been measured and is reported.

A companion to foambryo.infer_tensions: the point estimate is that of the corresponding infer_tensions call -- bit-identical for ForceBalance and YoungDupre (pinned by tests/test_uncertainty.py), to rounding (within 1e-12 on benchmark case 000) for Variational, whose interval is built on the ForceBalance operator. The YoungDupre tensions are normalised over the whole mesh at once, so they match infer_tensions on a mesh whose junction graph is in one piece. The returned calibration_note states the measured error/std of the interval rather than leaving the reader to assume it is 1.

The interval is not a calibrated error bar on a reconstructed mesh. The first-order AnglePropagation interval of YoungDupre is a lower bound on the error: one reconstruction's +- std held the true tension for 26-54 % of interfaces (nominal 68 %) and +- 2 std for 48-79 % (nominal 95 %), measured on 2 400 reconstructions with ground truth. The force-balance family's error is floored by rho_free on reconstructed meshes (see the module docstring and InferenceDiagnostics).

Only the estimators whose intervals have been calibrated are accepted. That is deliberate: an interval for a method nobody measured would be exactly the failure mode this module exists to close.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

Mesh to analyse, in any length unit; not cropped.

required mean_tension float

The normalisation: the mean of the returned tensions, met exactly. Defaults to 1.

1 method TensionComputationMethod

The estimator. One of ForceBalance, Variational (both the force-balance family, same estimator up to the solve route) or YoungDupre (the angle family). Defaults to ForceBalance.

ForceBalance model UncertaintyModel | None

How to build the interval. Defaults to None, which selects ProbeResidual for the force-balance family and AnglePropagation for the angle family — in both cases the best-calibrated model measured for that estimator.

None n_resamples int

Bootstrap draws, for the bootstrap models (ClusterBootstrap, LineBootstrap). Defaults to DEFAULT_N_RESAMPLES (200).

DEFAULT_N_RESAMPLES seed int

Bootstrap RNG seed, recorded so any number is reproducible. Defaults to 0.

0

Returns:

Name Type Description TensionUncertaintyResult TensionUncertaintyResult

Tensions (keyed by interface (label_1, label_2), label_1 < label_2), the per-interface interval half-width tension_std in the same unit, the mesh's diagnostics and the calibration note.

Raises:

Type Description NotImplementedError

If method has no calibrated interval (any method but ForceBalance, Variational and YoungDupre).

ValueError

If model does not apply to method's estimator family, if the mesh has crop faces, for which no interval is calibrated yet (foambryo.crop_faces), or if its dense force-balance operator has more than DENSE_OPERATOR_ENTRY_LIMIT entries (about 1 300 cells of real size, for every method and model, because the diagnostics are always computed; see the module docstring), raised before anything is built.

error_over_std(result: TensionUncertaintyResult, dict_truth_tensions: dict[tuple[int, int], float]) -> dict[str, float]

The calibration metric used throughout this module: |error| / std, gauge-matched, per interface.

Gauge matching is mandatory (the rule every accuracy comparison in this package follows): only tension ratios are physical, so the inferred tensions are rescaled by the single factor making their mean match the truth's, and the same factor is applied to the interval — an interval is in the same units as the quantity it bounds, so rescaling one without the other would be a units error dressed up as a calibration result.

required

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Validation and benchmarking tools: the unified force-balance operator and mesh checks, on raw mesh arrays.

The unified force-balance operator (the gradient of the capillary energy with respect to the mesh vertices, one column per unknown), its solvers and diagnostics, so that it can be tested and benchmarked within foambryo; the ForceBalance* tension methods are built on it. The test suite compares these functions with an independent reference implementation of the same algorithms (tests/reference/force_balance_reference_implementation.py). These functions check and benchmark an inference; they are not an inference method of their own.

A mesh here is three arrays, (V, F, regions): vertices (nv, 3), triangles (nf, 3) (vertex indices) and the two regions each triangle separates, (nf, 2), the medium being region 0 by default (foambryo.validation.mesh_io); foambryo.validation.force_balance builds and solves the operator on them.

docs.title: constrained_covariance
docs.text:
constrained_covariance(m: NDArray[float64], anchors: list[NDArray[float64]] | NDArray[float64], sigma_f: float) -> NDArray[np.float64]

Covariance of the solve_constrained estimator under i.i.d. force-balance noise.

Model: the vertex force residual M @ beta is not exactly zero but epsilon ~ N(0, sigma_f^2 I), so beta_hat is a constrained generalised-least-squares estimator. Its covariance is the usual GLS covariance projected onto the constraint's null space,

Sigma = sigma_f^2 (H^-1 - H^-1 A^T (A H^-1 A^T)^-1 A H^-1),     H = M^T M,

which is singular along every constraint direction — variance exactly zero in the gauge that was fixed by hand, which is the correct statement: the overall tension scale is a convention, not a measured quantity. This is the error bar that belongs with the KKT solve, and it needs no prior; contrast map_estimate, whose posterior covariance is non-singular only because the prior supplies the missing information.

Honest caveat: geometric noise on a good mesh is correlated between neighbouring vertices, since they share triangles, so an i.i.d. epsilon understates the true uncertainty. Use these as relative, comparable error bars across interfaces, not as calibrated absolute ones.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default m NDArray[float64]

The force-balance operator.

required anchors list[NDArray[float64]] | NDArray[float64]

The same constraint row vectors passed to solve_constrained.

required sigma_f float

Standard deviation of the per-component vertex force residual. residual_noise_scale estimates it from the fit itself.

required

Returns:

Type Description NDArray[float64]

NDArray[np.float64]: Covariance of beta, shape (ncols, ncols).

docs.title: effective_surface_tensions
docs.text:
effective_surface_tensions(m: NDArray[float64], ni: int, nj: int, mean_tension: float = 1.0) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.float64], float]

Ask which surface tensions balance the mesh, fixing nothing but the overall gauge.

This is the surface-tension analogue of the effective-line-tension check (keep the true surface tensions and ask which line tensions balance the mesh), which detects a factor on a subset of interfaces (for example, some line tensions encoded at half their value by the program that generated the mesh) — a defect in the data, not in the inference. Here the harness operator carries no line-tension block (beta = (gamma, p), by design), so the same question is asked of the surface tensions directly: solve

min ||M beta||^2   subject to   mean(gamma) = mean_tension

and compare gamma to nominal. Only ratios are physical, so the constraint is a gauge choice, not a physical input — without it beta = 0 is the trivial minimiser. A comparison of the returned tensions against nominal ones is therefore only meaningful after gauge matching (see foambryo_benchmarks.metrics.effective_tension_ratios in the source repository).

The only constraint imposed is the mean surface tension, because the harness operator has no line block; with a line block, block_anchors gives a constraint for each tension block. nj > 0 is accepted here only so the residual is reported consistently, and the caller is expected to pass nj = 0.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default m NDArray[float64]

The force-balance operator.

required ni int

Number of interfaces (surface-tension columns).

required nj int

Number of junctions (line-tension columns).

required mean_tension float

The gauge: the mean of the returned surface tensions. Defaults to 1.0, matching foambryo.infer_tensions' own convention and the benchmarking-dataset ground truth.

1.0

Returns:

Type Description tuple[NDArray[float64], NDArray[float64], float]

tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.float64], float]: (gamma_eff, p_eff, residual_fraction), where residual_fraction is ||M beta_eff|| / ||M_gamma gamma_eff|| — the force left unbalanced once the tensions themselves are free (rho_free). It is the ratio at the minimiser of ||M beta|| under the gauge, not the minimum of the ratio itself, so it is close to, but not strictly, the lowest value residual_at's rho can take at any given tensions. rho far above it means the nominal tensions are wrong; both being large means the mesh is not an equilibrium of any tensions at all.

docs.title: marginalise_pressures
docs.text:
marginalise_pressures(m: NDArray[float64], ni: int, nj: int = 0) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.float64]]

Eliminate the pressure block in closed form, keeping the tension columns.

For any fixed tensions the pressures that minimise ||M beta||^2 are unique (when M_p has full column rank) and given by p* = -M_p^+ (M_gamma gamma + M_t t). Substituting them back leaves

min ||P_perp [M_gamma | M_t] (gamma, t)||^2,     P_perp = I - M_p M_p^+,

an exactly equivalent problem in the tensions alone — this is block elimination of a quadratic form, not an approximation, so any constraint acting only on the tension columns (the mean-tension gauge) gives the same tensions from the reduced and the joint problem. The test test_marginalised_and_joint_solves_agree in tests/test_force_balance_inference.py checks this numerically.

P_perp is applied through a thin QR factorisation of M_p rather than by forming the 3nv x 3nv projector, which would be a ~9 GB dense array on a 20 000-vertex mesh.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default m NDArray[float64]

The force-balance operator.

required ni int

Number of interfaces (surface-tension columns).

required nj int

Number of junctions (line-tension columns). Defaults to 0, the harness-default operator M = [M_gamma | M_p].

0

Returns:

Type Description tuple[NDArray[float64], NDArray[float64]]

tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.float64]]: (reduced, pressure_map). reduced is P_perp [M_gamma | M_t], shape (3nv, ni + nj); pressure_map recovers the eliminated pressures as p = pressure_map @ (gamma, t), shape (n_cells, ni + nj).

docs.title: residual_at
docs.text:
residual_at(m: NDArray[float64], ni: int, nj: int, gamma: NDArray[float64], t: NDArray[float64]) -> float

Fraction of the surface-tension force left unbalanced once pressures are fitted.

This is the equilibrium residual rho: the norm of the force left over at the given tensions once the best pressures are fitted, relative to the norm of the surface-tension force. With b = M_gamma @ gamma + M_t @ t, the best pressures are p* = -M_p^+ @ b and rho = ||b + M_p @ p*|| / ||M_gamma @ gamma|| = ||P_perp @ b|| / ||M_gamma @ gamma||, with P_perp = I - M_p M_p^+ the projector orthogonal to the pressure column space, computed here via an explicit least-squares fit of the best pressures rather than forming P_perp directly (equivalent, cheaper). rho ~ 0 means the mesh is at equilibrium at the given (gamma, t).

The force-balance operator.

required ni int

Number of interfaces (surface-tension columns).

required nj int

Number of junctions (line-tension columns).

required gamma NDArray[float64]

Surface tensions, shape (ni,).

required t NDArray[float64]

Line tensions, shape (nj,). Pass np.zeros(0) when nj == 0 (the no-line-tension operator).

required

Returns:

Name Type Description float float

rho.

docs.title: check_label_orientation_convention
docs.text:
check_label_orientation_convention(v: NDArray[float64], f: NDArray[int64], regions: NDArray[int64], exterior: int = 0) -> dict

Check that a mesh's triangle winding agrees with its label column order.

foambryo requires each triangle's right-hand-rule normal to point away from its first-listed region and into its second (see foambryo.dcel._normalize_label_order). That tie between winding and label order cannot be checked from the labels — sorted label columns are neither necessary nor sufficient — so this checks its geometric consequence instead: every bounded cell must enclose a positive volume.

Use this once on any mesh from a source other than dw3d (a simulation, a hand-written .rec, or a mesh whose label columns were sorted by a tool that did not reorient the triangles). Without it the failure is silent: compute_volume_cells simply returns negative volumes and everything downstream consumes them.

Assumes a closed mesh. An open or cropped mesh will report non-positive volumes for the cells it truncates, which is a limitation of the check and not a defect in the mesh; n_nonpositive_cells and the returned volumes let a caller judge which case it is looking at.

list_junctions(f: NDArray[int64], regions: NDArray[int64]) -> tuple[list[tuple[int, int, int]], dict[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int, int]]]

Find triple lines: edges carrying three interfaces on exactly three incident triangles.

An edge is admitted as a genuine triple line only under the rule mesh_integrity already documents and enforces as triple_line_ok: three distinct region labels (regions_per_edge == 3), spanning three distinct interfaces (interfaces_per_edge == 3), on exactly three incident triangles (triangles_per_edge == 3) -- not merely three region labels. An edge with three region labels but a fourth (or more) incident triangle is a malformed triple line (mesh_integrity's n_malformed_triple_line_edges), not a genuine one, and is excluded: admitted, it would give a region-triple whose derived interface pair need not be any triangle's actual region pair in the mesh, which junction_graph.partition_by_junction_graph's union-find has no key for (a KeyError).

docs.title: mesh_integrity
docs.text:
mesh_integrity(v: NDArray[float64], f: NDArray[int64], regions: NDArray[int64]) -> dict

Structural integrity report for a multimaterial mesh.

Implements the dataset-integrity check — no dangling vertex references, and every triple line shared by exactly 3 interfaces — and reports the surrounding edge statistics that say how a mesh fails when it does.

intact is deliberately narrow: exactly those two conditions. Everything else (open boundary edges, quadrijunction edges, non-manifold interface edges, degenerate or duplicated triangles) is reported separately, because those are mesh-quality facts rather than integrity failures. In particular quadrijunction edges are expected meshing artifacts, not corruption (in a dry foam exactly three films meet along an edge, so a valence-4 edge is an artifact of discretisation).

Edge terminology, all keyed by the number of distinct region labels appearing on the triangles incident to an edge. This region-label count alone is only a classification, not a validity check: list_junctions uses it to name candidate triple-line edges but, like this function's own n_bad_triple_lines below, only admits one once it also carries three interfaces on exactly three incident triangles (triple_line_ok). A non-manifold edge with three region labels but a fourth incident triangle is malformed, and is left out of the tension system.

  • 1 region: an edge interior to a single interface's triangulation;
  • 2 regions: an interface edge;
  • 3 regions: a triple-line edge — the physical Plateau junction;

  • = 4 regions: a quadrijunction edge.

A triple-line edge spanning regions {a, b, c} must carry all three interfaces (a,b), (a,c), (b,c), one triangle each. Fewer means the junction is malformed: the operator would then assemble a force balance for a junction that is not one.

required f NDArray[int64]

required regions NDArray[int64]

Per-triangle region pair, shape (nf, 2).

required

Returns:

Name Type Description dict dict

Integrity report. intact is True when there is no dangling vertex reference and every triple-line edge carries exactly its three interfaces.

signed_cell_volumes(v: NDArray[float64], f: NDArray[int64], regions: NDArray[int64]) -> dict[int, float]

Divergence-theorem volume per region, with foambryo's sign convention.

Accumulates +det([v0, v1, v2]) / 6 into each triangle's first-listed region and -det(...) / 6 into its second — the same rule as foambryo.geometry.compute_volume_cells, applied to raw arrays so it can be run on a mesh file before building a DcelData.

The result is invariant under DcelData's label-order normalisation (swapping a row's two labels also reverses its winding, which negates det, so the contribution is unchanged), and it was verified equal to DcelData.compute_volumes_cells() on benchmarking-dataset/000_mesh.rec to floating-point precision.

A correctly-wound closed mesh gives a positive volume for every bounded cell and a negative one for the unbounded exterior label, whose faces are all wound inward from its point of view.

docs.title: The Polyscope viewer
docs.text:
The Polyscope viewer: a mesh coloured by its tensions and pressures, in a window with their colour bars.

Sacha Ichbiah 2021 Matthieu Perez 2024

This module needs Polyscope (pip install "foambryo[viewing]"), and its viewers need a display. The colour bars alone are written without either by save_colour_bars (also in foambryo.colour_scales).

The three force viewers (plot_force_inference, plot_tension_inference, plot_pressure_inference) draw the mesh coloured with the library's colour functions (foambryo.colour_scales):

  • tensions: coolwarm (blue for low, light grey for the mean tension, red for high), over a range centred on the mean of the finite tensions and symmetric around it, its half-width the farther of the alpha and 1 - alpha quantiles from the mean;
  • pressures: magma, reversed (light for low) and trimmed to its 10-90 % range, from 0 to the 1 - alpha quantile of the pressures over the surface's triangles;
  • undetermined values (nan): green, #1b9e77 (UNDETERMINED_COLOR). In the tension view an interface whose tension is undetermined is drawn as its outline in this green, without fill; a cell whose pressure is undetermined is filled green;
  • crop faces (where the image box cut the tissue): see-through glass with its edges drawn; they carry no value;
  • other quantities drawn on the surface (a seed spread, the sphere-fit residual, the curvatures) keep jet.

With tensions and pressures, the surface shows the tensions first. The viewers with tensions also draw a graph of the tissue (a node at each cell's centroid, an edge per interface coloured by its tension; with pressures, the nodes coloured by pressure) and, with pressures, each cell's principal stresses. Polyscope's window gets a panel, "foambryo", that shows:

  • the colour bars of what is drawn: the library's colours over the library's ranges (the ones save_colour_bars writes), with a green swatch when a value is undetermined and a glass one for crop faces. Polyscope is handed the colours, not the values: its own scalar colour maps would draw nan in their top colour;
  • which values the colours show: the inference call that produced them (the library's options are the viewers' own, mode_tension, mode_pressure, mean_tension, base_pressure, solver, with the library's defaults), or where they were read from;
  • with tensions and pressures, which one colours the surface (the tensions by default);
  • a length scale bar when the mesh's unit is known (length_unit): a segment of round length in the scene, its length written beside it; and an optional x, y, z frame, three labelled segments along the mesh's columns (z, y, x);
  • the background: white (Polyscope's), light grey, dark grey or black (BACKGROUND_COLOURS, the napari plugin's choices too), or a custom colour; on a dark one, the scale bar, the frame, their labels and the graph's black nodes are drawn light;
  • Explode (the scattered view: each cell moved away from the tissue's centre by a coefficient; the graph's nodes stay on their exploded cells) and Cut (a scene slice plane normal to z, y or x, at a chosen position, keeping either side);
  • Save figure (the view with its colour bars and scale bar, PNG / PDF / SVG), Save colour bars, and Export: foambryo infer's files for the values shown (tensions.csv, pressures.csv, solves.csv, run.json, colour_bars.png), in a folder; a file is never overwritten without asking;
  • a choice of tension method, pressure method or no pressures, solver and diagnostics, Recompute, and the foambryo infer command line that gives the same numbers.

view_mask opens the window on a segmentation mask instead (foambryo view MASK --spacing DZ DY DX): the mask first, then its reconstruction and the inference, run in child processes that the panel follows and can cancel.

save_figure=PATH writes the same figure from Python, without keeping the window open when show=False (Polyscope still needs a display to render the view).

plot_force_inference(mesh: DcelData, dict_tensions: dict[tuple[int, int], float] | None = None, dict_pressure: dict[int, float] | None = None, alpha: float = 0.05, scalar_quantities: bool = False, scattered: bool = False, scatter_coeff: float = DEFAULT_SCATTER_COEFF, *, mean_tension: float = _INFER_FORCES_DEFAULTS['mean_tension'], base_pressure: float = _INFER_FORCES_DEFAULTS['base_pressure'], mode_tension: TensionComputationMethod = _INFER_FORCES_DEFAULTS['mode_tension'], mode_pressure: PressureComputationMethod = _INFER_FORCES_DEFAULTS['mode_pressure'], solver: str = _INFER_FORCES_DEFAULTS['solver'], length_unit: str | None = None, scale_bar: bool | float = True, save_figure: str | PathLike[str] | None = None, show: bool = True, values_from: str | None = None, mesh_file: str | None = None) -> None

Show a mesh's tensions and pressures in Polyscope's window, with their colour bars; what foambryo view opens.

The surface is coloured by the tensions first (coolwarm, centred on the mean tension); the panel switches it to the pressures (reversed magma, trimmed to its 10-90 % range). An undetermined tension (nan) is drawn as its interface's green outline, without fill, and an undetermined pressure fills its cell green; crop faces are see-through glass. The graph of the tissue and each cell's principal stresses are drawn too. The module docstring lists what the panel offers.

Needs Polyscope (pip install "foambryo[viewing]") and a display, also with show=False (Polyscope renders the figure). Returns when the window is closed.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mesh DcelData

the mesh, in its own length unit.

required dict_tensions dict[tuple[int, int], float] | None

tension per interface, keyed (label_1, label_2) with label_1 < label_2 (0 is the medium). Defaults to None: the tensions and the pressures are inferred with infer_forces and the options below.

None dict_pressure dict[int, float] | None

pressure per label, the medium (0) included. Defaults to None: inferred with infer_forces, or, when dict_tensions is given, with infer_pressures from those tensions and the options below.

None alpha float

the quantile clipped at each end of the colour scales, in [0, 0.5): the tension range reaches the farther of the alpha and 1 - alpha quantiles from the mean, the pressure range runs from 0 to the 1 - alpha quantile. Defaults to 0.05.

0.05 scalar_quantities bool

also add the sphere-fit residual, the area and volume derivatives and the curvatures as surface quantities (jet). Defaults to False.

False scattered bool

open the window exploded: each cell moved away from the tissue's centre by scatter_coeff times (its centroid - the tissue's centroid). The panel changes it. Defaults to False.

False scatter_coeff float

the explode coefficient. Defaults to 0.2 (DEFAULT_SCATTER_COEFF).

DEFAULT_SCATTER_COEFF mean_tension float

the mean the tensions are gauged to. Defaults to 1. Keyword-only.

_INFER_FORCES_DEFAULTS['mean_tension'] base_pressure float

the pressure of the medium, label 0. Defaults to 0. Keyword-only.

_INFER_FORCES_DEFAULTS['base_pressure'] mode_tension TensionComputationMethod

the tension method. Defaults to YoungDupre. Keyword-only.

_INFER_FORCES_DEFAULTS['mode_tension'] mode_pressure PressureComputationMethod

the pressure method. Defaults to Variational. Keyword-only.

_INFER_FORCES_DEFAULTS['mode_pressure'] solver str

"auto", "dense" or "sparse". Defaults to "auto". Keyword-only. These five are infer_forces' options, with its defaults, passed to it unchanged when the viewer infers (bitwise foambryo infer's numbers); the panel names the call that produced the colours.

_INFER_FORCES_DEFAULTS['solver'] length_unit str | None

the unit of the mesh's coordinates ("um", ...); with a unit, a length scale bar is drawn. Defaults to None: no scale bar. Keyword-only.

None scale_bar bool | float

draw the scale bar (True, its length 1, 2 or 5 times a power of ten, at most a quarter of the tissue's largest side), not (False), or with this length, in length_unit. Defaults to True. Keyword-only.

True save_figure str | PathLike | None

write the first view, with its colour bars and scale bar, to this file (.png, .pdf, .svg; matplotlib chooses the format from the suffix), before the window is shown. Defaults to None. Keyword-only.

None show bool

open the window; False with save_figure only writes the figure. Defaults to True. Keyword-only.

True values_from str | None

where given values come from, shown in the panel and under a saved figure. Defaults to None. Keyword-only.

None mesh_file str | None

the mesh's file name, for the foambryo infer command line the panel shows for values inferred in the window. Defaults to None (no command line). Keyword-only.

None

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

when the viewer infers and the library refuses the tensions or the pressures (the library's message; UndeterminedTensionError, a ValueError, when the given tensions are not all finite on a mesh without crop faces).

plot_valid_junctions(mesh: DcelData, dict_tensions: dict[tuple[int, int], float] | None = None) -> None

Show in Polyscope's window which triple lines the tensions can balance: green if they can, red if not.

At a triple line between cells a, b and c, three tensions can balance only if each is at most the sum of the other two (they form a triangle). A line where one tension exceeds the sum of the other two is drawn red ("bad trijunctions"), every other line green ("valid trijunctions"), over the mesh drawn white and mostly see-through (opacity 0.1). A line with a crop interface (absent from the tension map) is not judged and is drawn green. When every line is judged and bad, only the red lines are drawn. Used to check an inference. When no line is judged (the mesh has no triple line, or every line has a crop interface), no line is drawn: the window shows the mesh alone, with a UserWarning that says so.

Needs Polyscope (pip install "foambryo[viewing]") and a display. Polyscope's structures are removed first; returns when the window is closed, and removes them then.

docs.title: Wedge refusal
docs.text:
Refusal policies: declining a trijunction observation the mesh's own geometry makes infeasible.

A WedgeRefusal is passed as refusal= to infer_tensions and its relatives, and to infer_tensions_young_dupre_local. Only the methods of foambryo.tension_inference.ANGLE_READING_METHODS honour it; the others raise ValueError on any policy but NO_REFUSAL. refusal_report counts what a policy declines.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
At a trijunctional edge three films meet and the three interior wedge angles sum to a full turn. A reflex wedge is one wider than a straight angle: the surface is locally folded there, the three films do not enclose the edge the way a trijunction requires, and the Young-Dupré balance every angle-reading estimator in this package imposes has no solution for such a triple. Feeding the estimator that row is feeding it an observation that cannot have come from the object being measured.

Two facts make this worth acting on rather than documenting:

  • foambryo.geometry's oriented reading can see the fold — but it cannot undo it. The per-edge estimator's rows are built from cos of the wedge, and cos is even about a full turn, so a reflex wedge and its reflection are literally the same row; no reading reaches it.
  • The log-of-sin estimator does not merely degrade on such a row, it fails: a reflex wedge has a negative oriented sine, and the row's logarithm is not defined.

So the estimator should refuse the observation. This module is the machinery for that, and it is off by default — NO_REFUSAL reproduces every existing number bitwise, and which policy (if any) should become a default is a separate decision taken on its own evidence.

docs.title: The three policies, and the unit each acts on
docs.text:
Every angle-reading estimator here builds its rows from one of two observation units: a whole junction line (the region triple), for the methods that average the wedge angles along the line and weight the row by the line's arclength share; or a single trijunctional edge, for the per-edge method, whose row is one edge. The policies are defined on the unit, so each is one intervention with one meaning in both families:

  • :attr:WedgeRefusalPolicy.ExcludeEdgeFromLineMean (E) — a refused edge contributes neither its angles nor its length to its line. The line keeps its row, computed from the surviving edges and weighted by their surviving arclength. A line that loses every edge has no mean and therefore no row.
  • :attr:WedgeRefusalPolicy.DropLine (D) — a line carrying at least one refused edge loses its row entirely.
  • :attr:WedgeRefusalPolicy.DownweightLine (W) — nothing is removed from the measurement: the line's angle means are what they always were, and only its row weight is scaled, by the fraction of its arclength that is not refused. A line with no unrefused arclength has weight zero, which is the same as having no row.

A refused wedge takes the other two wedges of its own edge with it. The three are one observation of one edge and every row consumes all three; dropping one wedge key and keeping its two partners would leave a line's three means computed over different edge subsets and no longer summing to a full turn.

Two consequences follow from the definitions and are asserted as tests rather than assumed (tests/test_wedge_refusal.py):

  1. For the per-edge method the unit is one edge, so under E a refused edge's unit is empty and it has no row — E and D are the same intervention there and agree exactly. W is not: it keeps the refused rows and scales every row of their line instead.
  2. For the line-averaged methods E and W give a surviving line the same row weight (E's surviving arclength over the surviving total; W's full arclength times the surviving fraction, over that same total). So E and W differ only in the angle a line reports, and D and E only in whether a partly folded line reports at all.

docs.title: Underdetermination is an outcome, not an error
docs.text:
Refusing rows can leave an interface with no surviving junction line at all, or split the junction graph into pieces that no longer share a gauge. That is handled exactly as foambryo.junction_graph already handles a closed interface and a fragmented mesh: the partition is rebuilt over the surviving lines (junction_graph.partition_over_surviving_junctions), an interface touched by no surviving line is reported float("nan") and never a number, a survivor graph in several pieces is normalised in each piece, and JunctionGraphGaugeWarning fires unchanged. A mesh all of whose lines are refused returns every interface undetermined rather than raising: an empty answer is a result, and it is one the caller can count.

Report the refused counts next to any accuracy number. A policy that improves an error statistic by declining a large share of the data has not improved anything, and :func:refusal_report is what makes that visible.

docs.title: Two reasons to decline an edge: a fold, and the crop
docs.text: A junction edge with a vertex on a crop face (foambryo.crop_faces) is not an observation of the tissue either: the tissue beyond the crop was cut away. It is declined for that reason on every cropped mesh, whatever the policy, and always edge by edge: it leaves its line's mean and length, and the rest of the line still reports. The policy then acts on what remains, as if the crop edges were not part of the line: under DropLine a line is dropped when one of its other edges is refused, and under DownweightLine its weight is the unrefused fraction of the arclength that is not on the crop. The two sets are held apart (WedgeRefusal.crop_edges beside the policy's own edges) and counted apart in RefusalReport. On a mesh without crop faces the crop set is empty and nothing here changes.

docs.title: Reading nothing but the mesh
docs.text: :func:reflex_trijunction_edges takes a mesh and a tolerance. There is no parameter through which a reference geometry, a target angle or an expected value could reach it, and the decision is therefore available on data that has no reference at all.

docs.title: WedgeRefusalPolicy
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

Which observations an angle-reading estimator declines, and how. See the module docstring.

  • NoRefusal: the default. Nothing is declined and every result is bitwise what it was before this module existed.
  • ExcludeEdgeFromLineMean: a refused edge leaves its line's angle mean and its line's length; the line still reports, from what survives.
  • DropLine: a line carrying any refused edge does not report at all.
  • DownweightLine: every line reports its unchanged mean, with its row weight scaled by the fraction of its arclength that is not refused.

docs.title: Anisotropic voxels
docs.text:
A mask whose voxels are longer along z: give the spacing, and the mask is resampled to cubic voxels first.

A microscope stack usually has a z step larger than its pixel size. This example builds a foam of Voronoi cells on cubic voxels of 0.5 um, keeps every second z slice (voxels of 1.0 x 0.5 x 0.5 um, an anisotropy of 2), and shows what giving the spacing changes:

  • the estimate of the reconstruction's time and memory counts the voxels after resampling (twice as many);
  • dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask, spacing=(1.0, 0.5, 0.5)) resamples the mask to cubic voxels of 0.5 um by shape-based interpolation, meshes it, and returns the mesh in um; mesh.source_spacing records the spacing, and so does the .rec file that reconstruct_mask writes (the foambryo mesh route);
  • the cells' volumes, in um^3, agree with their voxel counts times the voxel volume;
  • without the spacing, the same stack is meshed in voxel units and squashed along z: every volume is half what it should be, and every contact angle is read on a deformed tissue.

The accuracy gain of resampling first is measured, not shown here: on 12 simulated tissues at equilibrium with cells as small as those of real tissues, down-sampled along z, the contact-angle error grew by +0.83, +0.71 and +1.17 degrees at an anisotropy of 5/3, 2 and 3 when the mask is resampled first, against +1.38, +1.97 and +4.10 when the native grid is meshed and the mesh scaled afterwards (each against the same tissue meshed at full resolution; see BENCHMARKS.md). One small example cannot show a difference of a degree: its own seed-to-seed spread is larger.

pip install "foambryo[viewing]"          # matplotlib, for the figure
python anisotropic_voxels.py             # under a minute; writes ./anisotropic-voxels-output/

The script: Examples/anisotropic_voxels.py. It needs only foambryo (and matplotlib, from foambryo[viewing], for its figure); it generates its own tissue.

One xz section of the generated stack (voxels 1.0 x 0.5 um) and of its resampling to cubic voxels of 0.5 um; colour = cell label.

docs.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""A mask whose voxels are longer along z: give the spacing, and the mask is resampled to cubic voxels first.

A microscope stack usually has a z step larger than its pixel size. This example builds a foam of Voronoi cells on
cubic voxels of 0.5 um, keeps every second z slice (voxels of 1.0 x 0.5 x 0.5 um, an anisotropy of 2), and shows
what giving the spacing changes:

* the estimate of the reconstruction's time and memory counts the voxels **after** resampling (twice as many);
* `dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask, spacing=(1.0, 0.5, 0.5))` resamples the mask to cubic voxels of 0.5 um
  by shape-based interpolation, meshes it, and returns the mesh **in um**; `mesh.source_spacing` records the
  spacing, and so does the `.rec` file that `reconstruct_mask` writes (the `foambryo mesh` route);
* the cells' volumes, in um^3, agree with their voxel counts times the voxel volume;
* without the spacing, the same stack is meshed in voxel units and squashed along z: every volume is half what it
  should be, and every contact angle is read on a deformed tissue.

The accuracy gain of resampling first is measured, not shown here: on 12 simulated tissues at equilibrium with cells
as small as those of real tissues, down-sampled along z, the contact-angle error grew by +0.83, +0.71 and +1.17
degrees at an anisotropy of 5/3, 2 and 3 when the mask is resampled first, against +1.38, +1.97 and +4.10 when the
native grid is meshed and the mesh scaled afterwards (each against the same tissue meshed at full resolution; see
BENCHMARKS.md). One small example cannot show a difference of a degree: its own seed-to-seed spread is larger.

    pip install "foambryo[viewing]"          # matplotlib, for the figure
    python anisotropic_voxels.py             # under a minute; writes ./anisotropic-voxels-output/
"""

import argparse
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from dw3d import resample_to_isotropic
from dw3d.io import load_rec_appendix
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

from foambryo import dcel_mesh_from_file, dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask, infer_tensions, reconstruct_mask
from foambryo.reconstruction_cost import estimate_reconstruction_cost, voxels_handed_to_dw3d

VOXEL_UM = 0.5  # the cubic voxels the foam is generated on


def generated_foam(n: int = 96, n_cells: int = 12, seed: int = 7) -> np.ndarray:
    """Voronoi cells filling a ball, on an `n`^3 grid of cubic voxels; label 0 is the medium."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    radius, centre = 0.46 * n, (n - 1) / 2
    seeds: list[np.ndarray] = []
    while len(seeds) < n_cells:  # well-separated seeds inside the ball
        point = rng.uniform(-0.75 * radius, 0.75 * radius, 3)
        if np.linalg.norm(point) < 0.75 * radius and all(np.linalg.norm(point - s) > 0.35 * radius for s in seeds):
            seeds.append(point)
    grid = np.indices((n, n, n)).reshape(3, -1).T.astype(float)
    _, nearest = cKDTree(np.asarray(seeds) + centre).query(grid)
    inside = np.linalg.norm(grid - centre, axis=1) <= radius
    return np.where(inside, nearest + 1, 0).reshape(n, n, n).astype(np.uint16)


def volume_ratios(mesh: object, mask: np.ndarray, voxel_volume: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Each cell's mesh volume divided by its voxel count times the voxel volume (1 when the units agree)."""
    volumes = mesh.compute_volumes_cells()
    labels, counts = np.unique(mask[mask > 0], return_counts=True)
    return np.array([volumes[int(k)] / (c * voxel_volume) for k, c in zip(labels, counts, strict=True)])


def main() -> None:
    """Mesh the stack with and without its spacing, write its .rec file, and draw the resampling."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=Path("anisotropic-voxels-output"))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    stack = generated_foam()[::2]  # every second z slice: voxels twice as long along z
    spacing = (2 * VOXEL_UM, VOXEL_UM, VOXEL_UM)  # (dz, dy, dx) in um: axis 0 of the mask is z
    print(f"the stack: shape {stack.shape}, {len(np.unique(stack)) - 1} cells, spacing {spacing} um")

    voxels = voxels_handed_to_dw3d(stack.shape, spacing)
    estimate = estimate_reconstruction_cost(voxels)
    print(f"voxels handed to the reconstruction: {voxels:.3g} (the stack has {stack.size:.3g}); estimated "
          f"{estimate.seconds[1]:.1f} s and {estimate.peak_gib[1]:.2f} GiB (fitted on tissues of 2 to 1 866 cells)")

    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        mesh = dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(stack, spacing=spacing)
    for warning in caught:
        if issubclass(warning.category, DeprecationWarning):
            continue  # notices about the libraries' own internals
        print(f"  {warning.category.__name__}: {str(warning.message)[:110]}")
    extent = mesh.v.max(axis=0) - mesh.v.min(axis=0)
    print(f"with spacing: mesh in um, extent (z, y, x) = {np.round(extent, 1)}, source_spacing {mesh.source_spacing}")
    ratios = volume_ratios(mesh, stack, voxel_volume=float(np.prod(spacing)))
    print(f"  cell volume / (voxels x voxel volume): median {np.median(ratios):.3f}")

    squashed = dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(stack)  # no spacing: voxel units, z not scaled
    extent = squashed.v.max(axis=0) - squashed.v.min(axis=0)
    ratios = volume_ratios(squashed, stack, voxel_volume=float(np.prod(spacing)) / VOXEL_UM**3)
    print(f"without spacing: mesh in voxels, extent (z, y, x) = {np.round(extent, 1)}: the tissue is squashed along z;"
          f"\n  cell volume / (voxels x true voxel volume): median {np.median(ratios):.3f}")

    # The `foambryo mesh` route: the same mesh, written as a .rec file that records its frame and spacing.
    reconstruction = reconstruct_mask(stack, spacing, spacing_unit="um")
    rec = args.output_dir / "stack.rec"
    reconstruction.write_rec(rec)
    appendix = load_rec_appendix(rec)
    print(f"{rec}: {reconstruction.summary()}; recorded "
          f"{ {k: appendix[k] for k in ('coordinate_frame', 'spacing', 'spacing_unit', 'resampling')} }")
    read_back = dcel_mesh_from_file(rec)
    print(f"  read back: source_spacing {read_back.source_spacing}")

    tensions = infer_tensions(mesh)
    print(f"tensions of {len(tensions)} interfaces, mean {np.nanmean(list(tensions.values())):.3f} (normalised to 1)")

    try:
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    except ImportError:
        print("matplotlib is not installed: no figure (pip install 'foambryo[viewing]')")
        return
    resampled = resample_to_isotropic(stack, spacing)
    figure, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 4.4))
    for axis, (title, image, aspect) in zip(axes, (
        ("the stack: voxels 1.0 x 0.5 um (z, x)", stack[:, stack.shape[1] // 2, :], 2.0),
        ("resampled to cubic voxels of 0.5 um", resampled[:, resampled.shape[1] // 2, :], 1.0),
    ), strict=True):
        colours = plt.get_cmap("tab20").with_extremes(bad="white")  # the medium, label 0, in white
        axis.imshow(np.ma.masked_equal(image, 0), cmap=colours, interpolation="nearest", aspect=aspect,
                    origin="lower")
        axis.set(title=title, xlabel="x (voxels)", ylabel="z (voxels)")
    figure.suptitle("A generated foam (12 cells), one xz section through its middle; colour = cell label")
    figure.tight_layout()
    figure.savefig(args.output_dir / "stack_and_its_resampling.png", dpi=150)
    print(f"figure: {args.output_dir / 'stack_and_its_resampling.png'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: The script
docs.text:
#!/bin/sh
# The foambryo command, from a mask to the figures, on a synthetic mask whose answer is known.
#
#     pip install "foambryo[viewing]"
#     sh command_line_example.sh
#
# Everything is written into ./foambryo-command-example/. The mask is a doublet at equilibrium: two
# equal spheres of radius R = 30 voxels whose centres are R apart, split by the plane between them,
# so that the three surfaces meet at 120 degrees. All three tensions are then equal (1, with the
# default mean tension of 1) and each cell's pressure is 2 / R = 0.133 per um on voxels of 0.5 um
# (R = 15 um). The inferred values come within about 10 % of these: the gap is the cost of
# meshing a voxel mask at this size.
#
# The steps:
#   1. foambryo mesh             the mask's mesh, in um (a .npz that records its voxel size; then a
#                                stack with voxels twice as long along z, whose size is given with --spacing)
#   2. foambryo infer            tensions.csv, pressures.csv, run.json, and solves.csv with --diagnostics
#   3. foambryo infer --no-pressures   the tensions only
#   4. foambryo view             the colour bars without a window (--colour-bars, --no-show), and the
#                                view itself as a figure (--figure; needs Polyscope and a display)
#   5. foambryo infer-over-seeds the tensions over eight reconstructions, with their spread
set -e
mkdir -p foambryo-command-example
cd foambryo-command-example

python - <<'EOF'
import numpy as np

n, radius = 102, 30
z, y, x = np.indices((n, n, n))
c = (n - 1) / 2
left = (z - c) ** 2 + (y - c) ** 2 + (x - (c - radius / 2)) ** 2 <= radius**2
right = (z - c) ** 2 + (y - c) ** 2 + (x - (c + radius / 2)) ** 2 <= radius**2
mask = np.where(left | right, np.where(x < c, 1, 2), 0).astype(np.uint16)
np.savez("doublet.npz", mask=mask, spacing=np.array([0.5, 0.5, 0.5]), spacing_unit=np.array("um"))
np.save("doublet_every_second_z_slice.npy", mask[::2])  # no voxel size in the file
EOF

# 1. The .npz records its spacing, so --spacing is not needed. The .npy records none: --spacing is
#    required (there is no default), and a stack with longer voxels along z is resampled to cubic
#    voxels before meshing (a message says so).
foambryo mesh doublet.npz -o doublet.rec --overwrite
foambryo mesh doublet_every_second_z_slice.npy --spacing 1.0 0.5 0.5 --spacing-unit um \
    -o doublet_from_the_stack.rec --overwrite

# 2. Tensions and pressures, with the defaults of the library (bit for bit those of infer_forces),
#    and one row per linear solve in solves.csv.
foambryo infer doublet.rec -o results --diagnostics basic --overwrite

# 3. The tensions only (no pressures.csv; run.json says the pressures were not computed).
foambryo infer doublet_from_the_stack.rec -o results-tensions-only --no-pressures --overwrite

# 4. The colour bars need neither a display nor Polyscope. The figure (the view with its colour bars
#    and length scale bar) needs both; without a display, this step says so and the script goes on.
foambryo view doublet.rec --results results --colour-bars results/colour_bars.png --no-show
foambryo view doublet.rec --results results --figure results/figure.png --no-show \
    || echo "no figure: 'foambryo view --figure' needs Polyscope and a display"

# 5. The same mask reconstructed at the dither seeds 0 to 7, and the tensions averaged over them:
#    tensions.csv gains the spread over the seeds, and tensions_per_seed.csv holds each seed's own
#    values. The spread is a lower bound on the error, not an error bar.
foambryo infer-over-seeds doublet.npz -o results-over-seeds --seeds 8 --overwrite

cat results/tensions.csv
cat results/pressures.csv
cat results/solves.csv
cat results-tensions-only/tensions.csv
cat results-over-seeds/tensions.csv

# To look at the tissue in the window (needs a display):
#     foambryo view doublet.rec --results results
# or start from the mask, and reconstruct and infer in the window:
#     foambryo view doublet.npz

docs.title: Cropped tissue
docs.text:
A tissue the image cuts: crop faces, cut cells, nan pressures, and a pressure method that refuses.

When a cell of the mask reaches a face of the image box, the mesh closes it with triangles on that face. They are not contact with the medium: the tissue goes on beyond the image. delaunay-watershed-3d marks them as crop faces, and foambryo keeps them out of every equation:

  • the tensions are inferred from the junctions the image shows; an interface made only of crop faces is absent;
  • the pressures of the cut cells (the cells the crop cuts) are nan, with a CutCellPressureWarning, because part of their surface and volume was not observed;
  • the Laplace pressure methods have no formulation for crop faces and raise ValueError on a cropped mesh (PressureComputationMethod.has_crop_face_formulation says which methods accept one: only Variational).

This example builds a foam of Voronoi cells, cuts away a third of it along x, and runs the inference on the cut mask. The foam is not at mechanical equilibrium: its tensions show the workflow, not the method's accuracy. (On 433 plane crops of 47 simulated tissues at equilibrium, the tensions of the interfaces next to the crop had 13 %, 33 % and 40 % error with 10 %, 25 % and 40 % of the tissue cut away when crop faces were read as medium contact, and 10 %, 9 % and 12 % with crop faces kept out.)

If the tissue really ends on a face of the image (for example on a coverslip), declare that face physical: dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask, physical_image_faces=("axis2_low",)); its triangles are then contact with the medium.

pip install "foambryo[viewing]"          # matplotlib, for the figure
python cropped_tissue.py                 # under a minute; writes ./cropped-tissue-output/

The script: Examples/cropped_tissue.py. It needs only foambryo (and matplotlib, from foambryo[viewing], for its figure); it generates its own tissue.

The middle z section of the generated foam: the image box starts at the black line; the cut cells, whose pressures are nan, in red.

docs.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""A tissue the image cuts: crop faces, cut cells, `nan` pressures, and a pressure method that refuses.

When a cell of the mask reaches a face of the image box, the mesh closes it with triangles on that face. They are
not contact with the medium: the tissue goes on beyond the image. delaunay-watershed-3d marks them as **crop
faces**, and foambryo keeps them out of every equation:

* the tensions are inferred from the junctions the image shows; an interface made only of crop faces is absent;
* the pressures of the **cut cells** (the cells the crop cuts) are `nan`, with a `CutCellPressureWarning`, because
  part of their surface and volume was not observed;
* the Laplace pressure methods have no formulation for crop faces and raise `ValueError` on a cropped mesh
  (`PressureComputationMethod.has_crop_face_formulation` says which methods accept one: only `Variational`).

This example builds a foam of Voronoi cells, cuts away a third of it along x, and runs the inference on the cut
mask. The foam is not at mechanical equilibrium: its tensions show the workflow, not the method's accuracy. (On 433
plane crops of 47 simulated tissues at equilibrium, the tensions of the interfaces next to the crop had 13 %, 33 %
and 40 % error with 10 %, 25 % and 40 % of the tissue cut away when crop faces were read as medium contact, and 10 %,
9 % and 12 % with crop faces kept out.)

If the tissue really ends on a face of the image (for example on a coverslip), declare that face physical:
`dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask, physical_image_faces=("axis2_low",))`; its triangles are then contact with
the medium.

    pip install "foambryo[viewing]"          # matplotlib, for the figure
    python cropped_tissue.py                 # under a minute; writes ./cropped-tissue-output/
"""

import argparse
import warnings
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

from foambryo import (
    CutCellPressureWarning,
    PressureComputationMethod,
    dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask,
    infer_pressures,
    infer_tensions,
)


def generated_foam(n: int = 96, n_cells: int = 12, seed: int = 7) -> np.ndarray:
    """Voronoi cells filling a ball, on an `n`^3 grid of cubic voxels; label 0 is the medium."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    radius, centre = 0.46 * n, (n - 1) / 2
    seeds: list[np.ndarray] = []
    while len(seeds) < n_cells:  # well-separated seeds inside the ball
        point = rng.uniform(-0.75 * radius, 0.75 * radius, 3)
        if np.linalg.norm(point) < 0.75 * radius and all(np.linalg.norm(point - s) > 0.35 * radius for s in seeds):
            seeds.append(point)
    grid = np.indices((n, n, n)).reshape(3, -1).T.astype(float)
    _, nearest = cKDTree(np.asarray(seeds) + centre).query(grid)
    inside = np.linalg.norm(grid - centre, axis=1) <= radius
    return np.where(inside, nearest + 1, 0).reshape(n, n, n).astype(np.uint16)


def main() -> None:
    """Cut a foam, infer its tensions and pressures, and show what a cropped mesh refuses."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=Path("cropped-tissue-output"))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    foam = generated_foam()
    cut_at = foam.shape[2] // 3
    mask = foam[:, :, cut_at:]  # the image box starts a third of the way into the tissue, along x
    print(f"the cut mask: shape {mask.shape}, {len(np.unique(mask)) - 1} cells")

    mesh = dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask)
    print(f"{int(mesh.crop_faces.sum())} crop faces of {len(mesh.f)} triangles; cut cells {mesh.cut_cells}; "
          f"interfaces made only of crop faces: {mesh.crop_interfaces}")

    tensions = infer_tensions(mesh)
    crop_interface_kept = any(k in tensions for k in mesh.crop_interfaces)
    print(f"{len(tensions)} tensions; any crop interface among them: {crop_interface_kept}")

    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter("always", CutCellPressureWarning)
        pressures = infer_pressures(mesh, tensions)  # Variational, the default
    for warning in caught:
        if issubclass(warning.category, CutCellPressureWarning):
            print(f"CutCellPressureWarning: {str(warning.message)[:120]}")
    reported = {c: p for c, p in pressures.items() if c != 0 and np.isfinite(p)}
    print(f"pressures: {len(reported)} cells reported, {sum(np.isnan(p) for p in pressures.values())} nan "
          f"(the cut cells)")

    for method in PressureComputationMethod:
        print(f"  {method.name:16s} has a formulation for crop faces: {method.has_crop_face_formulation}")
    try:
        infer_pressures(mesh, tensions, mode=PressureComputationMethod.Laplace)
    except ValueError as error:
        print(f"Laplace on a cropped mesh refuses: {error}")

    coverslip = dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask, physical_image_faces=("axis2_low",))
    print(f"with the cut face declared physical (a coverslip): {int(coverslip.crop_faces.sum())} crop faces, "
          f"cut cells {coverslip.cut_cells}")

    try:
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap
    except ImportError:
        print("matplotlib is not installed: no figure (pip install 'foambryo[viewing]')")
        return
    section = foam[foam.shape[0] // 2]
    status = np.zeros(section.shape)  # 0 medium, 1 an uncut cell, 2 a cut cell, 3 outside the image
    status[section > 0] = 1
    status[np.isin(section, mesh.cut_cells)] = 2
    status[:, :cut_at] = np.where(section[:, :cut_at] > 0, 3, 0)
    figure, axis = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 4.6))
    axis.imshow(status, cmap=ListedColormap(["white", "#9ecae1", "#de2d26", "#d9d9d9"]), interpolation="nearest",
                origin="lower", vmin=0, vmax=3)
    axis.axvline(cut_at - 0.5, color="black", linewidth=1.2)
    axis.set_title("Mid z section; the image box starts at the black line.\nRed: cut cells (pressure nan). "
                   "Blue: pressure reported.\nGrey: not imaged.", fontsize=10)
    axis.set(xlabel="x (voxels)", ylabel="y (voxels)")
    figure.tight_layout()
    figure.savefig(args.output_dir / "cut_cells_in_a_section.png", dpi=150)
    print(f"figure: {args.output_dir / 'cut_cells_in_a_section.png'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: What junction relocation changes
docs.text:
Since delaunay-watershed-3d 0.5.0, every reconstruction moves the trijunction vertices onto the junction curves the mask gives. Examples/default_junction_relocation.py reconstructs a label image twice, with and without the relocation, infers the tensions of both meshes and draws the junction line the relocation moved most. Run it on your own label image (medium 0); it needs scikit-image to read it:

python Examples/default_junction_relocation.py path/to/labels.tif --out junction.png

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""What dw3d 0.5.0's default junction relocation changes in the tensions foambryo infers.

Since `delaunay-watershed-3d` 0.5.0 every reconstruction moves the finished mesh's trijunction
vertices onto the trijunction curves the segmentation mask itself gives (triangles and labels are
untouched). This example reconstructs one timepoint twice -- with the default and with
`relocate_junctions = False`, the 0.4 behaviour -- infers Young-Dupre tensions on both meshes, and
draws the trijunction line the relocation moved most, beside the mask's own curve, with the three
tensions that meet there before and after.

Run it on your own label image (exterior `0`), for example one timepoint of a time series::

    python Examples/default_junction_relocation.py path/to/labels.tif --out junction.png

Needs `foambryo`, `delaunay-watershed-3d>=0.5.0` and, for the figure, `matplotlib`.
Tensions are relative (the gauge is fixed by the solver's own normalisation), so compare the two
columns, not the absolute values.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

import numpy as np
import skimage.io as io
from dw3d import extract_junction_curves, get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm
from dw3d.junction_curves import mesh_trijunction_components

from foambryo import TensionComputationMethod, infer_tensions
from foambryo.dcel import DcelData


def reconstruct(mask: np.ndarray, min_distance: int, relocate: bool) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """dw3d's default reconstruction, with junction relocation set explicitly."""
    algorithm = get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm(min_distance=min_distance)
    algorithm.relocate_junctions = relocate
    return algorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask)


def shared_limits(point_sets: list[np.ndarray], margin: float = 1.0) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
    """One (low, high) per axis covering every point set, padded to a cube so both panels match."""
    everything = np.vstack(point_sets)
    low, high = everything.min(axis=0) - margin, everything.max(axis=0) + margin
    half = (high - low).max() / 2
    centre = (high + low) / 2
    return [(c - half, c + half) for c in centre]


def main() -> None:
    """Reconstruct twice, infer tensions twice, print and draw one junction."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("mask", help="label image, exterior 0")
    parser.add_argument("--min-distance", type=int, default=3)
    parser.add_argument("--out", default="default_junction_relocation.png")
    arguments = parser.parse_args()
    mask = io.imread(arguments.mask)

    points, triangles, labels = reconstruct(mask, arguments.min_distance, relocate=True)
    base_points, base_triangles, base_labels = reconstruct(mask, arguments.min_distance, relocate=False)
    assert np.array_equal(triangles, base_triangles), "relocation must not change connectivity"
    assert np.array_equal(labels, base_labels), "relocation must not change labels"

    # One tension per interface, keyed by the (smaller, larger) label pair.
    tensions = infer_tensions(DcelData(points, triangles, labels), 1, TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre)
    base_tensions = infer_tensions(
        DcelData(base_points, base_triangles, base_labels), 1, TensionComputationMethod.YoungDupre,
    )

    # The trijunction line the relocation moved most, among lines with one mesh counterpart.
    curves = extract_junction_curves(mask, base_points, base_triangles, base_labels)
    components = mesh_trijunction_components(base_points, base_triangles, base_labels)
    best = None
    for curve in curves.matched:
        parts = components.get(tuple(int(x) for x in curve.triple), [])
        if len(parts) != 1 or len(parts[0]["vertices"]) < 6:
            continue
        vertices = parts[0]["vertices"]
        moved_by = float(np.median(np.linalg.norm(points[vertices] - base_points[vertices], axis=1)))
        if best is None or moved_by > best[0]:
            best = (moved_by, curve, parts[0])
    moved_by, curve, line = best
    a, b, c = (int(x) for x in curve.triple)
    print(f"trijunction ({a}, {b}, {c}): median vertex displacement {moved_by:.2f} voxels")
    print(f"{'interface':>12}  {'relocation off':>14}  {'default':>10}")
    for pair in ((a, b), (a, c), (b, c)):
        before, after = base_tensions.get(pair, float("nan")), tensions.get(pair, float("nan"))
        print(f"{pair!s:>12}  {before:>14.4f}  {after:>10.4f}")

    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # optional dependency, only for the figure

    # Both panels share one set of limits and ticks, so the two lines can be compared by eye.
    vertices = line["vertices"]
    limits = shared_limits([base_points[vertices], points[vertices], curve.points])
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4.5))
    for panel, (mesh_points, title) in enumerate(((base_points, "relocate_junctions=False (0.4)"),
                                                  (points, "default (dw3d 0.5.0)"))):
        ax = fig.add_subplot(1, 2, panel + 1, projection="3d")
        ax.set_xlim(*limits[0])
        ax.set_ylim(*limits[1])
        ax.set_zlim(*limits[2])
        for axis, (low, high) in zip((ax.xaxis, ax.yaxis, ax.zaxis), limits, strict=True):
            axis.set_ticks(np.linspace(low, high, 5).round(1))
        for v1, v2 in line["edges"]:
            ax.plot(*np.stack([mesh_points[v1], mesh_points[v2]]).T, color="k", linewidth=2)
        ax.plot(*curve.points.T, color="tab:red", linestyle="--", label="mask trijunction curve")
        ax.set_title(title)
        ax.set_xlabel("x (voxels)")
        ax.set_ylabel("y (voxels)")
        ax.set_zlabel("z (voxels)")
    ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(arguments.out, dpi=120)
    print(f"saved {arguments.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.text:
A large tissue: the cost estimate, the sparse solves, and the table of every linear solve.

Every tension and pressure foambryo infers is the solution of a linear least-squares system. Small systems are solved densely, exactly; a dense system grows as the product of its dimensions in memory and as their cube in time, so solver="auto" (the default) solves a system sparsely from sparse_threshold unknowns on (2 000 by default). This example generates a foam of several hundred Voronoi cells, and:

  1. estimates the reconstruction's time and memory before running it (foambryo.reconstruction_cost: power laws fitted on one machine to medians over the benchmark tissues of 2 to 10 cells and to single tissues of 90 to 1 866 cells; the band is the fit's, not a guarantee);
  2. reconstructs the mesh and infers tensions and pressures with diagnostics=True, which returns one record per linear solve (the solver used, the system's size, rank, residual, condition number, time). It calls infer_tensions_then_pressures, the two calls of infer_forces made one after the other, as foambryo infer does: if an interface has no triple line, its tension is undetermined (nan), the pressure solve refuses, and the tensions are kept instead of lost;
  3. writes them as solves.csv, the table foambryo infer --diagnostics basic writes (from a direct call with diagnostics=True, save_solve_diagnostics writes the same records as JSON and NPZ files);
  4. solves the tensions again with the dense and with the sparse solver forced, and compares them.

The foam is not at mechanical equilibrium: its tensions show the workflow and the solvers, not the method's accuracy. On a 1 866-cell tissue the sparse and dense tensions agree to 1.5e-11 of their scale and the pressures to 1e-11; the dense solve took 6 to 9 minutes and 14-18 GiB there, the sparse one 9 s and 1 GiB.

python large_tissue_solvers.py                # about a minute and 5 GiB; writes ./large-tissue-output/
python large_tissue_solvers.py --cells 300    # smaller and faster

The script: Examples/large_tissue_solvers.py. It needs only foambryo; it generates its own tissue.

docs.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""A large tissue: the cost estimate, the sparse solves, and the table of every linear solve.

Every tension and pressure foambryo infers is the solution of a linear least-squares system. Small systems are
solved densely, exactly; a dense system grows as the product of its dimensions in memory and as their cube in time,
so `solver="auto"` (the default) solves a system sparsely from `sparse_threshold` unknowns on (2 000 by default).
This example generates a foam of several hundred Voronoi cells, and:

1. estimates the reconstruction's time and memory before running it (`foambryo.reconstruction_cost`: power laws
   fitted on one machine to medians over the benchmark tissues of 2 to 10 cells and to single tissues of 90 to
   1 866 cells; the band is the fit's, not a guarantee);
2. reconstructs the mesh and infers tensions and pressures with `diagnostics=True`, which returns one record per
   linear solve (the solver used, the system's size, rank, residual, condition number, time). It calls
   `infer_tensions_then_pressures`, the two calls of `infer_forces` made one after the other, as `foambryo infer`
   does: if an interface has no triple line, its tension is undetermined (`nan`), the pressure solve refuses, and
   the tensions are kept instead of lost;
3. writes them as `solves.csv`, the table `foambryo infer --diagnostics basic` writes (from a direct call with
   `diagnostics=True`, `save_solve_diagnostics` writes the same records as JSON and NPZ files);
4. solves the tensions again with the dense and with the sparse solver forced, and compares them.

The foam is not at mechanical equilibrium: its tensions show the workflow and the solvers, not the method's
accuracy. On a 1 866-cell tissue the sparse and dense tensions agree to 1.5e-11 of their scale and the pressures to
1e-11; the dense solve took 6 to 9 minutes and 14-18 GiB there, the sparse one 9 s and 1 GiB.

    python large_tissue_solvers.py                # about a minute and 5 GiB; writes ./large-tissue-output/
    python large_tissue_solvers.py --cells 300    # smaller and faster
"""

import argparse
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree

from foambryo import (
    PressureComputationMethod,
    dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask,
    infer_tensions,
    infer_tensions_then_pressures,
)
from foambryo.reconstruction_cost import estimate_reconstruction_cost, voxels_handed_to_dw3d
from foambryo.results import write_solve_table


def generated_foam(n_cells: int, cell_radius: float = 12.0, seed: int = 3) -> np.ndarray:
    """About `n_cells` Voronoi cells of radius ~`cell_radius` voxels filling a ball; label 0 is the medium."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    radius = cell_radius * n_cells ** (1 / 3) * 1.05
    n = int(2 * radius) + 8
    centre = (n - 1) / 2
    candidates = rng.uniform(-radius, radius, (40 * n_cells, 3))
    candidates = candidates[np.linalg.norm(candidates, axis=1) < radius - 0.6 * cell_radius]
    seeds: list[np.ndarray] = []
    for point in candidates:  # a simple dart throw: seeds at least 1.4 cell radii apart
        if len(seeds) == n_cells:
            break
        if not seeds or np.min(np.linalg.norm(np.asarray(seeds) - point, axis=1)) > 1.4 * cell_radius:
            seeds.append(point)
    grid = np.indices((n, n, n)).reshape(3, -1).T.astype(float)
    _, nearest = cKDTree(np.asarray(seeds) + centre).query(grid)
    inside = np.linalg.norm(grid - centre, axis=1) <= radius
    return np.where(inside, nearest + 1, 0).reshape(n, n, n).astype(np.uint32)


def scale_relative_difference(a: dict, b: dict) -> float:
    """The largest |a - b| over the shared finite values, relative to the largest |b| (the solution's scale)."""
    keys = [k for k in a if k in b and np.isfinite(a[k]) and np.isfinite(b[k])]
    return max(abs(a[k] - b[k]) for k in keys) / max(abs(b[k]) for k in keys)


def main() -> None:
    """Estimate, reconstruct, infer with diagnostics, and compare the dense and sparse solves."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--cells", type=int, default=600)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=Path("large-tissue-output"))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    started = time.perf_counter()
    mask = generated_foam(args.cells)
    n_cells = len(np.unique(mask)) - 1
    print(f"generated foam: shape {mask.shape}, {n_cells} cells, {time.perf_counter() - started:.0f} s")

    estimate = estimate_reconstruction_cost(voxels_handed_to_dw3d(mask.shape, (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)))
    print(f"estimated reconstruction: {estimate.seconds[1]:.0f} s ({estimate.seconds[0]:.0f}-{estimate.seconds[2]:.0f})"
          f", {estimate.peak_gib[1]:.1f} GiB ({estimate.peak_gib[0]:.1f}-{estimate.peak_gib[2]:.1f})")
    started = time.perf_counter()
    mesh = dcel_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask)
    print(f"reconstructed: {len(mesh.v)} vertices, {len(mesh.f)} triangles, {time.perf_counter() - started:.0f} s")

    started = time.perf_counter()
    outcome = infer_tensions_then_pressures(
        mesh, mode_pressure=PressureComputationMethod.WeightedLaplace, diagnostics=True,
    )
    undetermined = sum(not np.isfinite(t) for t in outcome.tensions.values())
    print(f"{outcome.library_call}: {outcome.status}, {time.perf_counter() - started:.1f} s; "
          f"{len(outcome.tensions)} tensions ({undetermined} undetermined), "
          f"{'no' if outcome.pressures is None else len(outcome.pressures)} pressures")
    if outcome.error:
        print(f"  {outcome.error[:160]}...")
    print(f"  {'system':48s} {'solver':22s} {'rows':>7s} {'unknowns':>8s} {'condition':>10s} {'seconds':>8s}")
    for record in outcome.records:
        condition = f"{record.condition_number:.3g}" if record.condition_number is not None else "-"
        print(f"  {record.system[:48]:48s} {record.solver[:22]:22s} {record.n_rows:7d} {record.n_unknowns:8d} "
              f"{condition:>10s} {record.seconds:8.2f}")
    write_solve_table(args.output_dir / "solves.csv", outcome.records)
    print(f"wrote {args.output_dir / 'solves.csv'}")

    timings = {}
    solutions = {}
    for solver in ("dense", "sparse"):
        started = time.perf_counter()
        solutions[solver] = infer_tensions(mesh, solver=solver)
        timings[solver] = time.perf_counter() - started
    print(f"tensions, dense solve {timings['dense']:.1f} s, sparse solve {timings['sparse']:.1f} s; they differ by "
          f"{scale_relative_difference(solutions['sparse'], solutions['dense']):.1e} of the tensions' scale")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: The Polyscope viewer from Python
docs.text:
The Polyscope viewer from Python: tensions and pressures on the tissue, saved figures, and a seed ensemble.

foambryo's viewer draws the mesh coloured by the inferred values, with a panel that shows their colour bars, which call produced them, a length scale bar, and controls to explode and cut the tissue, change the methods and recompute, change the background, and export the values. Every colour is computed by the library's own colour functions (foambryo.colour_scales), the ones the napari plugin uses too:

  • tensions: coolwarm, light grey at the mean tension (1 by default), blue below, red above, over a range centred on the mean;
  • pressures: magma, light for low pressures, trimmed to its 10-90 % range so that no cell is drawn black or white;
  • an undetermined value (nan) is green, and an undetermined tension's interface is drawn as its outline; crop faces are see-through glass with their edges.

This example generates a foam of Voronoi cells imaged with voxels of 1.0 x 0.5 x 0.5 um (not at mechanical equilibrium: the colours show the viewer, not the method's accuracy), and

  1. writes the colour bars without any window (save_colour_bars: matplotlib only);
  2. writes the viewer's first view of the tensions and pressures as a figure (plot_force_inference(..., save_figure=..., show=False)), then of the tensions exploded, then of tensions averaged over four reconstructions with their seed spread (plot_tension_inference(..., seed_ensemble=...)). Saving a figure needs Polyscope and a display; the window closes once the figure is written;
  3. with --show, opens the same views as windows to explore (close each window to go on);

  4. with --from-mask, opens the window on the mask itself (view_mask): the panel reconstructs it and infers, in separate processes, with their elapsed time, an estimate and Cancel. This is what foambryo view MASK --spacing DZ DY DX opens.

    pip install "foambryo[viewing]" python polyscope_viewer.py # writes ./polyscope-viewer-output/ python polyscope_viewer.py --show # and opens the windows python polyscope_viewer.py --from-mask # the window that starts from the mask

The script: Examples/polyscope_viewer.py. It needs only foambryo and foambryo[viewing]; it generates its own tissue.

The figure plot_tension_inference(..., scattered=True, save_figure=...) writes: the generated foam's tensions, exploded, with the colour bar and the length scale bar.
